This full-time Consultant in General Adult Psychiatry post is based within the North Hampshire Community Mental Health Team (CMHT) in Basingstoke. The role provides senior clinical leadership across a multidisciplinary team aligned to a Primary Care Network, delivering high-quality assessment and treatment for adults with complex mental health needs. The consultant manages a small caseload of the most complex patients, offers advice and guidance to the wider team, and contributes to service development within a transforming community mental health model. Responsibilities include clinical supervision, Mental Health Act work as an Approved Clinician, participation in governance, teaching, and supporting trainees. The post includes 10 PAs (7.5 DCC, 2.5 SPA) with opportunities for flexible working, research involvement, and leadership roles. The consultant also joins a 1:9 senior on call rota. The Trust offers strong CPD support, mentoring, and a collaborative working culture grounded in CARE values.

The post holder will work within the North Hampshire and Basingstoke CMHT, which is divided into two teams, each aligned with three Primary Care Networks (PCNs). Each team is led by a Band 8a Service Manager and a Band 7 Team Leader, supported by a full multidisciplinary team and a well-resourced psychological therapies service.

The Consultant will be primarily aligned with one PCN, attending monthly PCN MDT meetings and working closely with local GP practices. The role includes providing clinical input and guidance to the PCN MDT and supporting the wider CMHT MDT.

The post holder will conduct scheduled and urgent clinical assessments and reviews, flexibly responding to service need and providing cross-cover for Consultant colleagues during leave. The CMHT works closely with co-located services, including Early Intervention in Psychosis (EIP) and a newly commissioned personality disorder service offering DBT.

There are strong links with local services including GPs, CAMHS, Substance Misuse, OPMH, and Learning Disability teams. Junior medical staff, including GP, core, and higher trainees, as well as medical students from Southampton and St George's, are attached to the team, contributing to a strong teaching culture.

Crisis and urgent assessments are managed by the Crisis and Home Treatment Team (CRHT), ensuring that the CMHT focuses on routine and "soon" referrals

title: Salaried Frailty General Practitioner
descriptionHtml:
This is a new role funded by the Launceston and Tamar Valley Integrated Neighbourhood Team (INT). The post holder will be employed by Launceston Medical Centre while working with the wider neighbourhood to develop and implement a frailty model of care, incorporating a proactive care test and learn project and improving coordination across the INT.

The role combines clinical frailty work with service development, collaboration and clinical leadership. As the project develops, the balance of duties may vary to reflect the stage of implementation and learning.

The Frailty Test and Learn is an 18-month project aiming to improve care for people living with frailty. It will focus on early identification, proactive support and better coordination across services, with the intention of improving outcomes for people while reducing avoidable use of acute hospital care.

The project will primarily focus on people aged 65 and over living with moderate to severe frailty.

The two principal goals of the test and learn are to -

Reduce non-elective admissions to acute hospitals for the identified cohort.

Reduce length of stay and bed days within acute settings for the identified cohort through a system-wide, co-designed pull model supporting earlier discharge.

The post holder will be part of the Launceston and Tamar Valley INT frailty team and will contribute actively to the co-design, implementation and evaluation of this project.

As the role sits within a developing neighbourhood frailty model, responsibilities will evolve with the project. Expected responsibilities include -

Spend time with organisations and professionals within the INT frailty team to understand their roles, capacity, pathways and workload.

Build effective working relationships across organisations and help identify and reduce barriers to collaboration.

Work with the INT to improve coordination of frailty care across the neighbourhood and reduce duplication between services.

Collaborate with system partners in the development of the pull model intended to support earlier and safer discharge from acute care.

Take an active role in overseeing implementation of the Frailty Test and Learn within Launceston Medical Centre, working closely with the social prescribing team, Health Hub, managers and other relevant staff.

Contribute to the evaluation of the project, including clinical governance, quality improvement, learning, service outcomes and changes required as the model develops.

Launceston Medical Centre is a large dispensing practice providing care to around 19,000 patients in and around Devon and Cornwall.

We enjoy working from modern, purpose-built premises. The partners and staff have a shared belief in the delivery of high quality, traditional and personal family healthcare. Our patients enjoy good access to care, and we have a strong ethos to recognise their needs when driving forward patient services. It is important to the partners to treat our staff well. We are proud to be a teaching Practice. To promote a multi-disciplinary team approach, we share our premises with other providers including mental health services and social prescribers.

title: Clinical and Strategic Lead for Nursing and Advanced Clinical Practice
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for an experienced and motivated Advanced Nurse Practitioner to join Sid Valley Practice as our new Clinical and Strategic Lead for Nursing and Advanced Clinical Practice.

It offers a unique opportunity to shape the future direction of nursing services and advanced clinical practice within a progressive, patient-focused and highly regarded practice.

We are looking for someone who wants to do more than manage day-to-day operations. We are seeking a strategic, innovative and forward-thinking clinical leader who can support, develop and inspire our nursing and advanced clinical practice workforce whilst identifying opportunities to improve services, patient pathways and ways of working.

As Clinical and Strategic Lead for Nursing and Advanced Clinical Practice, you will provide professional, clinical, strategic and operational leadership across our nursing services and advanced clinical practice, supporting the integration of urgent and planned care to improve patient outcomes, continuity of care and workforce flexibility.

You will work closely with GP Partners, the Practice Manager and GP Clinical Lead to:

  • Ensure high standards of clinical governance and patient safety, including CQC and QOF
  • Develop services that meet the needs of our growing and evolving patient population.
  • Identify and implement best practice from across primary care and the wider NHS.
  • Maintain your own advanced clinical practice skills through autonomous assessment, diagnosis and treatment of patients.

This role offers genuine opportunity to influence the future direction of nursing and advanced clinical services and make a lasting impact on patient care.

You'll be joining an experienced, supportive and highly skilled nursing and advanced clinical practice workforce.

Our team includes:

  • Experienced Practice Nurses, the majority of whom are independent prescribers.
  • Three experienced Advanced Nurse Practitioners.
  • Two experienced Paramedics.

Sid Valley Practice is a forward-thinking training practice serving approximately 15,000 patients across two sites in Sidmouth on Devon's beautiful Jurassic Coast.

employer: Gloucestershire Health and Care NHS Foundation Trust
title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
Gloucestershire Health and Care NHS Foundation Trust are looking for experienced GPs to join the Integrated Urgent Care Service (IUCS).

The overall aim of the Integrated Urgent Care Service is to provide a consult and complete model of care for people needing urgent care. The key features of the service include NHS 111, Clinical Assessment Service and Out of Hours services (face-to-face base and home visiting). The NHS 111 service will be provided by Health Advisors and Clinical Advisorshosted by our partner organisation, IC24. Where a senior clinical review is indicated, this will be completed within the Clinical Assessment Service, which will be jointly delivered by GHC Senior Clinical Leads based at Edward Jenner Court, Gloucester and remotely by IC24 CASclinicians. The post holder will act as the Senior Clinical Lead for CAS and be part of the rota covering the service 24/7.

This role is offered on a permanent basis. We currently have a range of hours and shifts available during the week and at weekends, between 08:00-00:00. These can be offered as a fixed pattern.

Please note that enhancements are offered, please see attached, for out of hours working and any CAS Senior Lead hours attract 3% if salaried before the enhancements are then added. For any bank hours you will see the different rates attached for the two types of roles.

The qualification, training & experience requirements for the role are underlined in the Job Description/Person Specification.

The postholder will work collaboratively with the service team and have oversight of all clinical queues across the IUCS pathway to direct patients without delay to the correct parts of the urgent care system utilising the Gloucestershire Directory of Service.

The Senior Clinical Lead will provide support and guidance to all colleagues across the service ensuring everyone is confident and supported to work to the top of their license.

As a GP working within the service they will use their clinical expertise and professional knowledge to assess and manage patients as part of clinical telephone triage, working as part of a multi-disciplinary team to deliver high quality and patient centred service when in hours General Practice is closed.

Where required and available, the CAS will haveaccess to direct booking into the Out of Hours bases and Home visiting service and work closely with other community services within GHC such as Minor Injury and Illness Units, Rapid Response and Evening and Overnight District Nursing. The CAS will provide an enhanced assessment supported by the NHS Pathways Clinical Consultation Support (PaCCS) module to identify clinical need/risk. It will also oversee and take actions relating to any abnormal urgent pathology results communicated by Gloucestershire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (GHFT) Pathology Service during the OOH period.

We have a skilled and dedicated workforce of over 5000 colleagues working in a diverse range of services over 55 sites and within people's homes. We strive to enable a welcoming workplace culture that builds and celebrates civility, inclusivity and diversity, while providing a sense of belonging and trust.

Annual staff surveys, regular Pulse surveys and other engagement opportunities provide our people with lots of opportunity to tell us about their experiences of working with us. In the latest staff survey, 61% of colleagues gave us their views. It was great to hear that:

  • 72% of colleagues would recommend the Trust as a place to work, ranking us 1st for Provider Trusts in the South West region on this question.
  • 76% would recommend the standard of care provided in our services if a friend or relative needed treatment, also ranking us 1st in the South West region.
  • 81% said that care of patients and service users is the Trust's priority, compared with an average in comparable NHS Trusts in England of 64%.

This high-level overview shows we are in a healthy position, with higher scores than average for comparable organisations, alongside a great response rate, indicating good staff engagement. However, we also know we have plenty of room for improvement in many areas. To that end, we continue to prioritise and invest in our commitment to genuinely becoming a Great Place to Work with consistent top-quartile performance in the annual staff survey and Pulse surveys.

title: Consultant in Rehabilitation Medicine: Community Neuro-Rehabilitation
descriptionHtml:
Join an innovative rehabilitation service in one of the UK's most beautiful coastal locations

Livewell Southwest is seeking an enthusiastic and forward thinking Consultant in Rehabilitation Medicine to join our expanding Rehabilitation Medicine team in Plymouth.

This substantive consultant post is primarily focused on leading and developing our community neuro-rehabilitation service, working within a highly skilled multidisciplinary team delivering specialist rehabilitation to people with neurological conditions across Plymouth and surrounding area. An Innovative Rotational Consultant Opportunity

For candidates seeking a broader rehabilitation medicine experience, this post can also form part of our new and innovative rotational consultant programme.

The rotational model offers substantive employment whilst providing the opportunity to rotate annually across three specialist rehab services:

  • Community Neuro-Rehab
  • Inpatient Neurological Rehab (Level 2a Specialist Rehabilitation Unit)
  • Stroke Rehab Medicine

Consultants participating in the programme will rotate between these services on a 12-month basis, allowing them to broaden their clinical expertise, develop specialist interests and work alongside a range of multidisciplinary teams across the rehab pathway. This unique model has been designed to support professional development whilst strengthening integrated rehabilitation services across Plymouth.

Candidates may apply either:

  • For the substantive Community Neuro-Rehabilitation Consultant role; or
  • To join the rotational consultant programme incorporating all three rehabilitation medicine services. Lead and shape a developing Community Neuro-Rehabilitation service.

Why choose to work with us

  • Work alongside experienced rehabilitation medicine consultants and specialist multidisciplinary teams
  • Participate in specialist services including spasticity management, intrathecal baclofen and spinal rehab
  • Opportunities for undergraduate teaching and research collaboration with the University of Plymouth
  • Strong commitment to consultant development, CPD and service innovation
  • Live and work in Plymouth, surrounded by the stunning coastlines of Devon and Cornwall

Find out more

Teresa Barrett, Medical Workforce Manager on Livewell.Medical-Workforce@nhs.net

Livewell Southwest is an independent, award-winning social enterprise delivering integrated health and social care services across Plymouth, South Hams, and West Devon, with specialist services in parts of Devon and Cornwall. title: Six Month Fixed Term Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
Primary Care Networks (PCNs) form a key building block of the NHS long-term plan. Bringing general practices together to work at scale has been a policy priority for some years for a range of reasons, including improving the ability of practices to recruit and retain staff; to manage financial and estates pressures; to provide a wider range of services to patients and to more easily integrate with the wider health and care system

Following the release of ARRS GP funding we are looking for a GP, to join Chester Central Primary Care Network on a six month fixed term salaried contact. We will consider applications for a minimum of four sessions with a start date of January 2027, but are prepared to wait for the right candidate .

As a reflection of the lower sessional rate the post holder will not be required to complete home visits or duty doctor (on call) duties.

Our clinical system for all practices is EMIS Web and we have a structured administrative team to help with letters, results, medication management, etc.

Working as part of our multidisciplinary team, you will have the opportunity to support and care for a diverse patient group

We reserve the right to close the application early, so would encourage early application

  • Working across a maximum of three of the six practices you will undertake a variety of duties including face to face and telephone consultations and queries, with no home visits.
  • Making professional, autonomous decisions in relation to presenting medical problems, whether self-referred or referred from other healthcare workers within the organisation.
  • Assessing the healthcare needs of patients with undifferentiated and undiagnosed problems;
  • Screening patients for disease risk factors and early signs of illness;
  • Developing care plans for health in consultation with patients and in line with practice disease management protocols;
  • Recording clear consultation notes to agreed standards;
  • Collecting data for audit purposes and complying with QOF requirements;
  • Compiling and issuing computer-generated acute and repeat prescriptions;
  • All general duties and responsibilities associated with a GP working within primary care.

Chester Central PCN is a well established PCN, delivering excellent care to over 41,000 patients across the city of Chester. We have six practices, four of which are in one building, The Elms Medical Practice, Fountains Medical Practice, Northgate Medical Centre and Northgate Village Surgery, with Garden Lane Medical Centre and St. Werburghs practice for the homeless within a short walking distance.

We have a number of excellent additional roles (ARRS) within our PCN including social prescriber link workers, clinical pharmacists, pharmacy technicians, paramedics, dieticians, and physiotherapists which offer additional patient services and allow the Doctors to focus on patient care and signpost to the most relevant colleague or team.

We have two clinical directors who work closely together and a PCN Manager, who manages the day to day needs of the PCN and together offer a strong leadership team.

The practices within the PCN have all secured a rating of GOOD by the Care Quality Commission (CQC). The PCN is an established limited company having moved to this model in 2023.

We offer:

  • NHS pension scheme.
  • Full compliance with the BMA contract
  • Excellent training opportunities and progression provided

As an accredited GP Training Practice, we are passionate about developing the next generation of healthcare professionals. We provide training placements for GP Registrars creating an environment that encourages learning, mentorship, and professional development.

We work collaboratively with neighbouring practices through our Primary Care Network and the Warrington Innovation Network (WIN), sharing expertise, driving service innovation, and working together to improve health outcomes for our local community.

At Springfields Medical Centre, we believe that looking after our staff is fundamental to delivering outstanding patient care. We foster a positive and inclusive workplace where wellbeing, professional growth, and continuous improvement are actively encouraged, making our practice an excellent place to build a rewarding career.

title: Fixed Term Consultant in Acute Medicine
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for the post of a Fixed Term Acute Medical Consultant within an expanded assessment area medical team. This new model will involve working across existing assessment areas, including support of same day emergency care which has been facilitated with a brand new £2.4 million unit.

PREVIOUS APPLICANTS NEED NOT APPLY

This opportunity will involve working as part of a team responsible for assessing patients in an urgent care setting and providing support with senior decision making early in the patient journey.

This new model has been facilitated by a further £2.6 million investment to support workforce across assessment care which now includes Same Day Emergency Care, two Assessment wards, and a Clinical Decisions Unit.

The Acute Medical / Surgical teams have developed robust clinical pathways which will underpin patient assessment and Same Day Emergency Care at Bolton. All patients attending the Emergency Department will be assessed utilising the pathways and exclusion criteria to ensure patients are managed effectively and efficiently.

This is an exciting new venture for Bolton NHS Foundation Trust and we are now looking to build a substantial team that share our vision and drive the service forward. You will work alongside a friendly, supportive, and professional integrated team comprising of Consultants, Nurses, Occupational Therapists, Physiotherapist, Coordinators, Advanced Clinical Practitioners, Pharmacists, Social Services and Community Services to provide a safe, effective and efficient care environment for patients, relatives and carers.

title: General Practitioner
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking a dedicated and compassionate General Practitioner (GP) to join our GP practice and provide high-quality, patient-centred medical care. The successful candidate will assess, diagnose and manage a wide range of acute and chronic health conditions, while supporting patients with preventative healthcare and ongoing wellbeing.

Working as part of a multidisciplinary team, the GP will contribute to the effective day-to-day running of the practice and work collaboratively with clinical and administrative colleagues to ensure patients receive safe, effective and accessible care.

  • Conduct face-to-face and remote consultations, assessing patients and developing appropriate management plans.
  • Diagnose and treat a broad range of acute and chronic medical conditions.
  • Provide ongoing management and monitoring of patients with long-term conditions.
  • Prescribe medications safely and appropriately in accordance with current guidance.
  • Make appropriate referrals to secondary care and other healthcare professionals where required.
  • Provide preventative healthcare, including health promotion, screening and lifestyle advice.
  • Maintain accurate, timely and confidential patient records.
  • Respond appropriately to urgent and complex clinical presentations.
  • Work collaboratively with nurses, healthcare assistants, pharmacists, administrative staff and other members of the wider healthcare team.
  • Participate in clinical meetings, significant event reviews, audits and practice development activities.
  • Maintain professional knowledge and skills through continuing professional development (CPD).
  • Follow practice policies, clinical guidelines, safeguarding requirements and relevant NHS standards.
  • Contribute to quality improvement and the ongoing development of services within the practice.

    • We are a friendly, patient-focused GP practice committed to providing high-quality, safe and accessible healthcare to our local community. Our aim is to deliver personalised care that meets the individual needs of our patients while promoting health, wellbeing and preventative care.

    Our practice is supported by a multidisciplinary team of GPs, nurses, healthcare professionals and administrative staff who work collaboratively to provide a comprehensive range of primary care services. We value teamwork, open communication and a supportive working environment where all members of staff are encouraged to contribute to the continued development of the practice.

    We are committed to delivering care in line with current clinical guidance and NHS standards, while continually looking for opportunities to improve our services and patient experience.

    We value our staff and recognise the important contribution each team member makes to the practice. We encourage professional development, learning and innovation, and strive to create a positive working environment where staff feel supported, respected and valued.

    As a practice, we are proud to serve our local community and remain committed to providing compassionate, inclusive and high-quality primary care to our patients.

title: Salaried GP  4-6 Sessions | Supportive Practice | Slough
descriptionHtml:
Bharani Medical Centre is seeking a confident and enthusiastic Salaried GP to join our established and supportive clinical team in Slough.

We care for approximately 18,000 patients across three nearby sites and offer a structured working environment supported by experienced GP partners and a comprehensive multidisciplinary team.

Our digital-first working model is designed to provide clinicians with a predictable and manageable workload while maintaining high standards of patient care.

We offer approximately 15 consultations per clinical session, dedicated administrative time, no traditional duty doctor rota and infrequent home visits. Working days can be agreed in advance, with 46 sessions available.

We are particularly interested in clinically confident GPs who can work independently and manage a broad range of presentations. Previous experience working in general practice following qualification would be advantageous.

Informal discussions via Microsoft Teams are warmly encouraged.

The successful candidate will provide comprehensive general medical services to registered patients, working independently while contributing to our multidisciplinary team.

Main responsibilities include:

  • Undertaking approximately 15 patient consultations per clinical session, predominantly telephone-first, with face-to-face assessments when clinically appropriate.
  • Assessing and managing acute presentations, chronic conditions and complex clinical problems.
  • Prescribing safely, requesting investigations, reviewing results and arranging appropriate referrals.
  • Managing clinical correspondence and associated tasks through Anima Documents, with dedicated administrative slots.
  • Managing occasional additional urgent appointments, including childhood emergencies, according to clinical need.
  • Undertaking home visits where appropriate, although these are infrequent.
  • Maintaining accurate clinical records using EMIS Web, Anima and Accurx.
  • Participating in clinical governance, quality improvement, safeguarding and continuing professional development.

Bharani Medical Centre is a well-established, GP-led practice providing NHS primary care to approximately 18,000 patients across three nearby sites in Slough.

Our experienced multidisciplinary team includes GP partners, salaried GPs, advanced nurse practitioners, clinical pharmacists, first-contact physiotherapists, practice nurses and administrative colleagues.

We pride ourselves on providing high-quality, patient-centred care within a friendly, supportive and collaborative working environment.

We have invested in digital systems, including EMIS Web, Anima and Accurx, to improve clinical efficiency, streamline administrative workflows and support sustainable working arrangements.

We recognise the importance of clinical independence, professional development and a healthy work-life balance. Our working arrangements are informed by BMA salaried GP guidance and recognised contractual standards.

We encourage open communication, shared learning and clinical innovation, while ensuring colleagues feel supported and valued.

We welcome clinicians who are confident, motivated and enthusiastic about contributing to a progressive general practice team.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for an enthusiastic and dedicated GP to join our team at Rush Hill & Weston surgery. Whether you are aSalaried GP ready to take the next step in your career or anewly qualified GP seeking your first role in primary care, we would like to hear from you.

The Role

  • 6-session salaried GP post
  • Friday working required

  • Work within an experienced multidisciplinary team

  • About You

About Us

Rush Hill & Weston Surgery is a well-established, patient-focused practice serving the city of Bath. We have 2 sites; Weston surgery is opposite the RUH and Rush Hill Surgery is on the opposite side of Bath. We are a GP Training Practice with a strong multidisciplinary team including GPs, nurses, pharmacists, healthcare assistants, care coordinators, home visiting team and social prescribers. We pride ourselves on delivering high-quality patient care while supporting staff wellbeing, learning and development. We understand that life outside of work matters and aim to create a working environment where our GPs can thrive both professionally and personally.

title: Consultant Psychiatrist - Assertive Outreach Team Oxford
descriptionHtml:
Are you ready to take the next step on your career and be our leading Consultant Psychiatrist for the newly established Assertive Outreach Team?

This is a full time position based in Oxford where you will lead on delivering a specialised services to vulnerable adults with severe and enduring mental disorders following NHSE guidance to enhance intensive and assertive community mental health care.

Working alongside a newly formed team you'll be delivering a service to meet the needs of around 90 patients across Oxford city who have severe and complex psychosis, multiple comorbidities, high rates of hospital admission, present with significant risks and find it hard to engage with mental health services. Assertive engagement, evidence-based bio psycho social treatment plans, collating and sharing information with system partners, carers and families, risk formulation and safety planning will be at the heart of the service's therapeutic approach.

This is a unique opportunity to build a service that will make a lasting impact to mental health care and patient recovery outcomes. We're looking for applicants who have full GMC registration and are on the Specialist Register or within six months of CCT. You'll need to be eligible for Section 12 Approval/Approved Clinician status or willing to apply for this once in post.

If you're a ready for a challenge and want to work for one of the UK's leading mental health Trusts, we would be delighted to receive your application.

  • Provide clinical leadership and medical input to the team in delivering responsive, effective and inclusive mental health community services to the designated catchment area.
  • Provision of evidence-based bio-psychosocial interventions to promote recovery and social inclusion, including integrative working with external agencies to ensure community engagement.
  • Responsibility for those patients seen by himself/herself, together with those patients seen by medical staff directly supervised by them.
  • Provide expert assessments informed by evidence for referred individuals with severe and enduring mental health difficulties and complex needs.
  • Have responsibility for the clinical governance of the team as one of the clinical leads for the team.
  • Actively liaise with other mental health teams to ensure continuity of care and appropriate information sharing.
  • Provide RC responsibility for outpatients under the provisions of the MHA.
  • Communicate and liaise with patients, families, relatives, carers and any other agencies as appropriate.
  • Play an active role in training for team members as well as in the programme and wider Trust, including teaching medical students, Resident doctors and members of the MDT.

Oxford Health is a great place to work and to be able to showcase the best of yourself when making an application please read the "candidate guide to making an application" and ensure your supporting statement is tailored to the role you are applying for and addresses any essential criteria.

As a Trust we provide physical, mental health and social care for people of all ages across Oxfordshire, Buckinghamshire, Swindon, Wiltshire, Bath and Northeast Somerset. Our services are delivered at community bases, hospitals, clinics and people's homes, delivering care as close to home as possible. Our vision is that no matter who you are or where you are, you will tell us that you receive: "Outstanding care delivered by an outstanding team"

Our values are: "Caring, safe and excellent"

We offer a wide range of benefits designed to support your career and wellbeing. These include:

o Excellent opportunities for career progressiono Access to tailored individual and Trust wide learning and developmento 33 days annual leave, plus bank holidays, rising to 35 days with continuous serviceo NHS Discount across a wide range of shops, restaurants and retailerso Competitive pension schemeo Lease car schemeo Cycle to work schemeo Employee Assistance Programmeo Mental Health First Aiderso Staff accommodation (please note waiting lists apply)o Staff networking and support groups hosted by our Equality, Diversity & Inclusion team

employer: University Hospitals of Leicester NHS Trust
title: Consultant in Clinical Oncology
descriptionHtml:
This is an exciting opportunity to join the Oncology Department at the University Hospitals of Leicester as a Consultant Clinical Oncologist with an interest in Urology and AOS.

This post will support, with other Consultant colleagues in the Centre, the provision of Oncological Services across the local network. Tumour site specialisation has been fully developed and the post holder will be expected to offer expertise in the management of Urology Tumours and working within an Acute Oncology services setting.   1. undertake clinical and managerial responsibility for the agreed oncology specialties and patients.

employer: The Hillingdon Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in O&G
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for a substantive Obstetrics and Gynaecology consultant post, joining the Obstetrics and Gynaecology Consultant team at Hillingdon Hospital. The post is a 10 PA plus 0.47 APA consultant post in obstetrics and gynaecology. The ideal candidate will have a high standard of general obstetrics and gynaecology skills. The timetable allows the postholder to maintain a breadth of skills across the specialty, with the intention of development of the job plan in line with special interests. The post holder will participate in the consultant on-call rota for obstetrics and gynaecology which includes 1 in 10 weekends on call with prospective cover (approximately 5 weekends per year). This is a non-resident on-call rota. The obstetrics and gynaecology consultant body at Hillingdon Hospital are known for working cohesively and supporting each other, both in clinical settings and with regards to professional development. The department maintains a reputation for being extremely sociable and a pleasant place to work. We also work hard at maintaining our popularity with junior doctors, resulting in a very high standard of middle grade staff. We are primarily looking for an individual who will work well with our team. Any interested candidates are strongly encouraged to visit the department.

Regular departmental meetings for education, audit and administration occur. There is teaching for the junior doctors within the department at lunchtimes through the week.

Please see attached Job Description and Person Specification for a full list of role requirements and responsibilities.

Hillingdon Hospital is the only acute hospital in the London Borough of Hillingdon and offers a wide range of services including accident and emergency, inpatient care, day surgery, outpatient clinics and maternity services.

Our services are provided from both Hillingdon Hospital and Mount Vernon Hospital. The Trust has a turnover of around £222 million and we employ over 3,300 staff. We deliver high quality healthcare to the residents of the London Borough of Hillingdon, and increasingly to those living in the surrounding areas of Ealing, Harrow, Buckinghamshire and Hertfordshire, giving us a total catchment population of over350,000 people.

The Trust's services at Mount Vernon Hospital include routine day surgery at a modern treatment centre, a minor injuries unit, and outpatient clinics.The Hillingdon Hospital is currently being reviewed for a completely new build on site to accommodate new technology and improve both patient and staff experience.

title: Theatre Practitioner - Major Ortho Scrub (Bank)
descriptionHtml:
Theatre Practitioner - Major Ortho Scrub (Bank)

Exeter Hospital | Nursing | Bank | Ad Hoc |

Up to £26.50 per hour depending on experience

Nuffield Health is the UK's largest Healthcare Charity. From our innovative healthcare and leisure facilities to our community access programmes, we're committed to building a healthier nation. Inside our award-winning hospitals, this starts with commitment to quality and the highest standards of patient care. It starts with you. As a Theatre Practitioner Major Ortho Scrub, you will: 

Work with leading consultants and like-minded professionals
Enjoy a varied caseload with state-of-the-art technology, equipment and facilities
Supervise, support and develop junior members of staff
Create high-quality care and patient experiences that are clinically effective and evidence based
Interact well with colleagues on the ward, understanding that continuity in patient care is key
Deliver high-quality care to patients in the anaesthetic and recovery phases of surgery
Collaborate with anaesthetists and surgical teams to prepare and monitor patients pre, during, and post-surgery
Have ample opportunities for continuous growth and personal developmentNuffield Health Exeter Hospital

The Exeter Nuffield hospital is based next to the RD&E hospital in Wonford, Exeter. The hospital has 2 theatres, as well as a hybrid cardiac catheter laboratory/theatre and an Endoscopy suite. There are two ward areas: an inpatient area with 21 beds and a day-case ward with 12 beds. We also have a busy outpatient department, pharmacy, physiotherapy, and radiology department including an MRI scanner. We specialise in elective orthopaedic and spinal surgery, cardiology including invasive procedures, general surgery, plastics and cosmetic surgery, ENT, and gynaecology. The Hospital has a MAKO robot that undertakes some of the joint replacement surgery which we have become well known for in this field of surgery.

title: Consultant Psychiatrist - General Adult - CMHT
descriptionHtml:
Pennine Care NHS Foundation Trust is looking to recruit a full-time substantive Consultant Psychiatrist. This post is based on the CMHT in Bury and is a Community post.

title: Health Care Assistant
descriptionHtml:
The Healthcare Assistant (HCA) will support the clinical team in delivering high-quality, patient-centred care to the practice population of approximately 7,300 patients. Working as part of the multidisciplinary team, the post holder will undertake a range of clinical duties including venepuncture, NHS Health Checks, new patient health checks, recording observations, ECGs and health promotion activities.

The successful candidate will have experience working within a Primary Care or General Practice setting and will demonstrate a professional, compassionate and proactive approach to patient care. They will contribute to the smooth running of clinical services while supporting patients to improve and maintain their health and wellbeing.

  • Undertake NHS Health Checks and new patient health checks.

  • Provide health promotion and healthy lifestyle advice.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
East Hill Surgery is looking for a salaried GP to join their busy practice, covering 6 sessions per week.

Working as part of our multidisciplinary team, you will have the opportunity to support and care for a diverse patient group.The role will include all general duties and responsibilities associated with a GP working within primary care.

  • Undertaking a variety of duties including surgery consultations, telephone consultations and queries, checking and signing repeat prescriptions and dealing with queries, paperwork, reports and correspondence in a timely fashion;

employer: The Dudley Group NHS Foundation Trust

title: Locum Consultant Psychiatrist - Inpatient P.I.C.U.  (Ward 1)
descriptionHtml:
Locum Consultant Psychiatrist - Adult Inpatient Services

Full Time 10PAs

Fixed Term Contract - 8 months

The Trust is seeking to appoint an experienced Consultant Psychiatrist to work in our Psychiatric Intensive Care Unit (P.I.C.U.) on Ward 1 to cover the maternity leave of the current post holder for a period of approximately 8 months. This post is based at Springfield Hospital, in Tooting, London SW17.

This is an exciting opportunity for an energetic and dynamic consultant psychiatrist to join this friendly ward team.

We are a progressive, financially stable mental health trust which has been rated 'good' by the CQC both overall and specifically for our acute & urgent care services.

The Acute & Urgent Care Service Line comprises Acute General Psychiatric Wards on two hospital sites, intensive care unit, a psychiatric decision unit, acute care co-ordination and advanced clinical practice teams, home treatment and street triage teams, perinatal psychiatry, liaison psychiatric teams at three general hospitals, and two recovery cafs. All our clinicians are able to participate in a Trustwide quality improvement programme.

We are investing in further improvements to our mental health services, including a major redevelopment programme on both the Springfield and Tolworth sites.

The post-holder will provide medical leadership on Ward 1. The Consultant will work closely with the Ward Manager to ensure a safe, efficient and effective service that meets the Trust's Key Performance Indicators.

While individual clinicians within the team have responsibility for the clinical care they deliver, the consultant shares with the ward manager and other team members responsibility for ensuring the care delivered by the team is safe and of a good standard. This includes participating in systems of audit and clinical governance, working to resolve problems on their own initiative, and where necessary drawing any concerns they have been unable to resolve themselves to the attention of the ward manager and others.

South West London and St George's Mental Health NHS Trust has a rich history, well-established community links and an international reputation. We provide a full range of local mental health services to the Kingston, Merton, Richmond, Sutton and Wandsworth London boroughs, as well as specialist forensic mental health services, including specialised services such as national deaf adults and CAMHS inpatients and OCD.

We are committed to providing high quality integrated health and social care for local people with mental health problems in South West London and more specialist mental health services for people throughout the UK. The Care Quality Commission already rates our services as 'good' however we aim to be 'outstanding'.

We are Proud to Belong at South West London and St George's Mental Health NHS Trust.

We have expert services, a rich history and a clear commitment to providing the best quality care for those with mental ill-health. The Care Quality Commission already rates our services as 'good' - we aspire to be 'outstanding'.

This is a great time to join us. We are transforming the way we care for our communities to support our mission of Making Life Better Together. We have built two brand new mental health facilities at Springfield University Hospital, which are amongst the best in the world. More developments are planned across our sites and services.

Clinical Responsibilities

This is an exciting opportunity to join a multidisciplinary CAMHS team, providing specialist assessment, diagnosis, management and treatment for children, young people & families experiencing severe & complex mental health difficulties.

Clinical Activity

You will undertake psychiatric assessments, provide clinical reviews & contribute to effective treatment planning. The role includes offering specialist consultation and advice to colleagues and partner agencies, working closely with education, social care, primary care & other services to support positive outcomes for young people.

You will provide expert psychiatric input across a varied caseload, including medication management, mental state monitoring, formulation and joint working with care coordinators and multidisciplinary colleagues. There will also be involvement in urgent clinical work where required.

Leadership and Service Development

As a senior clinician, you will provide clinical leadership within the multidisciplinary team, supporting high standards of care and contributing to service development and quality improvement. Working alongside senior clinical and operational colleagues, you will help shape responsive, evidence-based services for the local population.

Special Interests

The post offers opportunities to develop specialist clinical interests aligned with service priorities and local needs, supporting both professional development and the ongoing enhancement of CAMHS provision.

title: MOD General Practitioner
descriptionHtml:
At Defence Primary Healthcare we are an inclusive, dedicated organisation working to provide outstanding care to our entitled personnel.

Are you a GP looking for a role where you can make a real difference, work alongside the military, and rediscover the satisfaction that first drew you to medicine?

We are seeking a professional, patient-focused GP to join the friendly Reserves Medical team at Baden Powell House, Catterick Garrison.

This is an opportunity to practise medicine in a way that allows you to do a thorough, meaningful job. You will spend time with members of the Reserve Forces, exploring their health, fitness and occupational requirements, helping them return to work, remain deployable, or prepare for military service.

The focus is on the application of core GP skills within an occupational setting, without the need for specialist occupational health qualifications to start the role.

This part time role offers 27 hours per week and all requests to work flexibly will be considered, allowing for business needs, and reviewed annually. The salary will be pro-rata.

Benefits:

  • An inclusive working environment with options to enable flexible working
  • Learning and development tailored to your role with a high standard of in-house training being offered
  • A Civil Service pension with an average employer contribution of 27%
  • Excellent sick pay provision Maximum 5 months on full pay and 5 months on half pay. Eligibility criteria will apply in accordance with a current MOD policy
  • Parking

The postholder will provide occupational healthcare to members of the Reserve forces in line with General Medical Council standards and relevant Defence policy to meet Commander Defence HealthCare Recovery Groups (Comd DHRG) objectives for best patient care.

As agreed by Comd DHRG, the postholder may be required to support Primary Medical Care services for Defence Primary Healthcare (DPHC) in the UK at regional level to enhance and sustain operational effectiveness.

The role plays an important part in force protection and military readiness, helping to ensure that the Armed Forces have personnel who are medically fit, employable and prepared for the demands placed upon them.

For many GPs, one of the greatest frustrations of modern practice is the feeling that there is never enough time to do the job properly. Endless demand, administrative burden and time pressure can make even a successful day feel incomplete. This role offers something different. The 27-hour working week genuinely feels like 27 hours. Clinical time is protected, administrative expectations are realistic, and you will work within a well-supported multidisciplinary team with excellent peer support and training.

The pace allows you to engage properly with your patients, consider complex issues carefully, and reach well-reasoned decisions. There is time for discussion, learning, and professional development. At the end of the day, you can leave knowing that your work has been completed to a high standard.

Our success depends on our people, our Whole Force, regular and reservist military, civil servants and contractors, all working as one, working together seamlessly to deliver for us.

Our civil servants are a central part of this Whole Force, developing strategy, making policy, supporting ministerial decision-making and Parliamentary processes. In fact, with over 2,000 different roles working across 650 sites around the world, now really is an excellent time to join one of the largest, most exciting departments in government.

The Ministry of Defence is committed to attracting and retaining people from across the full range of backgrounds and enabling flexible ways of working as the norm. We offer maternity, adoption or shared parental leave of up to 26 weeks full pay followed by 13 weeks of statutory pay and a further 13 weeks unpaid, and paternity leave of 2 weeks full pay.

In return, you can expect a department that helps you learn and develop that recognises your expertise and contribution, both as an individual and part of a team.

If you've ever wanted to do more, see more, go further or be better, we have roles in more professions and vocations than ever before. Let's see where your future will take you, together.

title: SevernSide IUC GP
descriptionHtml:
As a SevernSide GP your role will involve, managing a wide range of clinical presentations in urgent care settings, supporting patients via telephone, video, or face-to-face consultations, prescribing effectively, including adjustments to end-of-life care, maintaining thorough documentation for continuity of care, as well as mentoring new clinicians and contributing to peak-demand rotas.

Our IUC service, offers Clinicians a choice of diverse shift types to match their skills and interest.

Face-to-face appointments at one of our Treatment Centres

Mobile home visiting service

Telephone triage

As a ServernSide GP you will:

  • Assess and manage the full breadth of clinical presentations and age groups which present in the urgent primary care setting, including physical and mental health needs
  • Take telephone referrals from Health Care professionals within the BNSSG area for appropriate adult medical admissions whilst being sensitive to the capacity issues of the hosting acute trust
  • Demonstrate excellent communication skills with referring HCPs, in order to build positive relationships so that alternative management ideas can be discussed without confrontation
  • Gain familiarity with the other urgent care services available in the BNSSG system, and how to access these for patients
  • Undertake clinical work by telephone +/- video, consulting with patients and/ or their representatives and healthcare professionals in the community to appropriately assess the current concerns, establish an appropriate differential diagnosis and management plan
  • Seek to support community management wherever possible, but be able to recognise serious illness and emergency situations requiring admission and/ or an ambulance response
  • Be able to prescribe appropriately for the urgent primary care context, including initiating and changing end of life medications
  • Document the key findings from their assessment, such that the notes provide appropriate detail to log the assessment at the time, and support other clinicians who may be involved later in the patient's journey.

BrisDoc is an employee-owned social enterprise that has been providing NHS healthcare for over twenty years. Serving more than one million patients across Bristol, North Somerset, and South Gloucestershire, BrisDoc offers a range of primary care services, including:

descriptionHtml:

If you've ever wanted to do more, see more, go further or be better, we have roles in more professions and vocations than ever before. Let's see where your future will take you, together.

employer: Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in Thoracic Surgery
descriptionHtml: The thoracic surgery service attracts national referrals for specialist complex surgery in both adults and children. Between the Royal Brompton, Harefield and Evelina sites we offer a wide range of thoracic treatments and perform in excess of 2,000 cases each year. We are the designated centre for sarcoma in London and the South East, seeing a range of metastatic, primary and chest wall disease. We have a strong record for performing VATS, and particularly, single port VATS lung resections. Since the arrival of a Da Vinci Xi robot on the Brompton site in 2025, followed by a Da Vinci 5 on the Harefield site in 2026, we have rapidly developed a busy RATS programme. We perform a large number of interventional bronchoscopies, with both rigid and fibre-optic techniques.  The Thoracic Surgery Department is currently expanding in response to the forecasted activity increase following the introduction of Targeted Lung Health Checks (TLHC). TLHC pilot schemes are already underway offering low-dose CT scans to those assessed as high risk. It is expected that we will see stage migration with more patients diagnosed with stage 1 lung cancer in our lung MDMs, this will contribute to the national ambition for 75% of cancers to be diagnosed at Stage 1 and 2 by 2028. As a result of the programme, there will be a higher proportion of patients who are suitable for curative treatment, in particular a higher number of thoracic surgery cases. Provide High Quality Care to Patients o The post-holder must be medically qualified and maintain GMC specialist registration, hold a licence to practice and fulfill the requirements for revalidation. o To develop and maintain the competencies required to carry out the duties required of the post. o To ensure patients are involved in decisions about their care and to respond to their views.  Leadership and Team Working o To demonstrate excellent leadership skills with regard to individual performance, clinical teams, the Trust and when participating in national or local initiatives. o To work collaboratively with all members of the multi-disciplinary team and Kings Health Partners as required.  Performance Management o To work with medical, nursing and managerial colleagues to ensure high performance in the following areas: o Clinical efficiency e.g. LOS reductions, reducing cancelled operations and DNA rates. o Quality of outcomes e.g. infection control targets, reducing re-admission rates. o Financial management e.g. identification, implementation and achievement of cost improvement programmes and participating in efforts to ensure services are provided cost effectively. o Operational efficiency e.g. waiting list activity and meeting cancer treatment targets.Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust comprises five of the UK's best known hospitals - Guy's, St Thomas', Evelina London Children's Hospital, Royal Brompton and Harefield - as well as community services in Lambeth and Southwark, all with a long history of high quality care, clinical excellence, research and innovation.  We are among the UK's busiest, most successful foundation trusts. We provide specialist care for patients including heart and lung, cancer and renal services as well as a full range of local hospital and community services for people in Lambeth and Southwark.  Royal Brompton and Harefield hospitals joined Guy's and St Thomas' in February 2021 and is the largest specialist heart and lung centre in the UK and among the largest in Europe. We provide treatment for people with heart and lung disease, including rare and complex conditions, offering some of the most sophisticated treatment that is available anywhere in the world.  Our integrated approach to caring for patients from before birth, through childhood, adolescence and into adulthood and old age has been replicated around the world and has gained Royal Brompton and Harefield an international reputation as a leader in heart and lung diagnosis, treatment and research.  We strive to recruit and retain the best staff as the dedication and skills of our employees lie at the heart of our organisation and ensure that our services are of the highest quality, safe and focused on our patients.

title: Consultant Psychiatrist for Adult Community Mental Health Service
descriptionHtml:
Help shape the future of adult mental healthcare in Berkshire. Join a forward-thinking community of Consultant Psychiatrists committed to delivering high-quality compassionate care, driving clinical excellence, and working collaboratively to improve outcomes for patients.

As an experienced Consultant Psychiatrist, you'll join a friendly, well-established multidisciplinary team based in Maidenhead and Windsor. We are a CQC 'Outstanding' rated community and we're proud to be one of the first to achieve Advanced Foundation Trust (AFT) status - a new national mark of excellence from NHS England.

You'll play a central role in a supportive, clinically led service, where your knowledge and expertise directly influence how care is delivered. We'll support you to build a career that reflects your interests, whether that's advancing your clinical practice, getting involved in service transformation, research and development or stepping into leadership.

All of this comes with the added benefit of living and working in one of the UK's most desirable regions, offering an excellent balance between career and lifestyle.

If you meet the essential criteria and would like an informal discussion before applying, please contact one of the team (see details below).

We are pleased to offer aRecruitment premium of £15,000 and relocation allowance of £8,000 (if applicable) for external candidates.

As a Consultant Psychiatrist you will:

  • Provide consultant-level clinical leadership within the WAM Community Mental Health Team (CMHT), working with locality psychiatry colleagues to deliver high-quality, patient-centred care
  • Deliver direct and consultative psychiatric input into assessment, formulation, and ongoing patient management, supporting recovery-focused outcomes
  • Contribute to initial psychiatric assessments via the Common Point of Entry (CPE), supporting triage and referral management from primary care

  • Engage with GPs and primary care colleagues, supporting coordinated, integrated and seamless care pathways

This is a full-time role, with three days based in our Maidenhead office. Flexible options can be discussed.

Berkshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust is a specialist mental health and community health services trust. title: Salaried GP - GP Surgery
descriptionHtml:

Undertake home visits

employer: Royal United Hospitals Bath NHS Foundation Trust
title: Acute Medicine Consultant
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for the post of Consultant in Acute Medicine at the Royal United Hospitals Bath NHS Foundation Trust. This is a great opportunity for an enthusiastic individual to join a dynamic team of consultants at a time when the service is expanding from investment.

We are happy to support applicants who wish to work full time, part time or in a flexible working pattern. We are interested to hear from you if you have a passion for Acute Medicine, but also want to maintain a specialist interest in another area, as most of our team work in this way. We are a warm and welcoming MDT, proud to work in this fast-paced environment using evidence-based best practice. We would like to hear from candidates who want to develop skills in this engaging specialism, or more experienced physicians who can consolidate their own skills whilst supporting others.

The Acute Medicine service sits within Medical Division, and as part of the Integrated Front Door Service. We provide a responsive interface between primary and secondary care needs, identifying and managing those unwell patients who require inpatient acute hospital treatment, while also supporting primary care clinicians in managing other patients safely and effectively in the community.

If you would like to know more about this opportunity, please contact our Clinical Lead, Dr Sarah Gillett on sarahgillett@nhs.net, for an informal chat.

We have a rolling rota which encompasses 7 day cover for the Medical Short Stay (MSS) unit and patients remaining in the Medical Assessment Unit (MAU) for daily ward rounds, and post take rounds.

Our Same Day Emergency Care (SDEC) area, located next to the Emergency Department and MAU is a purpose-built space for this key front door service. The consultants are supported by specialty doctors, Medical Nurse Practitioners and nurses, to assess and treat patients referred from primary care, that require urgent assessment and diagnostic tests but do not necessarily require admission. We also care for patients referred by our own ED and acute medical teams, enabling a safe and supported and timely discharge from hospital. The SDEC service manages a dedicated phone line, for community partners to access consultant advice and guidance, supporting patients to be given the right care in the right place.

MAU has a target length of stay of up to 12-24 hours and is for the initial assessment and management of acutely ill medical patients prior to discharge or admission into the hospital. The RUH benefits from a separate front door frailty service and a dedicated Older Persons Assessment Unit.

MSS is for patients who need a 1 or 2-night stay in hospital, and these patients remain under the care of the acute medicine team, receiving consultant led ward rounds and MDT care.

At the RUH we put people at the heart of what we do, working together as one team to make a difference for our patients, each other, and our community. No matter what your role is, we value everyone's contribution in supporting the exceptional, person-centred care we pride ourselves on.

We are proud to be in the top 20 best hospitals to work for in the country.

We are committed to creating a compassionate and inclusive environment. This can be seen in our growing community of staff networks - celebrating successes and creating opportunities to listen and learn. We value our differences, champion kindness and civility, and truly believe that diversity makes us stronger.

A culture of learning, developing and innovating is the thread that runs throughout our whole organisation. We want to support you to thrive, taking your career to its full potential.

We value staff well-being, with a well-established programme of support. We believe in a holistic approach spanning all aspects of living a healthy life, including physical, emotional, spiritual and financial well-being. We've even got a pool!

We are committed to supporting you and hope you want to join our team. In the meantime, find out more about living and working the beautiful historic city of Bath, learn about our extensive package of staff benefits, and read about how we're providing healthcare fit for the future with the landmark Dyson Cancer Centre and our passion for research.

As an active member of a progressive Primary Care Network serving around 44,000 patients, and with a well-established Integrated Neighbourhood Team (INT), we work collaboratively to deliver high-quality, patient-centred care.

Based in the vibrant coastal city of Portsmouth, we offer an excellent work-life balance, with beaches, the South Downs National Park, and direct rail links to London all within easy reach.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
We are recruiting up to 6 sessions at NPC Spring Terrace, North Shields on a fixed term basis for 12 months. This is an excellent opportunity for a GP who is passionate about delivering high-quality patient care and is keen to play a key role in shaping the future of a thriving practice.

NPC Spring Terrace is a welcoming, community-focused practice serving the population of North Shields and surrounding areas, with a strong commitment to delivering high-quality, patient-centred care. As part of Northumbria Primary Care and the wider NPC North Tyneside neighbourhood, the practice benefits from a diverse multidisciplinary team and a collaborative network across four local sites, providing opportunities for shared learning, peer support, and service resilience.

As a teaching practice, Spring Terrace Health Centre takes great pride in developing our future work force in primary care. This includes GP registrars, medical students, nursing students and the continued development of all staff.

As a practice Spring Terrace has been on a journey of quality improvement over recent years and is subsequently growing its patient list, clinical space and workforce.

Please note we reserve the right to close this vacancy prior to the closing date once the required number of suitable applications have been received.

As a GP Practice which is part of Northumbria Primary Care, we work with flexibility and independence to run the surgery based on what is best for our patients and staff, and additionally we have the regular and consistent support of the management team to help us to focus on what is clinically important.

As a Salaried GP the post holder will be a key clinician within the team. A job plan will be agreed with you to provide general medical services and deal with a wide range of health needs in a primary care setting.

NPC is a pioneering partnership with local GPs and now manages several GP practices with around 120,000 registered patients in Northumberland and North Tyneside.

As an NPC GP we can offer some great benefits some of which are:

  • Protected time for QI and indirect clinical care.
  • 15 minute appointments.
  • Opportunities for portfolio working and development of specialist clinical interest roles.
  • Access to all benefits of Northumbria healthcare; lease cars; home electronics; health and wellbeing offers.
  • Support with education, monthly education timeout sessions as well as a quarterly, NPC practice wide education sessions covering a range of topics dictated by the needs of our clinicians. Free access to Red Whale, mentorship and coaching.
  • Support managing medication requests, reviews and document management (coders) to increase efficiency and reduce the admin burden on GPs.

Although part of a larger organisation, NPC, as a GP practice, we work with flexibility and independence to run the surgery based on what is best for our patients and staff, and additionally we have the regular and consistent support of the management team to help us to focus on what is clinically important.

We are a forward-thinking organisation and as part of our culture we are embracing new technologies to improve the services we offer our patients. We understand the importance of listening to our patients and are not afraid to make changes following feedback.

title: Training Programme Director - T&O Surgery - TV
descriptionHtml:
Within NHS England, South East Region, the Thames Valley Local Office is responsible for the planning, development, education and training of the future and current healthcare and public health workforce across Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire.

An opportunity has arisen for a Consultant with a strong interest in medical education and training to be the Training Programme Director in T&O.

Applications are invited from current STC members, or from those within the specialty who can demonstrate relevant interest in education and training.

The successful candidate will be responsible for the overall delivery of the training programme. For more information regarding the post please refer to the attached Job Description with enclosed Person Specification.The role of the Training Programme Director is to work with the Head of School in leading the delivery of a wide range of functions, aligned to NHS England mandate.

The Training Programme Director will focus upon improvement of learner supervision, assessment and experience, engagement of faculty and ensuring effective educational outcomes, both now and in the future. The role is evolving and will also focus on whole workforce transformation and developing multi-professional links.

The ideal candidate will be an experienced NHS Consultant, currently working within the Thames Valley, with a thorough understanding of T&O training across the region and who will also have strong leadership and communication skills and be able to work effectively as a member of a multi-professional team.

NHS England has a wide range of statutory functions, responsibilities and regulatory powers. These are focused on supporting the wider NHS to deliver high quality care, as well as doing those things that are best done once for the whole NHS.

Our staff bring expertise across clinical, operational, commissioning, technology, data science, cyber security, software engineering, education, and commercial specialisms -- enabling us to design and deliver high-quality NHS services.

In March 2025,the Government announced that NHS England and the Department of Health and Social Care will increasingly merge functions, ultimately leading to NHS England being fully integrated into the department.

If you currently work within the NHS and if successful at interview, we will initiate an Inter Authority Transfer (IAT) via the Electronic Staff Record (ESR). This retrieves key data from your current or previous NHS employer to support onboarding, including competency status, Continuous Service Dates (CSD), and annual leave entitlement. You may opt out at any stage of the process.

Colleagues with a contractual office base are expected to spend, on average, at least 40% of their time working in our offices.

We cannot offer visa sponsorship for any vacancies.

employer: Lancashire & South Cumbria NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Psychiatrist, General Adult - Darwen CMHT
descriptionHtml:
Consultant Psychiatrist - General Adult Community Psychiatry, Blackburn (10PA)

We are looking to recruit a substantive Consultant Psychiatrist to work with the Darwen CMHT, based at Daisyfield Mill, Blackburn. The post is full time (10PAs). This post is one of six CMHT Adult Consultant Psychiatrist posts (6 WTE) within the Pennine Lancs locality. The post holder will carry no responsibility for inpatients.

You will be expected to participate on the Consultant On Call rota, for which additional remuneration will be paid.

The Consultant will provide Medical Leadership to the CMHT MDT and will work with medical and non-medical colleagues as part of a Multi-Disciplinary Team.

The Multi-disciplinary Team will be made up of the Mental Health Nursing team, Pharmacists, Psychologists and Occupational Therapists with input from Social Workers from the relevant Local Authority.

The post will give opportunities for teaching colleagues including resident doctors, Medical students and other professionals.

Applicants should hold full GMC registration and be included on the Specialist register of the GMC or they should be eligible for entry to the Specialist Register within 6 months of the interview date.

It is a requirement that applicants are Section 12 Approved at the time of commencing employment and have or are eligible to have Approved Clinician Status. Remuneration will be as set out in the terms of the New Consultant Contract according to previous experience.

The role:

  • At least 2.5 SPAs as standard for a full time post (we would be flexible in looking at enhancements to support other activities that support the wider ambitions of the Trust).
  • Excellent peer support group
  • Opportunities to be a clinical supervisor
  • Study leave budget of £3000 over 3 years or up to £5000 over 3 years for newly qualified Consultants
  • Relocation package available.

At our Trust, we're really keen to develop our Consultant workforce and nurture their areas of interest in a flexible way where possible. Come and have a chat with us about what your special interest or development area and build a suitable job plan with us.

We also have an extremely active Medical Education department and support our Consultants in becoming Clinical & Educational Supervisors and nurturing their interests in this area.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
We are looking to welcome a motivated and enthusiastic salaried GP to join our friendly, patient focussed team. We can offer an attractive salary and would be pleased to provide more information and/or the option of an informal visit to meet our Practice team.

For further information about both the Practice and the post please contact our Practice Manager.

We have 6 sessions available on Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday each week.

We are looking for a professional who is committed to providing consistently high standards of patient focussed care and who will contribute to the wider clinical team and the development of the practice.

Key Responsibilities include :-

  • Assess, diagnose and manage patients across urgent, primary and community care settings.
  • Prescribe, investigate, refer and escalate care as clinically required.
  • Deliver face-to-face, telephone and remote consultations.
  • Maintain clear and accurate clinical records.
  • Provide high-quality patient communication and safety-netting.
  • Work effectively within multidisciplinary teams and established clinical pathways.
  • Support safe, patient-centred care while meeting governance and safeguarding requirements.
  • Contribute to service quality, patient safety and continuous improvement initiatives

This would be an ideal opportunity for either an experienced GP looking for a change or a newly qualified GP looking to make their mark. You will be joining a friendly, supportive team in a well-established, stable practice with good facilities and excellent opportunities for personal development.

We are a semi-rural dispensing practice of approximately 9,750 patients based in the historic market town of Evesham, on the edge of the Cotswolds, and with excellent transport links to Cheltenham, Stratford-upon-Avon, Birmingham, Oxford and London.

We pride ourselves on promoting a traditional caring ethos of General Practice, whilst evolving within a modern healthcare environment.

employer: Mid and South Essex NHS Foundation Trust

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
SALARIED GP POSITION

2 DAYS PER WEEK, NEGOTIABLE - Must be able to work Mondays and Tuesdays. Working hours between 8:00am and 6:30pm.

A new and exciting opportunity has arisen for a GP to join our friendly, progressive and efficient practice team. We are looking for an enthusiastic, hardworking, team player, for 2 days per week. Salary negotiable dependent on experience.

We are a practice who encourage a wide skill mix across the whole clinical workforce, and expect all clinical team members to work collaboratively.

Informal visits and questions are very welcome by contacting Izzy.Culliss@nhs.net

We are looking for a dynamic, professional and friendly GP to join our practice team to continue to deliver the high standard of clinical care we currently provide.

The post holder must be dedicated, responsible, and driven to contribute to the innovative and forward thinking practice direction, and be a key team player.

They must have an awareness of and compliance with all relevant practice policies/guidelines, e.g. safeguarding, prescribing, confidentiality, data protection, health and safety etc.

Excellent communication skills and a friendly attitude are essential.

Contract:

2 days per week

Mix of routine work, and on-call/duty days

Supervising colleagues/allied health professionals and supporting trainees (GP registrars, Nursing students, Reception apprentices)

15 minutes appointments

All work allocated on clinical screen i.e. no hidden work

Working day(s) would be Mondays and Tuesdays

Some evening and weekend may be required occasionally

Flexibility around start and end times and adherence to GP contract changes essential

Permanent position

Marysville Medical Practice is a developing and growing practice situated in the Belle Vue area of Shrewsbury providing medical care for approximately 6500 patients. We are a forward thinking team, keen to adopt and progress innovative ideas and solutions whilst providing excellent clinical care.
