title: Diabetes Specialist Nurse - Bedford Division
descriptionHtml:
Ready to make an impact?

We are seeking a skilled and compassionate Diabetes Specialist Nurse to join our team at Kingsway & Bramingham Practice of Modality Partnership on a full-time basis. Working as an autonomous specialist nurse providing expert assessment, treatment, care planning and ongoing management for adults with Type 1, Type 2 and complex diabetes, together with associated cardiometabolic conditions, across primary and community care. The postholder will manage an appropriate specialist caseload and focus particularly on patients whose needs extend beyond routine long-term-condition review, including treatment intensification, multimorbidity, frailty, renal impairment, cardiovascular risk and uncontrolled hypertension.

At Modality Partnership, our CARE values Commitment, Accountability, Respect, and Excellence guide everything we do, and youll be joining a team that brings these values to life in every patient interaction and across the wider organisation.

Why Join Us?

NHS pension scheme

Minimum 27 days annual leave + 8 bank holidays (pro rata)

Employee discounts and benefits scheme

Employee Assistance Programme (EAP)

Education and career development pathways

Enhanced family-friendly policies, flexible working options, and wellbeing initiatives

The role requires the postholder will manage an appropriate specialist caseload and focus particularly on patients whose needs extend beyond routine long-term-condition review including treatment intensification, multimorbidity, frailty, renal impairment, cardiovascular risk and hypertension.

  • Undertake comprehensive, person-centred assessment and formulate clear, evidence-based management plans with agreed goals, follow-up and safety-netting.
  • Optimise diabetes treatment, including oral therapies and injectable treatments within professional competence and agreed prescribing arrangements.
  • Assess and manage hypertension and wider cardiovascular and renal risk in people with diabetes in accordance with current NICE guidance, local pathways and individual clinical circumstances.
  • Work closely with GPs, pharmacists, nurses, healthcare assistants, dietitians, podiatry, community teams and secondary-care diabetes services as an expert member of the multidisciplinary team.
  • Provide specialist advice, education and clinical leadership to strengthen consistent, safe diabetes care across Modality sites.
  • Provide visible clinical leadership to nurses and healthcare practitioners, supporting supervision, mentoring, competency development and confidence in diabetes care and technology.
  • Use clinical audit, population-health data and quality-improvement methods to identify gaps in care and improve outcomes, while ensuring that individualised care remains central.

Our Bedford practices are part of Modality Partnership, one of the UKs largest GP super-partnerships, serving over 500,000 patients with a workforce of more than 1,800 staff. We continuously innovate to improve patient care and staff experience, embracing digital tools and automation to enhance how services are delivered.

All employees are welcomed to enrol in our employee benefits scheme and NHS pension scheme. We are committed to developing our people through education and career pathways and who align to our organisational values of CARE.

Modality Partnership is an Equal Opportunities Employer and is committed to ensuring equal employment opportunities for all our potential applicants in line with the Equality Act, 2010.

Application Process

If you are passionate about delivering high-quality care, supporting patients to adopt self-care strategies, and contributing to service improvement within primary care, and are looking for a career-advancing opportunity where your expertise is valued, we encourage you to apply. Join a growing team of like-minded professionals at Modality Partnership and make a real difference every day while developing your career.

employer: York and Scarborough Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Paediatrician with expertise in Cardiology
descriptionHtml:
York and Scarborough Teaching Hospital NHS Foundation Trust is delighted to invite candidates to apply to work with us as a Consultant in Paediatrics with an expertise in Cardiology at York Hospital.

title: Consultant in Rheumatology
descriptionHtml:
The appointee will join the well-established department of eight existing consultants in rheumatology. This post will be Cross site between Bedford and Luton Sites. The successful candidate will augment and complement the consultant capacity, to help drive forwards the department's vision of a comprehensive rheumatology service. Sub-specialty interest in any area appropriate for a DGH (such as vasculitis, bone health or axial spondyloarthritis) is welcomed, as is an enthusiasm for teaching, audit and research.

The post holders will work with the other Consultants to provide specialty rheumatology advice and support to patients within the Trust. They will attend the weekly multi-disciplinary departmental meetings and weekly X-ray meetings, and will be expected to help support and train the registrars and other junior medical staff in rheumatology/general medicine, and the Clinical Nurse Specialists.

Where possible, the post-holder will be encouraged to develop a research interest, compatible with the background of the department and its facilities. Audit will be a mandatory part of the role.

The Rheumatology Directorate has close links with local General Practitioners and there is an active teaching program for them, and also for all grades of doctors within the Trust. The post holder will be encouraged to continue teaching and training at all levels.

Clinical Governance and Audit projects are undertaken as an ongoing programme within the department of Rheumatology - examining local practice compared to National Standards of care (for example use of biologic therapy, DAS scoring, early arthritis pathways and comparison to BSR Standards) - and Trust-wide. It is expected that the appointee will be actively involved in this.

Bedfordshire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust provides hospital services to a growing population of around 700,000 people living across Bedfordshire and the surrounding areas across two busy hospital sites in Bedford and Luton. Both hospital sites offer key services such as A&E, Obstetrics-led Maternity and Paediatrics. You will be joining a friendly, high performing Trust committed to ensuring the health and wellbeing of staff. As one of the largest NHS Trusts in our region you will have access to a programme of high quality training and development to help you grow your career. The Trust continues to be committed to delivering the best patient care using the best clinical knowledge and technology.

Our Values

We not only recruit based on qualifications and experience - we recruit individuals who demonstrate the behaviours which underpin our Trusts core values. We achieve this by using values based recruitment. We are dedicated to making our recruitment practices as inclusive as possible for everyone, we are committed to promoting equality and diversity, and creating a culture that values differences.

Please note that vacancies may close prior to the advertised closing date when sufficient number of applications have been received. All new staff will be subject to a probationary period covering first 6 months in post. Travel between hospital sites may be required. Please review all documents attached to ensure you familiarize yourself with all requirements of the job.

title: Consultant - Gastroenterologist
descriptionHtml:
Applicants are invited to apply for an exciting Consultant Gastroenterologist opportunity at Royal Cornwall Hospitals NHS Trust, based in the cathedral city of Truro. This is an excellent opportunity to join a dynamic and supportive department delivering high-quality clinical care, education, research and innovation.

The successful candidate will join a team of nine Gastroenterologists and four Hepatologists serving a population of approximately 580,000. The department has benefited from significant investment, including a £3.4 million redevelopment of the Endoscopy Unit, which includes seven procedure rooms and supports a comprehensive endoscopy service.

The service provides advanced endoscopy including EMR, ESD, ERCP, EUS, capsule endoscopy and bowel cancer screening. We also deliver specialist services in IBD, nutrition, hepatology and complex polyp management, supported by experienced multidisciplinary teams and specialist nursing staff.

Applications are welcomed from clinicians with interests in advanced endoscopy, IBD, nutrition, hepatology, education, research, digital innovation or service development. Opportunities exist to undertake leadership, teaching and quality improvement activities.

Cornwall offers an exceptional quality of life, combining stunning coastline, beautiful countryside and excellent leisure opportunities with the chance to build a rewarding consultant career.

The successful candidate will play a central role in the continued development of gastroenterology services at Royal Cornwall Hospitals NHS Trust.

The job will entail:

Outpatients care - clinics (usually 2 a week), endoscopy lists (usually 2 a week)

Inpatient care - 1 in 9 ward weeks, 1 in 9 endoscopy on call, GiM post take ward round (3.5 hr evening ward round approx 1 in 18 weekdays only. No overnight or weekend GiM commitment)

Teaching - undergraduate and post graduate teaching (with opportunities to expand this if interested)

Attendance at MDTs and governance meetings

Personal development and leaderships opportunities if desired

Research opportunities if desired

Royal Cornwall Hospitals NHS Trust is the principal provider of acute and specialist healthcare services for Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly, serving a population of approximately 580,000 people. Services are delivered across Royal Cornwall Hospital in Truro, St Michael's Hospital in Hayle and West Cornwall Hospital in Penzance, alongside a range of community-based services.

The Trust provides a comprehensive range of acute and specialist care and works closely with partners across the health and care system to deliver high-quality, patient-centred services and improve outcomes for local communities.

As a teaching hospital and partner of the University of Exeter Medical School, the Trust has a strong reputation for education, training and research. Staff benefit from opportunities in leadership, teaching, innovation and clinical research, supported by continued investment in facilities, technology and service development.

Cornwall offers an outstanding quality of life, with dramatic coastline, beautiful countryside, excellent schools and thriving communities. Combined with strong transport links and extensive outdoor leisure opportunities, it provides an ideal location in which to build both a successful career and rewarding lifestyle.

title: Consultant Psychiatrist East Brighton NMHT (£45k RRP)
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking a Consultant Psychiatrist to join the East Neighbourhood Mental Health Team (NMHT) formerly known as East Assessment and Treatment Service (ATS) in Brighton & Hove. You will be joining a mutually supportive, friendly and enthusiastic team with a real passion for what we do.

Brighton and Hove Community services are split into three main teams, East and West and Central NMHT, each NMHT has a geographical patch determined by alignment to a small number of GP surgeries, this helps facilitate good liaison with our Primary Care colleagues. This post will be in Ardingly Court Cluster. We are also fortunate to have a large array of third sector organisations in Brighton and Hove whom we have developed strong links with.

This job attracts aRecruitment and Retention payment of £45,000,in addition to(up to) £8000 relocation allowance.The RRP payment is paid in the following instalments:

o£15,000 payable upon successful recruitment

o£10,000 payable at 12 months' service

o£10,000 payable at 24 months' service

o£10,000 payable at 36 months' service

The Recruitment and Retention payment is pro rata for part time employees. If you would like further information, or to know the full terms of the Recruitment and Retention Payment and/or the Relocation Allowance, then please do not hesitate to contact our Medical HR Team - spft.medicalhr@nhs.net

We are a large multi-disciplinary community mental health team, which provides specialist assessments and treatment to patients presenting with a range of complex and unstable mental health and social needs.

As a consultant psychiatrist in our team, your main duties will be to:

Provide specialist medical /psychiatric assessment and evidence-based treatment to patients referred to the service.

Provide clinical supervision to the HST and informal advice and supervision to non-medical members of the team

Fulfil the duties of Responsible Clinician for patient's subject to Community Treatment Orders including attendance at Mangers Hearings and Tribunals.

Mental Health Act assessments for patients on the team caseload

Liaison with inpatient Responsible Clinicians

Liaison with the forensic team/drug and alcohol services and risk panel as required

Sussex Partnership provides mental health and learning disability care for all age groups across Sussex and for children and young people in Hampshire.

Brighton & Hove is a unique, vibrant and exciting place to live and work, offering a lively city life with the opportunity to get away from it all to the South Downs National park just on the doorstep. The city offers excellent access to London and is in close proximity to Gatwick Airport. Brighton is proud to be a diverse and inclusive city, and this is reflected in the staff mix employed by SPFT, and by the ethos of the Trust.

We encourage flexible working. We know that a positive work/ life balance brings about huge health-related benefits, which has a positive impact on the care we provide. Please speak to us about flexible working, for example, home-working, part time hours, flexible start/ finish times or anything else. If it works for you and works for the role, we'll do our best to make it happen.

title: Senior Clinical Fellow in Maternal Fetal Medicine
descriptionHtml:
Whittington Health NHS Trust is seeking an enthusiastic Senior Clinical Fellow in Maternal Fetal Medicine to join its Women's Health Directorate. This role offers a valuable opportunity to develop specialist skills in fetal medicine, working closely with experienced fetal medicine consultants and the wider multidisciplinary team to support women with pregnancies affected by complex fetal conditions. The successful candidate will contribute to fetal medicine clinics, ultrasound assessment, antenatal care planning and coordinated multidisciplinary management, while also participating in teaching, quality improvement and research activities. The post includes broader obstetric and gynaecology responsibilities and provides excellent senior registrar-level experience within a busy and supportive London maternity service. Please note that this post may close early if sufficient applications are received.The Senior Clinical Fellow in Maternal Fetal Medicine will play a key role in delivering specialist fetal medicine services, supporting the assessment and management of pregnancies affected by complex fetal conditions. Working alongside experienced fetal medicine consultants in a multidisciplinary environment, the post offers excellent opportunities to develop advanced fetal medicine and ultrasound skills, contribute to education and research, and gain valuable senior registrar experience within a busy London maternity unit.About Whittington Health

Whittington Health is an integrated NHS organisation providing both acute and community healthcare services across North London. Serving a diverse population of more than 440,000 people, the Trust is recognised for delivering high-quality, patient-centred care and is one of the principal teaching campuses for University College London (UCL) Medical School.

About the Department

The Maternal Medicine, Diabetes in Pregnancy and Fetal Medicine services form part of the Women's Health Directorate within the Obstetrics and Gynaecology Department at Whittington Hospital. The department provides specialist, multidisciplinary care for women with complex maternal and fetal conditions, working closely with obstetricians, fetal medicine specialists, physicians, sonographers, specialist midwives, neonatal teams and allied health professionals to deliver coordinated, high-quality maternity care

title: Recovery Worker
descriptionHtml:
Join our team as a Recovery Worker in Shropshire.

Are you a compassionate and motivated individual who wants to change peoples lives? Our team in Shropshire is looking for a Recovery Worker to join them in providing high-quality recovery care to a diverse client group. If you are enthusiastic, creative and passionate about helping others, wed love to hear from you.

As a leading charity supporting people with drug, alcohol, and mental health challenges, we operate over 80 services across England and Scotland, providing free and confidential support to more than 100,000 people each year. Find out more about us on our website.

Please use the Job Description to support your application.

As a Recovery Worker, we offer a starting salary of £26,250 per annum, rising each year in line with our pay progression salary bands, to £30,900 per annum.

The closing date for applications is 20th November 2026. Please note that this role may close earlier than the stated deadline if we receive a high volume of applications, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. All applicants must submit a CV along with a cover letter explaining why they should be considered for this role.

Our South Shropshire Team offers a unique opportunity to work in one of the county's most rural communities, where no two days are ever the same. As a Recovery Worker, you'll enjoy the autonomy to manage a varied caseload across towns and villages, building meaningful relationships with the people you support and becoming a valued part of the local community. Rural working allows for truly person-centred care, strong partnerships with local agencies, and the chance to make a lasting difference where services can be harder to access. If you're someone who enjoys variety, independence, collaborative working and seeing the real impact of your work, our South Shropshire Team could be the perfect place for you to grow your career and change lives.

This is a frontline role at WithYou, where you will provide continuity of care through effective partnership working, care coordination, key work responsibilities, and intervention delivery. You will manage an active caseload, connecting quickly with clients and ensuring theyre always treated with respect and dignity. You will be working within a highly skilled and knowledgeable multi-disciplinary team who will support you in your development and your ability to deliver the best care you can to our clients.

This role is full time and permanent, based in Bridgnorth and the surrounding areas across the South of Shropshire. The working hours are 37.5 per week, including some Saturday work on a rota basis.

As a leading charity supporting people with drug, alcohol, and mental health challenges, we operate over 80 services across England and Scotland, providing free and confidential support to more than 100,000 people each year. Find out more about us on our website.

title: Salaried GP

2 Positions available

6 Sessions & 4 Sessions

Days to be confirmed

This is an exciting opportunity to work alongside a stable, experienced team that is committed to delivering high-quality patient care while continually improving workload management, clinical processes and staff wellbeing.

title: Advanced Medical Practitioner - Care Homes
descriptionHtml:
South Doc Services (SDS) is hiring an Advanced Medical Practitioner (AMP) on behalf of West Heath Surgery.

This will be a full time, permanent role with a 37.5 hours per week contract arrangement. The job location is at West Heath Surgery, 194 - 196 West Heath Road, Birmingham, B31 3HB. Pay / Salary is dependent on experience level.

If you wish to have the full job description, please email rhiannon.aiken@nhs.net

The Advanced Medical Practitioner (AMP) will provide high-quality, safe, effective and person-centred clinical care to patients registered with West Heath Surgery who reside in designated care homes.

The post-holder will work as an integral member of the Practice multidisciplinary team, working collaboratively with GPs, advanced practitioners, practice nurses, clinical pharmacists, community nurses, therapists, care coordinators, social care professionals, care-home staff and other relevant health and social care professionals.

The post-holder will contribute to the delivery of proactive, personalised and coordinated healthcare for care-home residents, with an emphasis on:

  • prevention of avoidable deterioration;
  • early identification and management of acute illness;
  • proactive management of frailty and long-term conditions;
  • personalised care and support planning;
  • medicines optimisation in collaboration with the appropriate prescriber/pharmacy professional;
  • reducing avoidable hospital admissions;
  • facilitating timely access to secondary and community care;
  • supporting residents to remain in their preferred place of care wherever clinically appropriate;
  • effective multidisciplinary working;
  • continuity and coordination of care; and
  • safe, evidence-based clinical decision-making.

The role will support the Practice in delivering its contractual requirements under the current NHS England Network Contract DES and Enhanced Health in Care Homes arrangements. The current EHCH model is designed around proactive, personalised and integrated care for people living in care homes rather than a predominantly reactive model.

The post-holder will work within their individual scope of professional practice, competence and authority. Where an activity requires GP, consultant, specialist or other professional input, the AMP will recognise this promptly and escalate appropriately.

Please note, this role is for West Heath Surgery, not South Doc Services.

West Heath Surgery is located within West Heath Medical Centre. We aim to provide first class up to date healthcare to the community while maintaining a family doctor relationship with all patients enabling continuity of care throughout a patients life. The Practice will continue to provide patient focused services using the criteria of clinical excellence providing healthcare to the community with equity and equality of access.

title: Consultant Psychiatrist, Director Patient Safety & Quality Governance
descriptionHtml:
This is an exciting opportunity for a Consultant Psychiatrist to become Director of Patient Safety and Quality Governance. Based in Worthing, the post provides strategic leadership across patient safety, quality governance, regulatory assurance, risk and organisational learning.

The postholder will report to the Chief Nursing Officer, advise the Board and Executive Team, and undertake up to two clinical sessions aligned with their CCT and interests. The role is permanent, comprising 10 programmed activities and a £25,000 responsibility allowance.The postholder will lead Trust-wide arrangements for patient safety and PSIRF, quality assurance, CQC readiness, risk management, health and safety, mortality review, suicide prevention and reducing restrictive practice. They will ensure that concerns are identified and escalated promptly, learning leads to measurable improvement, and the Board receives clear and timely assurance. The role includes senior cover for the Chief Nursing Officer, leadership of three direct reports and participation in the consultant on-call rota.Sussex Partnership provides mental health, learning disability and neurodevelopmental services to people of all ages across Sussex. We employ around 5,700 staff and deliver care across 53 sites, including 15 inpatient units, working closely with NHS, local authority and voluntary-sector partners. Our vision is"Delivering great care and improving outcomes together." We offer structured induction, CPD and study leave, peer support, mentoring for new consultants, wellbeing services and flexible-working opportunities.

employer: University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Clinical Fellow in Neurocritical Care
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for Clinical Fellow posts in Neurocritical Care (Intensive Care) at The National Hospital for Neurology & Neurosurgery, Queen Square, London, for a 6-month period, that can be extended to a year or more, subject to satisfactory appraisal. We have three posts available that will commence 3rd February 2027. The successful applicants will work under consultant supervision at a level best matched to their learning needs and experience.

The posts would be suited to anyone wishing to experience intensive care medicine in a nurturing environment with a view to improving their curriculum vitae with the aim of applying for core training in intensive care medicine, emergency medicine, acute medicine, neurology or neurosurgery. Despite being a neurosciences intensive care unit, many of the principles of intensive care medicine remain the same as for a general ICU. The posts are also suitable for those wanting to further their experience of neurocritical care for specialist training.

University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (UCLH) is one of the most complex NHS trusts in the UK, serving a large and diverse population. We provide academically led acute and specialist services, to people from the local area, from throughout the United Kingdom and overseas. Our vision is to deliver top-quality patient care, excellent education, and world-class research.

We provide first-class acute and specialist services across eight sites:o University College Hospital (incorporating the Elizabeth Garrett Anderson Wing)o National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgeryo Royal National ENT and Eastman Dental Hospitalso University College Hospital Grafton Way Buildingo Royal London Hospital for Integrated Medicineo University College Hospital Macmillan Cancer Centreo The Hospital for Tropical Diseaseso University College Hospital at Westmoreland Street

We are dedicated to the diagnosis and treatment of many complex illnesses. UCLH specialises in women's health and the treatment of cancer, infection, neurological, gastrointestinal and oral disease. It has world class support services including critical care, imaging, nuclear medicine and pathology.

We are committed to sustainability and have pledged to become a carbon net zero health service, embedding sustainable practice throughout UCLH. We have set an ambitious target of net zero for our direct emissions by 2031 and indirect emissions by 2040.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
Job summary

Four Elms Medical Centre is seeking two highly motivated and compassionate Salaried GPs to join our friendly / Supportive and forward-thinking team.

This post is for 6-8 sessions a week (3-4 days) primarily working in Lliswerry surgery, Newport. We have another surgery close by in Ringland, Newport and one in Cardiff. A successful candidate will predominantly work in Lliswerry but may be required to work at any of the surgeries if required, remotely or in-person. All of our doctors (11 currently) and PAs (2) work in the same capacity.

We are a well-established, forward-thinking practice supporting a 33,000 patient list shared over four sites. We have GP surgeries in the Cardiff Royal Infirmary, Pengam Green Cardiff, Ringland Newport and Lliswerry Newport. All surgeries are located just off M4 corridor with excellent transport links to Cardiff centre and Bristol.

This is an excellent opportunity for a GP looking for a fulfilling role within a strong clinical MDT setting, and the chance to become a long-term member of our thriving practice at this exciting and changing time in our General Practice.

Main duties of the job

Clinical responsibilities:

In accordance with the practice timetable, as agreed, the post-holder will make themselves available to undertake a variety of duties, including surgery consultations, telephone consultations and queries, visiting patients at home, checking and signing repeat prescriptions and dealing with queries, paperwork and correspondence in a timely fashion

Making professional, autonomous decisions in relation to presenting problems, whether self referred or referred from other health care workers within the organisation

Assessing the health care needs of patients with undifferentiated and undiagnosed problems

Screening patients for disease risk factors and early signs of illness

Developing care plans for health in consultation with patients and in line with current practice disease management protocols

Providing counselling and health education

Recording clear and contemporaneous consultation notes to agreed standards

Collecting data for audit purposes

Compiling and issuing computer-generated acute and repeat prescriptions

Prescribing in accordance with the practice prescribing formulary, or generically, whenever this is clinically appropriate

In general, the post-holder will be expected to undertake all the normal duties and responsibilities associated with a GP working within primary care.

This is not an exhaustive list of duties and responsibilities and in discussion with the recruiting manager.

Overview of your organisation

Are you looking for an exciting opportunity to join a forward thinking team under a well established partnership serving a shared 33,000 patient list in South Wales .

Our team is comprised of :

6 GP Partners and 5 salaried GPs

Mental Health practitioner

Physicians Associates

First Contact physiotherapists

General Practice Advanced Nurse Practitioner

Practice Pharmacists

Practice Nurses and Healthcare Assistants

Administrators

Reception Team

Management Team

We are an approved GP Specialty Training Practice with a strong focus on education for both GP registrars and medical students. We are recognised as a leading Postgraduate 'Training Practice' affiliated to the Wales College of Medicine, Cardiff, to provide undergraduate education.

As a partnership we are committed to giving our patients access to new treatments and healthcare opportunities through NHS-approved research studies.

If you are ready to make a commitment to our strong, highly capable team we welcome your application.

title: Locum Consultant in Geriatric Medicine
descriptionHtml:
We are looking to appoint an experience Locum Consultant in Geriatrics to join our Frailty team for a fixed period until April 2027.

We are proud to have an excellent acute frailty service and we have an enthusiastic and dynamic team of Consultants and Associate Specialists working closely together to deliver our overarching Frailty Strategy, aiming to improve the care of all patients living with frailty in Guildford and Waverley.

We are continuing to work to provide seamless care for our patients. For those with emerging or stable frailty we aim to provide standardised proactive Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment (CGA) and for those with frailty crisis, an effective alternative to admission including Urgent Crisis Response (UCR), Frailty Same Day Emergency Care (FSDEC) and Hospital at Home (H@H) / virtual wards.

We have established the Guildford and Waverley Frailty Academy which has embedded education and training across the local system and within the acute Trust. We have developed internal trainee Advanced Clinical Practitioner and Portfolio route training programmes (formerly CESR route) to support workforce development.

We are looking to innovate with local partners in delivery of a local strategy to develop our workforce and make it fit to meet the needs of our ageing population.

We would welcome applicants with experience in posts relevant to Geriatric medicine with a wide range of experience in Geriatric medicine specialty areas including community work (Hospital at Home, community wards, proactive care MDTs / clinics), acute frailty, rehabilitation, orthogeriatrics and stroke.

Royal Surrey is a compassionate and collaborative acute and community Trust. Recognising that our 5,000 colleagues are our greatest strength, we offer a comprehensive health and wellbeing programme alongside a strong commitment to developing your career. Our diverse and welcoming Royal Surrey family ensures you feel valued from your initial interview and throughout your time with us.

We are clinically led and provide joined-up care by bridging hospital and community services, alongside delivering regional specialist cancer care. Our main acute hospital site is in Guildford, with community sites at Milford, Haslemere and Cranleigh, and services delivered in patients' homes across Guildford and Waverley.

We work in partnership with Ashford & St Peter's Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust through a collaborative Group Model, supporting joined-up services, workforce flexibility and development opportunities.

The Care Quality Commission (CQC) has rated us as Outstanding. We are proud of our achievements and continue to invest in our people and infrastructure.

To learn more about life at Royal Surrey, please watch our short video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R96pMboIYdo

Adverts may close early, so you are encouraged to apply as soon as possible.

title: Training Programme Director - Emergency Medicine (South London)
descriptionHtml:
An outstanding individual or individuals is sought to fulfil the role of Training Programme Director for Emergency Medicine (South London).

The role of Training Programme Director is to work with and support the Postgraduate Dean in leading the delivery of a wide range of functions within their specialty, aligned to the NHS England mandate. The Programme Director will ensure that both national standards, determined by the Royal College and also guidelines and standards established within Emergency Medicine are met.

The successful applicant will work closely with the Head of School, other Medicine TPDs, LaSE team including; PGMDE Business Manager, Postgraduate Dean, and other key departments including Quality.

They will work with the Postgraduate Dean to produce doctors who will strive for the highest standards of patient-centred care and commit themselves to a lifetime of professional development.

The Programme Director will ensure that both national standards, determined by the Royal College, and guidelines and standards established within Emergency Medicine are met. Responsibilities will include:

  • To oversee the Specialty's Regional Training Programme
  • Specialty-specific matters and trainee/trainer concerns
  • Recruitment to training posts and programmes
  • Postgraduate programme management, including assessments, progression, rotations, support and remediation, OOP management, trainee management careers support, less than full-time training, inter-deanery transfer, academic training and other related work-streams.

The ideal candidate will be an experienced NHS Consultant with a thorough understanding of Emergency Medicine training across the region and who will also have strong leadership and communication skills and be able to work effectively as a member of a multi-professional team.

NHS England has a wide range of statutory functions, responsibilities and regulatory powers. These are focused on supporting the wider NHS to deliver high quality care, as well as doing those things that are best done once for the whole NHS.

Our staff bring expertise across clinical, operational, commissioning, technology, data science, cyber security, software engineering, education, and commercial specialisms -- enabling us to design and deliver high-quality NHS services.

In March 2025, the Government announced that NHS England and the Department of Health and Social Care will increasingly merge functions, ultimately leading to NHS England being fully integrated into the department.

If you currently work within the NHS and if successful at interview, we will initiate an Inter Authority Transfer (IAT) via the Electronic Staff Record (ESR).This retrieves key data from your current or previous NHS employer to support onboarding, including competency status, Continuous Service Dates (CSD), and annual leave entitlement. You may opt out at any stage of the process.

Colleagues with a contractual office base are expected to spend, on average, at least 40% of their time working in our offices.

We cannot offer visa sponsorship for any vacancies.

title: Clinical Fellow in Neonatal Transport (SONAR)
descriptionHtml:
The SoNAR Team is the neonatal transport service covering the South West Neonatal Network (ODN). This region has over 45,000 deliveries per year. The team runs 24 hours a day and undertakes approximately 1200 journeys per year. The transport team is able to undertake cooling, and delivery of Nitric Oxide and HFOV during transfer. The service covers both acute transfers and repatriations between the twelve neonatal units in the region as well as acute transfers to the Bristol Children's Hospital. The north team of SoNAR is based at the shared SoNAR/WATCh/Retrieve base in Aztec West (unit 350, Ash Ridge Road, Bradley Stoke, BS32 4QA). This is a hub for all three retrieval teams and houses the clinical teams, kit, drivers and vehicles all together.

We are seeking to appoint either an experienced, enthusiastic Clinical Fellow in Paediatrics/Neonates or a neonatal grid trainee seeking out of programme training from outside the Severn Deanery. The successful candidate must have level three NICU experience.

The successful candidate would be expected to become proficient and competent at delivering the vast majority of transfers on their own with consultant support although where necessary a consultant may also attend the transfer.

Knowledge and skills gained during this placement would include effective transport triage, call conferencing, prioritisation of journeys, appropriate team composition, enhanced patient assessment, management of the critically ill child during transfer and other transport related clinical skills. They would be expected to have excellent communication skills in order to facilitate good handover of information between units.

Applicants post CST wishing to widen their neonatal transport skills or considering an OOPE are actively encouraged to apply.

Bristol NHS Foundation Trust brings together more than 28,000 staff to deliver over 160 clinical services across thirteen hospital locations,operatingfrom three main sites at Southmead, Bristol citycentreand Weston.

With an annual turnover of £2.3 billion, we are now one of the largest NHS trusts in the United Kingdom. Our hospitals are spread across Bristol and Weston, join us and you can enjoy the very best of both worlds; city living within a stone's throw of the countryside or beside the seaside, both with easy access to all that theSouth Westhas to offer.

Bristol NHS Foundation Trust values all people as individuals. As an equal opportunities employer actively working towards a diverse workforce we aim to recruit andretaina workforce whichrepresentsthe rich diversity of the local population at all levels and are committed to designing our services around the needs of individual patients and those around them. title: Chief of Care Group
descriptionHtml:
CHIEF OF CARE GROUP

Senior Accountable Leadership Role

Posts Available:

  • Medicine Care Group
  • Women, Children, Young People and Families Care Group
  • Cancer Centre and Clinical Services Care Group

Swansea Bay University Health Board is implementing a clinically led Care Group model, aligning services around patient pathways to improve outcomes, experience and sustainability. This is a unique opportunity to shape how health services are designed and delivered for the population of Swansea Bay.

As Chief of Care Group, you will provide strategic leadership across a whole Care Group, holding overall accountability for quality, safety, patient experience, operational performance and financial sustainability. Working within a triumvirate model, you will lead the Care Group Clinical Director and Care Group Operational Director, ensuring cohesive, clinically informed and values-driven leadership.

You will lead service transformation, drive pathway improvement, promote staff engagement and ensure services are organised around the needs of patients, carers and communities. The role requires a visible, collaborative leader who can work across organisational boundaries and contribute to regional and system-wide priorities.

Applicants should indicate their top three Care Group preferences within their application and refer to the accompanying Care Group structure document for further information.

Interview dates: 11, 16 and 18 December

Hours: Minimum 6 sessions (3-days)

  • Act as the Accountable Officer for the Care Group, with overall responsibility for quality, safety, patient experience, operational performance and financial stewardship.
  • Provide line management and leadership to the Care Group Operational Director and Care Group Clinical Director, ensuring clarity of roles, effective decision-making and collective accountability within the triumvirate model.
  • Hold executive accountability for the effective management of professional standards and concerns within the Care Group, including oversight of consultant and senior clinician job planning, workforce utilisation and programmes to improve clinical productivity, ensuring safe, sustainable and value based clinical services.
  • Lead and sponsor the design and delivery of integrated, pathway-based models of care, ensuring services are organised around patient need rather than organisational or geographical boundaries.
  • Ensure a clinically led and prudent approach to decision-making, balancing benefit, harm and value while reducing unwarranted variation and inequality.
  • Provide assurance to Executive leadership and the Board through robust Care Group governance, including learning from complaints, incidents, mortality reviews and patient feedback, in line with Listening to People and Duty of Candour

Swansea Bay University Health Board is one of the largest public service organisations in Wales, with an annual budget of approximately £1.7 billion and a workforce of around 14,700 people. As a major employer in South West Wales, we play a pivotal role in improving health, wellbeing and life chances for the communities we serve.

We provide NHS care to a population of around 390,000 people across Swansea and Neath Port Talbot, delivering services across acute, community, mental health and primary care settings. We also host a range of specialist and tertiary services for patients from across Wales and beyond, including burns and plastics, renal services, cardiac surgery and specialist neonatal care.

Our services are delivered across Morriston Hospital, Singleton Hospital and Neath Port Talbot Hospital, alongside a comprehensive network of community and mental health provision. We also hold responsibility for commissioning primary care services, working in partnership to ensure care is accessible, timely and delivered as close to home as possible.

employer: Blackpool Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Acute Medicine
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity to join the Acute Medicine team at Blackpool Teaching Hospitals within the Division of Integrated Medicine and Emergency Care.

The Consultant team oversees and leads in the daily reviews of the medical take through these areas supporting and encouraging patient care being provided in the right place, first time ensuring national and local targets are recognised and achieved.

The service is staffed by a large team of Consultants, Registrars, junior doctors, ACP's and Physician Associates. The medical on call service is also coordinated through here that is staffed by a mixture of trainees and substantive colleagues. Many students also have their placements in the service making us a busy, fast-paced learning environment.

Please contact us to arrange an informal visit to meet the department and team.

Duties and Responsibilities as a Consultant

Maintain the knowledge and skills essential for fulfilling the job plan.

Responsible for the timely review of all medical patients attending the services.

Responsible to facilitate a rapid triage, assessment and discharge for the ambulatory patients and coordinate a clinic appointment if required.

Daily ward rounds and identifying morning discharges ensuring the patient is safely discharged from the department.

Administrative duties within the department.

Provide high quality care to patients including clinical leadership and supervision of junior medical staff..

To ensure adequate supervision of junior staff including break supervision and adherence to European Working Time Directive

Undertake re-validation as per the General Medical Council and will be required to undergo multi-source feedback and participate in reflective practice.

Adhere to all Trust policies and procedures.

Attend Clinical Governance and take on leadership roles to support continuous learning and improvement.

Liaise with clinicians and managers within and outside of the department to address issues arising that affecting the service.

Participate in relevant audit and quality assurance processes.

Management of the department to maintain efficient and timely patient flow with specific reference to both local and national standards.

Contribute towards the teaching of medical trainees and students in the department

Blackpool Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is ideally situated just a forty five minute drive from Manchester. The Trust provides services to the 440,000 residents of Blackpool, Fylde & Wyre and North Lancashire, as well as specialist tertiary care for Cardiac and Haematology patients.

As one of the United Kingdom's largest coastal resort, Blackpool has plenty to offer its residents - it's not just a good place to work; it's a great place to live. In addition to its bustling centre and historic seafront, the town is world famous for its many attractions, including the famous Blackpool Tower. employer: Central and North West London NHS Foundation Trust
title: Medical Director
descriptionHtml:
As Divisional Medical Director, you will share accountability for all aspects of the Diggory Division alongside the Managing Director and Director of Nursing. You will provide strong, compassionate clinical leadership, helping to shape the strategy, culture, and future direction ofmental health services within the Directorate.

You will be central to our transformation journey, ensuring clinical quality, developing the next generation of clinical leaders, and embedding research and innovation across services. You will represent CNWL in key system forums, influence regional strategy, and champion the delivery of high-quality, inclusive care.

Interviews will be held mid-January 2027

The postholder will be based in London but will be expected to maintain a regular and visible presence across the full geographical footprint of Diggory Division, including services in Milton Keynes and Surrey. This is a fundamental requirement of the role, ensuring accessible clinical leadership, effective engagement with staff and service users, and strong relationships with local partners. The postholder must therefore be willing and able to travel regularly between sites as required.

CNWL (Central and North West London NHS Foundation Trust) is one of the largest and most diverse community and mental health Trusts in the country. We have received a rating of "good" from the CQC; we care for people across the life course, from preconception through to the end of life. We have a wide range of outstanding partners and work across vibrant and expansive geography.

Our Trust is structured into three Operational Divisions, working alongside centralised corporate support services. Each Division is made up of borough teams and cross-boundary specialised Directorates. Each Division is managed by a team of three - a Managing Director, Director of Nursing and a Medical Director. These three report, respectively, to the Chief Operating Officer, the Chief Nurse and the Chief Medical Officer.

The Divisional teams work closely, along with their Borough and Service line leaders, with the local authority, public health, PCNs and other statutory and non-statutory partners.

We operate across two Integrated Care Systems (ICSs): West North London (WNL) and Central East.

As a trusted organisation at the heart of our communities, we recognise the important role we can play in supporting the public, patients, our own people and local partners in achieving the best of health for the local population and the communities in which they live by providing Exceptional Care Together

o We see on average 4810 OP appointments per day.o We are the 4th busiest Trauma & Orthopaedic outpatients department in England - an average of 2077 per week.o An average of 1115 patients are seen in A&Es across our network every day - 3rd largest in the country.o Our hospitals admit an average of 195 emergency patients daily.o Last year we undertook almost 33,700 planned surgical operations in our 57 operating theatres.o We are one of only 7 Trusts nationally with more than 50 operating theatres.o We carry out more than 140 elective procedures each working day.

Halesowen 24 sessions per week | Wednesdays and Fridays

Join a forward-thinking practice that puts patients and people first.

We are looking for an enthusiastic, committed and patient-focused GP to join our team in Halesowen through the Additional Roles Reimbursement Scheme (ARRS).

This is an excellent opportunity for a GP who enjoys delivering high-quality general practice, working collaboratively with colleagues and contributing to the ongoing development of a progressive primary care service.

We are a CQC-rated Good practice with a strong commitment to clinical quality, continuous improvement and staff wellbeing. We recognise that the best patient care is delivered by a supported, valued and motivated team.

The role

Working 24 sessions per week on Wednesdays and Fridays, you will provide high-quality, evidence-based general medical services to our registered patient population.

The role will involve:

Clinical consultations: Assessing, diagnosing and managing patients presenting with a broad range of acute and chronic conditions, using face-to-face and remote consultations as appropriate.

Clinical decision-making: Working autonomously within your competence, recognising when onward referral or escalation is required, and maintaining safe clinical practice.

Continuity and coordination of care: Supporting patients with ongoing healthcare needs and working effectively with the wider multidisciplinary team to ensure appropriate follow-up and coordinated care.

Prescribing and clinical management: Making safe, evidence-based prescribing decisions and managing clinical risk in line with current guidance and practice policies.

Accurate clinical documentation: Maintaining clear, timely and comprehensive patient records, including appropriate coding, safety-netting and follow-up arrangements.

Teamworking: Communicating effectively with GPs, nursing colleagues, ARRS professionals and administrative staff to support efficient patient care.

Quality and improvement: Contributing to clinical governance, significant event discussions and service improvement initiatives, helping us continually enhance the care we provide.

Our practice and culture

We believe that a positive working environment is fundamental to delivering excellent patient care. As a CQC-rated Good practice, we are committed to maintaining high standards while continuing to develop and improve our services.

Staff wellbeing is important to us. We value open communication, mutual respect, teamwork and a sustainable approach to work. We want our clinicians to feel supported, listened to and able to make a meaningful contribution to the practice.

employer: Great Ormond Street Hospital for Children NHS Foundation Trust
title: Clinical Research Fellow in Dermatology
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for an exciting 12-month full-time Clinical and Translational Research Fellowship within the National Epidermolysis Bullosa (EB) Service at Great Ormond Street Hospital for Children, London.

This unique fellowship offers an exceptional opportunity for a paediatrician or dermatologist to gain specialist clinical and academic experience at one of the world's leading centres for the care of children and young people with epidermolysis bullosa. The successful candidate will become an integral member of our multidisciplinary team, providing specialist care for patients with EB whilst contributing to pioneering translational research.

A particular highlight of this fellowship is the opportunity to play a leading role in MISSION EB DELIVER, an innovative open-label clinical study investigating EBSTROCEL mesenchymal stromal cell infusions for patients with epidermolysis bullosa. Working closely with the Clinical Research Facility at Great Ormond Street Hospital, the successful candidate will gain first-hand experience in delivering an advanced cell therapy programme, including patient assessment, infusion procedures, clinical trial delivery and longitudinal follow-up care.

This is a new post aimed for a doctor who wishes to acquire unique experience in a subspecialty of pediatric dermatology with some clinical and in addition the unusual opportunities to take part in research and the running of a clinical trial MISSIONEB-Deliver an open study of mesenchymal intravenous Stromal cell infusions, CRODStrom in children with recessive dystrophic Epidemolysis bullosa.

We are committed to recruiting the best person for the job through a fair, open and consistent process that is free from bias and discrimination.

We are working towards becoming an anti-racist organisation. This means creating a workplace where every colleague feels seen, heard and valued, and where racism in any form has no place. Our anti-racism commitment is backed by action through our Anti-Racism Statement and action plan, developed in collaboration with our REACH staff network.

We actively challenge discrimination, dismantle barriers and embed equity across all aspects of our workforce, including recruitment, progression and development. All applicants will receive equal consideration regardless of race, ethnicity, nationality, religion or belief, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, health condition or employment history.

We particularly welcome applications from ethnically diverse communities, people with disabilities or long-term health conditions, and LGBTQ+ community members. We are proud to be a Disability Confident Employer, a member of the Business Disability Forum, and a Stonewall Diversity Champion.

Our staff networks, including REACH, PRIDE, ENABLED and Women's Networks, are active and executive supported. These employee-led networks play a vital role in shaping an inclusive culture at GOSH and are open to all colleagues.

Together, we are building a culture where inclusion is not optional - it is essential.

descriptionHtml:

The Evelina PICU comprises 35 beds over 2 floors depending on activity and patient case load. The post-holder will be one of a team of 26 paediatric intensivists providing care for the paediatric critical care unit and integrated retrieval service, STRS at the Evelina.

title: Radiographer
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for an experienced HCPC-registered Diagnostic Radiographer to provide imaging for patients undergoing elective orthopaedic and spinal surgery.

You will perform post-operative orthopaedic X-rays and provide mobile C-arm fluoroscopy in theatre, including support for spinal procedures. Working with the theatre and ward teams, you will help coordinate imaging around operating lists and discharge plans.

This is an opportunity to help establish the imaging service within a new surgical hub.

The successful candidate will:

  • Perform post-operative orthopaedic X-rays and intra-operative imaging within your competence and agreed scope of practice.
  • Operate mobile C-arm equipment safely during orthopaedic and spinal procedures.
  • Check patient identity, imaging requests and pregnancy status where relevant, following agreed procedures.
  • Work within your employer entitlement under IR(ME)R, ensuring exposures are justified and authorised through the agreed pathway.
  • Optimise image quality and radiation dose, following IR(ME)R, IRR17 and local radiation protection rules.
  • Position and support patients safely, taking account of post-operative pain, mobility and surgical precautions.
  • Complete equipment checks and quality assurance tasks, escalating faults or image quality concerns promptly.
  • Maintain accurate imaging and exposure records, ensuring images are available for clinical review.
  • Follow agreed escalation pathways for urgent concerns, unexpected findings and radiation incidents.
  • Maintain infection prevention standards and work safely within the sterile theatre environment.
  • Work with the multidisciplinary team and contribute to audit, service improvement and safe imaging workflows.

One Health Group was established in Sheffield in 2004 and has steadily and successfully grown to become a significant healthcare provider in the region. Commissioned by the NHS, we provide services for patients referred for Orthopaedics, General Surgery, Spine, Urology and Gynaecology and with clinics located in over 30 locations across Yorkshire, Derbyshire, Nottinghamshire, Leicestershire and Lincolnshire, we bring healthcare closer to where people live. We are committed to clinical excellence, and our mission is to provide innovative, high quality medical and clinical services for our patients, optimising outcomes so they can quickly continue healthy lives.

Our service includes:

  • One modern operating theatre.

  • Dedicated pre-assessment and outpatient facilities.

We specialise in elective surgery, including:

  • Total hip replacement.
  • Total knee replacement.
  • Revision arthroplasty where clinically appropriate.
  • Spinal procedures including ACDF, cervical decompression, lumbar decompression, discectomy and spinal fusion procedures.

We are developing a clinical team focused on delivering safe, compassionate and high-quality patient care.

We also deliver specialist services such as Mohs' micrographic surgery, Laser, Biologics for Eczema, Vulval dermatology, and Psychodermatology. descriptionHtml:
We are recognised as one of the leading NHS Foundation Trusts in the UK, supporting around 2.8 million patient appointments every year. The Trust is a regional centre for cancer, trauma, burns & plastics and has the largest solid organ transplantation programme in Europe. Due to growth in services, particularly PET-CT, applications are invited for a permanent Consultant Radionuclide Radiologist with special interest in PET-CT/Nuclear Medicine. QEHB hosts the regional PET Centre with one of the busiest PET-CT scanners in the country with a new two-scanner PET Centre on the horizon. The Nuclear Medicine Department also performs a wide range of diagnostic imaging, in-patient and out-patient therapies and non-imaging tests, and supports numerous clinical trials. We have 3 SPECT-CT systems in the department including the first 64-slice Veriton in the UK. We have an on-site radiopharmacy and produce Gallium-68 (PSMA/Dota-peptide). The QEHB nuclear medicine department has a staff of 66 including 7 Radionuclide Radiologists and Nuclear Cardiologists. Duties will include general nuclear medicine and PET-CT reporting and participation in MDMs. Experience in radionuclide therapies will be welcomed but is not essential. There will be a requirement for a single acute inpatient CT reporting session in the job plan. The post is otherwise NM/ PET CT only and, as such, there will be no involvement in the diagnostic radiology on-call and no scope for additional subspeciality work

Duties will include reporting of general nuclear medicine and PET-CT studies as well as participation in specialist MDT meetings on behalf of the service. The postholder must be familiar with supporting a comprehensive Nuclear Medicine service including a wide range of both imaging and non-imaging studies, PET imaging including F-18 and Ga-68 tracers) and a large Radiopharmacy service. The post holder will act as an IR(ME)R practitioner (ARSAC practitioner) with a license covering the services provided in the Trust. Key skills with experience in justifying studies, answering clinical queries, troubleshooting, protocol development, study optimisation, radiation protection matters, audit and clinical governance are expected

The post-holder will be required to participate in out-of- hours Nuclear Medicine advice and guidance (ARSAC) (approx. 1 in 8). The scope of ARSAC cover is expected to expand with the upcoming new national PET contract, which may include planned out-of-hours PET CT reporting

Good communication skills with a wide range of key clinical staff is required. The post holder is expected to contribute and support to the teaching and training of a wide range of staff groups in the department

Experience in radionuclide therapies is welcomed but is not essential

7PA NM

1.75SPA(min)

title: Consultant Radiologist - Interventional
descriptionHtml:
An opportunity to join an established interventional radiology service and help shape its future development

The highly regarded, forward-thinking Radiology Department at Hampshire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is seeking an enthusiastic and motivated substantive Consultant Interventional Radiologist to join our friendly and ambitious team. This permanent appointment offers the opportunity to contribute to an established interventional radiology service, work across a broad range of procedures and help shape the future direction of the service across Hampshire Hospitals and the wider regional network.

This is an exciting time to join Hampshire Hospitals. We have invested in our interventional radiology service, with refurbishment and modernisation of our angiography suites to provide a modern clinical environment. We are looking for a colleague with a strong interest in vascular and general interventional radiology who would also welcome the opportunity to contribute to the ongoing development of our interventional oncology service.

The successful candidate will work across Basingstoke and North Hampshire Hospital and the Royal Hampshire County Hospital in Winchester, delivering a broad range of vascular and non-vascular interventional radiology procedures. Our established workload includes peripheral vascular intervention, embolisation, venous intervention, nephrostomy and biliary intervention, image-guided drainage and biopsy, vascular access and other minimally invasive treatments.

We are particularly interested in recruiting a colleague with a strong vascular interest and a broad-based general interventional radiology practice who is keen to develop their clinical interests within a supportive and collaborative team.

Alongside our established interventional workload, our interventional oncology service continues to develop, creating opportunities for the successful candidate to become involved in and contribute to the growth of minimally invasive oncological treatments, including tumour ablation and other image-guided therapies. We would welcome someone enthusiastic about developing their experience and expertise in this area and helping shape the future direction of the service.

Across HHFT we currently have 2 IR/Fluoro rooms and 1 Interventional room, 2 clinical rooms for ultrasound guided procedures, and day case recovery faculties on each site, 5 static CT scanners and 3 static MRI scanners (details below). This includes a private imaging facility on the Basingstoke site (Candover Clinic) which is part of the NHS trust and offers general X-ray, ultrasound, CT and MRI. Insignia PACS, CRIS and Talking point Voice Recognition are integrated across HHFT (PACS system undergoing replacement currently). Home-reporting workstations are provided for all Consultant Radiologists to facilitate the on-call service, flexible reporting and additional voluntary reporting ('insourcing').

The diagnostic on-call runs from 1700 - 2000 weekdays and 0900 - 2000 at the weekend, a separate rota for each site. An out of hours IR service is provided via a regional network with Frimley Health Foundation Trust.

The trust has recently committed to a multi-million pound programme of investment to refresh diagnostic imaging equipment over the next 10 years. The department has already benefited from a completely new fleet of Ultrasound machines, new X-ray rooms, and a new CT scanner. Two new MRI scanners are to be installed at the end of 2023.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
Grove Medical Centre are seeking to welcome a Salaried GP to the practice to ideally work 6 sessions per week.

title: Specialty Doctor
descriptionHtml:
The Trust is seeking a motivated and enthusiastic Specialty Doctor to join the Ealing crisis and home treatment team. Working alongside and under day-to-day supervision of the team consultants, the post-holder will provide medical input into the multidisciplinary team delivering crisis assessment and home treatment. Medical input can be provided through face-to-face contacts, case discussion with MDT colleagues, and attendance at daily huddles and clinical meetings. The post holder will be expected to participate in Mental Health Act assessments and should hold or be working towards Section 12 approval.

  • Conduct comprehensive psychiatric assessments including risk formulation and devising personalised risk management plans
  • Develop and review care plans within a multidisciplinary framework
  • Support admission avoidance by providing intensive community-based interventions
  • Participate in gatekeeping assessments for community-based patients
  • Facilitate early discharge from inpatient units through collaborative working
  • Undertake Mental Health Act assessments where necessary
  • Prescribe and monitor response to psychotropic medication
  • Contribute to urgent reviews and same-day assessments
  • Ensure high-quality clinical documentation and record keeping
  • Contribute to safeguarding assessments and processes
  • Participate in daily multidisciplinary handovers and reviews

West London NHS Trust is one of the most diverse healthcare providers in the UK, delivering a range of mental health and physical healthcare and community services. The Trust runs Broadmoor Hospital, one of three high secure hospitals in the country, with an international reputation.

Our high secure services care for patients from South of England and we provide low and medium secure services across eight London boroughs. The Trust also provides mental and physical healthcare in three London boroughs (Ealing, Hounslow and Hammersmith & Fulham). We employ over 5,000 staff, of whom 59% are BME. Our turnover for 2024-25 is over £500m.

The Trust is rated as 'Good' overallby the Care Quality Commission. Forensic services are rated as 'Outstanding'.

The Trust is an established partner and contributor in the development of the evolving North West London Integrated Care System and the Integrated Care Board. The Trust leads the NW London Children and Adolescent Mental Health provider collaborative.

title: GP with interest in Women's Health
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking an enthusiastic General Practitioner with a particular interest in Women's Health to join our established multidisciplinary womens health primary care team.

Our practice has a well-established focus on improving health outcomes for women and delivering high-quality, accessible care across all stages of life. The successful candidate will primarily provide General Medical Services (GMS) to registered patients, with a particular interest and expertise in the assessment and management of women's health needs within routine primary care.

The postholder will deliver comprehensive, holistic care for women presenting with a wide range of health concerns, ensuring that patients receive evidence-based assessment, treatment and ongoing management in line with current NHS guidance, NICE recommendations and the Women's Health Strategy for England.

The role is not intended to operate as a specialist or referral-based women's health service but rather to strengthen and enhance the delivery of women's healthcare within mainstream general practice.

  • 4 - 8 sessions per week
  • Study leave
  • Electric car and bike salary sacrifice scheme
  • NHS pension scheme

PLEASE NOTE THAT WE ARE UNABLE TO PROVIDE VISA SPONSORSHIP

Job Summary

Triage and manage patients presenting with a wide range of womens health issues ensuring the highest standards of care. This would include women and adolescents with gynaecological problems, the menopause, contraception and breast disease.

The work would mainly be in one of our routine sites, but some sessions may be undertaken at our urgent care hub. This hub is well supported by a team of doctors, ECP and ANPs.

Depending on clinical need you would also be expected to manage some more generic primary care presentations in patients of any gender.

Be available to carry out all the duties reasonably expected of an NHS GP using the standards expected by the GMC, RCGP in line with appropriate national, local clinical guidelines

St Austell Healthcare has a strong multidisciplinary team comprising GPs, ANPs, Nurses, Paramedics and Pharmacists and an ethos for innovation and collaboration with health and social care partners.

We are an award winning, happy team and take pride in our work and the care we offer our 38,000 patients.

We are constantly seeking new ways of working to enhance service provision and the patient experience, introducing new technologies and methods of working to meet the expectations of our patient group. We are ambitious and wish to provide the best service we can for the people of St Austell and Mevagissey.

employer: East Kent Hospitals University NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in Intensive Care Medicine and Anaesthetics
descriptionHtml:
We are delighted to welcome applications for a Consultant in Critical Care and Anaesthesia to join the expanding East Kent Critical Care team at the Kent and Canterbury Hospital, East Kent Hospitals University Foundation Trust.If you join our expanding department, you'll discover a rewarding role with great scope for professional development, research and teaching, plus a fantastic lifestyle. Our Trust is investing heavily in our Critical Care Units over the next 12 months, and we would love you to be a part of this.

Why choose us? When you make the move to East Kent Hospitals University Foundation Trust, your only regret will be that you didn't do it sooner. Here, you can be confident of making a difference to our patients, our incredible healthcare teams and our dedicated medical students and doctors in training.

The Kent & Medway Medical School has recently opened in Canterbury. This is a game-changing opportunity and one which the two universities and Kent and Medway trusts have been working towards for several years. Successful applicants with an interest in medical education will be supported in taking up an honorary senior lecturer post at the medical school - subject to agreement by KMMS.

Your opportunity.....As a GMC registered Consultant, you'll play a vital role in a progressive and forward-thinking East Kent Critical Care team. East Kent Critical Care operates across three units: Kent and Canterbury Hospital (8 beds), Queen Elizabeth the Queen Mother Hospital, Margate (9 beds), and the William Harvey Hospital (24 beds). This post, including on-call commitments, is based at the Kent and Canterbury Hospital, although sessions on other sites are available if requested.Our Critical Care team boasts some exciting special interests across our three units. There's a strong focus on critical care ultrasonography, with state-of-the-art equipment supporting focused echocardiography and bedside ultrasonography. Our consultants include accredited CUSIC and FICE mentors, plus two FICE supervisors. We have high spec ultrasound equipment available on all units, and have recently successfully procured a brand-new state of the art echo machine as well as a cutting-edge echo and ultrasound training mannequin with training modules for transthoracic and transoesophageal echo as well as lung and abdominal ultrasound (including a COVID lung ultrasound module). We also have an interest in advanced ventilation modes such as APRV and Intellivent ASV, and run regular advanced ventilation workshops. Outreach and a Critical Care Rehabilitation service are well established, and we are well supported by a full complement of allied health professionals.

We are one of the largest hospital trusts in England, with three acute hospitals and community sites serving a local population of around 700,000.We also provide specialist services for Kent and Medway.

We're on an exciting journey of transformation. With a new Medical School at the centre of our community, a focus on research, clinical leadership and making our trust a rewarding and friendly place to work, there's never been a better time to join us.

We offer flexible and fulfilling career solutions that work for you and unique opportunities to innovate and inspire - all in a county where you can enjoy your life to the full, whatever your interest.

title: Locum ST4+ General and Geriatric Medicine
descriptionHtml:
We are looking to appoint three geriatric medicine registrars to work at ST4+ level in General and Geriatric Medicine from December 2026 until 2nd February 2027. These vacancies has arisen as a result of the need for maternity cover.

This is an excellent opportunity for a candidate keen to pursue a career in geriatric and general medicine. The posts are spread over a 28-bedded male elderly care ward (Mortimer), a specialist hip fracture unit (Emmer Green), and our surgical liaison service. There will be a commitment to the medicine on-call rota, including hospital at night shifts. There is an opportunity to review patients in the Rapid Access Clinic for the Older Person (RACOP), reviews of older and frail patients under the care of other specialties within the hospital, as well as contribute to the peri-admission reviews of hip fracture patients. The three teams work under the supervision of consultants, many of whom who rotate every 8 weeks. Typically, there are 2 consultants allocated to a team at any time. Mortimer and Emmer Green also have specialty doctors as well as IMT, GPVTS, and foundation programme trainees, and a Physician's Assistant. The surgical liaison post is supported by 2 Physician's Assistants.

The post holder will also be on call as medical registrar for the unselected medical take as per rota.

  • Attend Consultant and own ward rounds
  • Work alongside the Consultant to provide expertise to the frail older patients under the care of the hip fracture unit
  • Gather collateral history from patients and their families or GP
  • Work alongside the multidisciplinary team to help patients to achieve their rehabilitation goals
  • Attend and contribute to the 'best interest meetings' with families of patients with cognitive impairment to plan for future care
  • Review Elderly Care ward referrals from other specialties as per rota
  • Attend RACOP (Rapid Access Clinic for the Older Person) as per rota
  • Undertake responsibilities from the medicine on-call rota, including hospital at night responsibilities

If you have the necessary qualifications and attributes, come and shape the future of front line medical care at our hospital.The successful candidates will play a pivotal role in the management of acute medical patients, bringing leadership, expertise, and a holistic approach to patient care. This is an exciting opportunity to make a significant impact on patient outcomes and contribute to the continuous improvement of our services.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Deliver expert clinical care to acute and general medical patients, focusing on comprehensive and individualized treatment plans.
  • Lead and manage the acute and general medical areas, fostering a culture of empathy, respect, and excellence.
  • Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to develop and implement effective patient care plans.
  • Engage with patients and their families, ensuring clear communication and shared decision-making.

The Humber Health Partnership is one of the largest acute and community Partnership arrangements in the NHS, seeing well over one million patients every year and managing a budget of over £1.3 billion.

Made up of two Trusts - Northern Lincolnshire and Goole NHS Foundation Trust (NLAG) and Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust (HUTH) - our Partnership has significant ambitions and is committed to delivering world-class hospital and community services for the 1.65 million people we serve.
