title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
Aitune Medical Practice is a friendly, well established GP practice serving approximately 8,000 patients in the Long Eaton community. As a Veteran Friendly accredited practice and a proud member of the Erewash Health Partnership, we work collaboratively with GP practices across Ilkeston and Long Eaton to deliver high-quality, patient-centred care within a supportive team environment. We use the SystmOne clinical system alongside Rapid Health Triage to ensure efficient and effective patient care.

We currently have availability for 4 to 6 sessions per week. You will work alongside GP partners, salaried GPs and other colleagues providing full general practice healthcare to our 8000 patients, with a proportionate number (pro rata of sessions worked) of patients under your care to support continuity. Your week will be split into routine appointment sessions and duty appointment sessions. Your days will include a mixture of 10/15 minute F2F and telephone appointments and the number of patients you are expected to see F2F in a day is 25. Most of our home visits are undertaken by a visiting hub available to us, but you would be expected to occasionally visit patients at home as needed.

In accordance with the practice timetable, as agreed, the postholder will make themselves available to undertake a variety of duties, including surgery consultations, telephone consultations and queries, visiting patients at home, checking and signing repeat prescriptions and dealing with queries, paperwork and correspondence in a timely fashion.

Please see job description for more details.

Our practice team currently consists of 2 GP partners, 3 salaried GPs, 3 practice nurses, a HCA, a phlebotomist, a pharmacist, and an experienced administrative and management team. We are committed to continuous improvement and maintaining a positive work-life balance for our clinicians.

employer: Robert Jones and Agnes Hunt Orthopaedic Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Anaesthetist with special interest in Regional Anaesthesia
descriptionHtml:
This is an exciting opportunity for a Consultant Anaesthetist to join a specialist orthopaedic hospital providing high-quality anaesthetic and perioperative care across a broad range of services.

The successful applicant will have a special interest in regional anaesthesia and will be expected to support the delivery and development of high-quality regional anaesthetic techniques for orthopaedic surgery, including acute pain management and enhanced recovery pathways. Applicants should be able to demonstrate substantial experience in ultrasound-guided regional anaesthesia and perioperative care for patients undergoing major orthopaedic surgery.

Applications are particularly welcomed from candidates with experience in specialist orthopaedic practice, including paediatric orthopaedics and/or orthopaedic oncology. An additional interest in perioperative critical care would be highly valued.

Where candidates are otherwise closely matched, preference may be given to applicants who can demonstrate additional capability in perioperative critical care, paediatric orthopaedic anaesthesia, orthopaedic oncology anaesthesia, or development of specialist regional anaesthesia pathways relevant to the Trust's clinical services.

Consultant Anaesthetist Interviews including applications in this round will take place on 3rd December 2026.

This full time post comprise 8.5 PA for direct clinical care with 1.5 supporting professional activities (SPA) with the opportunity to progress to 2.5 for specific activities which are agreed upon between the consultant and their clinical manager.

We encourage all potential candidates to come to the site for an informal visit.

The On-Call commitment for the post is low frequency.

The Robert Jones and Agnes Hunt Orthopaedic NHS Trust (RJAH)is one of the leading orthopaedic hospitals in the country, with some of the highest levels of staff and patient satisfaction, as well as a strong reputation for research and innovation.

We have a range of fantastic staff benefits on offer to everyone who joins RJAH and you'll have access to outstanding professional development opportunities and state-of-the-art facilities - including our recently-opened £6 million Headley Court Veterans' Orthopaedic Centre (the first unit of its kind in the UK).RJAH has strong links with a range of universities including Staffordshire, Keele, Glyndwr, Chester and Birmingham.The hospital is located on a site outside Oswestry in Oswestry, just off the A5. The nearest train station is in Gobowen, approximately two miles from the hospital. The station is part of the Chester to Birmingham line.We are based in North Shropshire, close to the border with North and Mid Wales. It offers outstanding opportunities for anyone who enjoys an outdoor lifestyle or is looking to raise a family.

employer: Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Senior Fellow in Paed Critical Care and Retrieval Medicine
descriptionHtml:
OXFORD UNIVERSITY HOSPITAL NHS FOUNDATION TRUST

The Paediatric Critical Care (PCC) department at Oxford University Hospital (OUH), Oxford, UK, invites applications for Paediatric Critical Care and Retrieval Fellow posts.

One Clinical Fellow (ST5-ST8) posts in Paediatric Intensive Care and Paediatric Retrieval Medicine (Southampton Oxford retrieval team (SORT -Oxford))

Fixed Term for 12 months

This post would be suitable for an enthusiastic candidate from a Paediatric, Intensive Care, Adult Intensive Care, Anaesthetic, or Emergency Medicine background, interested in training in Paediatric Intensive Care in accordance with the standards of the Intercollegiate Training Committee in Paediatric Intensive Care Medicine (ICTPICM). The appointee will work full-time within Paediatric Critical Care (PCC) Services at the John Radcliffe Hospital in Oxford. The main responsibility would be to the PCC and SORT retrieval service. Duties would be undertaken within the Paediatric Intensive Care Unit, the High Dependency service, and the retrieval service.

This role is fixed term for 12 months with the first month spent on OUH PCC before rotating with SORT Oxford.

This post offers a structured training in Paediatric Critical Care and Retrieval Medicine. It is aimed at senior trainees in Paediatrics, Intensive Care Medicine, Anaesthetics, or Emergency Medicine who wish to improve their skills in the assessment, stabilisation, and management of the critically ill child.

Supervised practical instruction will be given in:

o Airway skills: Basic & Advanced

o Vascular access: Central venous & arterial

o CVP, Arterial, and Intracranial pressure access and interpretation

o Cerebral function analysis monitoring

o Ventilation - standard techniques, BIPAP pressure and volume controlled modes, pressure release ventilation, high frequency oscillation and Non-invasive techniques.

o Neuro intensive care

o Advanced renal support

o Application of Brain Death Criteria

o Talking to parents in critical situations

o Stabilisation and Transport of sick infants and children

Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is one of the largest NHS teaching trusts in the country. It provides a wide range of general and specialist clinical services and is a base for medical education, training and research. The Trust comprises four hospitals - the John Radcliffe Hospital, Churchill Hospital and Nuffield Orthopaedic Centre in Headington and the Horton General Hospital in Banbury.

Our values, standards and behaviours define the quality of clinical care we offer and the professional relationships we make with our patients, colleagues and the wider community.

We call this Delivering Compassionate Excellence, and its focus is on our values of compassion, respect, learning, delivery, improvement and excellence.

These values put patients at the heart of what we do and underpin the quality healthcare we would like for ourselves or a member of our family. Watch how we set out to deliver compassionate excellence via the OUH YouTube channel.

In 2023NHS England launched its first sexual safety charter, and our Trust proudly signed it. We pledge zero tolerance for inappropriate sexual behaviour and commit to the ten core principles

Oxford University Hospitals promotes a safe, respectful hiring environment.

If you want to make a difference with us, come and join our team. Together, we will uphold the highest standards of care and professionalism.

employer: James Paget University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Radiologist
descriptionHtml:
Job Overview

Join the Radiology Team at James Paget University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

An exciting opportunity has arisen for a motivated and forward-thinking Consultant Radiologist to join the Radiology Directorate at James Paget University Hospital NHS Foundation Trust. We are looking for an enthusiastic clinician who is committed to delivering high-quality patient care and helping to shape the future of imaging services within a modern and progressive NHS organisation.

You will work alongside a supportive team of Consultant Radiologists and multidisciplinary colleagues, providing a comprehensive range of diagnostic and interventional radiology services. The successful candidate will play a key role in maintaining excellent clinical standards, supporting service development, and contributing to innovative ways of delivering care for our local population.

As a teaching hospital, we are committed to education, training, research, and professional development. You will have opportunities to supervise and mentor junior doctors, radiographers, and other healthcare professionals while contributing to undergraduate and postgraduate medical education.

This is an excellent opportunity to join a friendly, collaborative department that values innovation, teamwork, clinical excellence, and continuous improvement.

As a Consultant Radiologist, you will share responsibility with colleagues for the delivery of a comprehensive and high-quality radiology service across the Trust. Your clinical duties will include reporting and specialist input across a range of modalities, which may include plain film radiography, ultrasound, CT, MRI, fluoroscopy and image-guided intervention.

The post holder will contribute to:

  • Emergency and acute imaging services.
  • Cancer and Faster Diagnostic Pathway services.
  • Urgent and routine outpatient imaging.
  • National screening programs ( Breast and Lung Cancer Screening) where appropriate.
  • Multidisciplinary Team (MDT) meetings across a range of specialties.
  • Service improvement and transformation projects within the department.

You will participate in the consultant on-call rota and provide cross-cover during annual, study, and professional leave. The role also involves providing expert radiological advice to clinical colleagues across the Trust and working closely within multidisciplinary teams to ensure the highest standards of patient care.

In addition, there will be opportunities to contribute to teaching, training, governance, audit, and departmental development

JPUH serves a population of approximately 250,000 people across Great Yarmouth, Lowestoft, and surrounding communities in Norfolk and Suffolk. Our vision is to provide excellent patient-centred care while fostering a culture where staff can thrive, develop, and reach their full potential.

Our busy and dynamic Radiology Department performs more than:

  • 70,000 X-rays annually
  • 50,000 CT and MRI scans annually
  • 30,000 ultrasound examinations annually

The Clinical Team currently comprises 15 Consultant Radiologists, reporting radiographers, sonographers and trainees rotating from Norwich Radiology Academy.

We are proud of our strong commitment to education and workforce development. We provide training for:

  • Specialist Registrars from NNUH
  • Medical students from the University of East Anglia Medical School.
  • Sonographers from the University of Hertfordshire.
  • Radiography students from the Universities of Suffolk and Exeter.
  • Practical mammography training for our radiography workforce.

Located on the beautiful Norfolk coast, the Trust offers an excellent work-life balance with easy access to stunning beaches, the Norfolk Broads, vibrant market towns, and affordable housing, making it an ideal place to build both your career and lifestyle.

You'll be joining a welcoming, ambitious organization where your expertise will be valued and where you can make a genuine difference to the lives of our patients and community.

descriptionHtml:
King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust is one of London's foremost teaching trusts, combining clinical excellence with a culture of innovation. We are seeking an outstanding Consultant Histopathologist to join our forward-thinking department at an exciting moment in its evolution.

Our recent transition to fully digital pathology reporting has transformed how we work -- offering flexibility, efficiency, and a platform for the future. You will manage a diverse, high-volume caseload with rich subspecialty exposure, supported by close MDT integration and digital infrastructure. Academic opportunities are available through our partnership with King's College London, with scope for research, audit, and teaching at all levels.

If you are a resourceful, ambitious histopathologist ready to embrace digital-first working and the opportunities of a truly multi-site trust, we would love to hear from you.

The Histopathology department at Denmark Hill undertakes histopathology (including frozen sections), diagnostic cytopathology (excluding cervical cytology) and autopsy pathology.

We are looking to recruit a locum consultant. This is a replacement post, timetabled for 8 PA per week, however there is scope to expand this to a full time (10 PA) role should the candidate prefer this. The post will require the post holder to play an active role in the general running of the department, with specialist interests in Gastrointestinal pathology, Cytopathology. If desired, autopsy work can be arranged by mutual consent with the Clinical Leads and local Coroner. The successful candidate will join an impressive team dedicated to providing a first-class patient-centred service.

Potential applicants will be welcome to visit the department and discuss this post.

You must be fully registered with the GMC and hold a Licence to Practice and be on the Specialist Register, or within six months of attaining your CCT or equivalent to be eligible for interview.

The Trust provides a full range of local and specialist services across its five sites. The trust-wide strategy of Strong Roots, Global Reach is our Vision to be BOLD, Brilliant people, Outstanding care, Leaders in Research, Innovation and Education, Diversity, Equality and Inclusion at the heart of everything we do. By being person-centred, digitally-enabled, and focused on sustainability, we aim to take Team King's to another level.

We are at a pivotal point in our history and we require individuals who are ready to join a highly professional team and make a real, lasting difference to our patients and our people.

King's is committed to delivering Sustainable Healthcare for All via our Green Plan. In line with national Greener NHS ambitions, we have set net zero carbon targets of 2040 for our NHS Carbon Footprint and 2045 for our NHS Carbon Footprint Plus. title: Consultant in Diabetes and Endocrinology
descriptionHtml:

title: General Practitioner - Primary Care Streaming
descriptionHtml:
Looking for a GP role that combines the variety of primary care with the pace and clinical challenge of an acute hospital environment? Primary Care 24 (PC24) is recruiting GPs to join our Primary Care Streaming Service within the Linda McCartney Centre at the Royal Liverpool University Hospital. You will be providing high-quality assessment and management for patients presenting to urgent and emergency care.

What will I be doing?

  • Provide high quality holistic clinical care, using skills and experience in accordance with the GMCs Good Medical Practice (2024), demonstrating care, compassion, dignity and respect
  • Make independent, professional decisions to address individual patient issues effectively
  • Evaluate and address the urgent healthcare needs of patients presenting with undiagnosed and undefined conditions.
  • Prescribe treatments appropriately, adhering to national guidance and the local formulary.
  • Making professional, autonomous decisions in relation to presenting problems..
  • Work as part of a multidisciplinary team to facilitate the safe and timely referral and/or admission of patients who require same day hospital care, following the principal that it is preferential to refer on to medical/surgical teams, whilst referral to ED should only occur if a medical/surgical referral is less appropriate.
  • Maintain accurate and contemporaneous electronic medical records with the PC24 clinical system.
  • Perform any other duties as agreed with the Medical Director, Clinical Lead or Head of Service to meet the needs of the service/organisation.

About us Primary Care 24 (PC24) is a not-for-profit social enterprise established in 2004, predominately delivering NHS contracts. The majority of our surplus is reinvested in patients and staff. We believe that primary healthcare should be accessible for everyone and are committed to delivering the best quality care we can, challenging social exclusion and working locally, where and when we can, to support our communities. We combine the best of the NHS with social enterprise innovation, developing solutions for NHS primary care and caring for our clinicians so that they can, in turn, care for our patients. Come join our proud team!

  • Ensure accurate and timely clinical documentation, including follow-up recommendations in line with Trust pathways.

Requirements:

  • GMC registration with Specialist Register accreditation in Dermatology.
  • Active Licence to Practise.
  • Proven experience working as a Consultant Dermatologist within the NHS.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to work autonomously and make sound clinical decisions.

18 Week Support is a leading NHS insourcing provider, working in partnership with NHS Trusts across the UK to increase clinical capacity, reduce waiting times and improve patient access to care.

Our clinical teams work alongside NHS services to deliver additional outpatient and surgical capacity, supported by experienced Clinical Leads and Nurse Leads. Patient safety, clinical governance and quality of care are central to everything we do.

title: Consultant Stroke Geriatrician
descriptionHtml:
This is a substantive post replacing a colleague who is retiring. The successful applicant will work as a stroke physician embedded within the elderly care department, which forms part of the London stroke model. The post will be based at Croydon University Hospital; other work locations including off site working may be agreed within the job plan where appropriate. In addition to weekend on-call commitments within elderly care, there is the option to hold an honorary contract with the HASU at St George's Hospital to be part of the on-call HASU rota. There is some flexibility around this, and it can be discussed as part of negotiations prior to contract signing.

You will enjoy a high level of autonomy and support from your team, and you will share your specialist expertise while provide a stroke consultation and advisory service to medical colleagues in other specialties in the Trust, potentially in other locations.

The job plan is anticipated to contain 10 programmed activities per week. We are prepared to negotiate any changes on the job plan for the benefit of clinical service delivery and the department as a whole.

Supported by a team of 2 stroke consultants and a multidisciplinary team, you will be responsible for TIA clinics, and support inpatient referrals, ward rounds and MDT under consultant supervision as per an internal rota.

As part of your professional development, you will participate in current and future research programmes as well as in service developments in line with national targets and locally commissioned improvements.

The stroke physician will be responsible for half of the stroke unit and provide prospective cover to their colleagues for leave. They will rotate to cover the TIA clinic and perform and advise on stroke reviews from referrals elsewhere in the hospital. In addition, the individual will be required to play an active role in the general workload of the department while having a significant commitment to teaching and training of junior staff.

Croydon Health Services provides integrated NHS services to care for people at home, in schools, and health clinics across the borough as well as at Croydon University Hospital and Purley War Memorial Hospital.

CUH provides more than 100 specialist services and is home to the borough's only Emergency Department and 24/7 maternity services, including a labour ward, midwifery-led birth centre and the Crocus home birthing team.

Purley War Memorial Hospital (PWMH) in the south of the borough offers outpatient care, including diagnostic services, physiotherapy and ophthalmology services run by Moorfields Eye Hospital, alongside an onsite GP surgery.

Our experienced district nursing teams, Allied Health Professionals and community matrons look after for people of all ages across Croydon and our Children's Hospital at Home cares for children with long-term conditions without them having to come to hospital.

We are a very close-knit and friendly organisation where every one of our 3600 members of staff is valued. We strongly believe that our employees are our greatest asset.

title: Portfolio General Practitioner
descriptionHtml:
South Coast Alliance (SCA) is seeking an enthusiastic and motivated Portfolio General Practitioner to join our team, working across services in Portsmouth and South East Hampshire.

This is an exciting opportunity for a GP looking to develop a varied and rewarding portfolio career, combining clinical practice with opportunities to contribute to leadership, education, quality improvement and service development.

The role offers four sessions per week, comprising three out-of-hours sessions and one in-hours session, providing experience across a range of primary and urgent care settings.

We are looking for a GP who is passionate about delivering high-quality, patient-centred care, enjoys working collaboratively and is keen to contribute to the ongoing development of our services.

At South Coast Alliance, we are committed to supporting professional development, innovation and a positive working environment, giving you the opportunity to develop your interests while making a meaningful difference to patient care.

The Portfolio GP will deliver high-quality, patient-centred care across South Coast Alliance services in Portsmouth and South East Hampshire, undertaking face-to-face, telephone and remote consultations.

The role involves assessing, diagnosing and managing a range of acute and urgent conditions, making appropriate referrals, prescribing safely and maintaining accurate clinical records.

Alongside clinical duties, the postholder will have opportunities to contribute to clinical leadership, education, quality improvement, service development and clinical governance, working collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams to improve patient care and service delivery.

South Coast Alliance (SCA) is a collaborative healthcare organisation delivering primary and urgent care services across Portsmouth and South East Hampshire.

We work in partnership with local healthcare providers to deliver safe, effective and high-quality patient care, supporting patients to access the right care, in the right place, at the right time.

Our services bring together experienced GPs, nurses, allied health professionals and operational teams, working collaboratively to meet the needs of our local communities.

At SCA, we are committed to continuous quality improvement, clinical excellence and workforce development. We encourage innovation, shared learning and professional development, creating a supportive environment where our staff can make a positive difference to patient care.

title: Salaried GP (Part Time)
descriptionHtml:
Chorley Together Primary Care Network are supporting Dr Dawoud's Surgery in their search for an enthusiatic and compassionate GP to join their team.

Please note the employer for this role is Dr Dawoud's surgery

Based in Clayton-Le-Woods Chorley, you will be part of their friendly, dynamic, forward thinking multi disciplinary team and will support them in their mission of deivering high quality care to its patients.

The role offered is 4 sessions per week on either a Monday and Thursday or a Tuesday and Friday and provides an excellent opprotunity for both new and experienced General Practitioners

Informal enquiries and practice visits are welcomed. For more information, please contact Janine Melia, Practice Manager. janine.melia1@nhs.net

Applications are via CV and covering letter, direct to the Practice Manager and not via NHS Jobs. Applications should be emailed to janine.melia1@nhs.net no later than 23:59 on 27 November 2026.

Please note this vacancy may close early if sufficient applications are received. You are therefore encouraged to apply as soon as possible.

The ideal candidate will be:

  • Caring and Compassionate
  • Dynamic and Creative
  • Team spirited and Flexible with a sense of humour
  • Keen to learn and share learning.
  • Willing to embrace new ways of working, innovation and quality improvement.

You will work as an autonomous practitioner, responsible for the provision of medical services to the practice population. You will deliver an excellent standard of clinical care whilst complying with the GMS contract and other contractual and regulatory obligations. The postholder will adhere to the GMS standards for good medical practice, leading by example, maintaining a positive and collaborative working relationship with the multidisciplinary team.

Dr Dawoud's Surgery is one of six practices across Chorley and Leyland that make up Chorley Together PCN. They are also a member of Chorley and South Ribble Primary Care Group, the local GP Federation, made up of 25 practices from across the Chorley and South Ribble area.

A teaching practice with a list size of approximately 3000 patients, they are located in the semi rural area of Clayton-Le-Woods. Located on the A6 the practice has good access to the M6, M61 and M65 motorways. On site parking is available.

The surgery consists of two GP Partners, a salaried GP, an in house pharmacist and two practice nurses, supported by a friendly admin and reception team.

Their practice values are Collaboration / Compassion / Learning

title: Consultant Audiological Physician
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking a Consultant Audiovestibular Physician to join our established Audiology and ENT service within Hywel Dda University Health Board. This is an opportunity to work collaboratively with clinical, medical, professional and managerial colleagues to provide high-quality, patient-centred care whilst contributing to the ongoing development of Audiovestibular Medicine services across the Health Board.

The successful candidate will be responsible for the assessment, diagnosis and management of paediatric and adult patients with hearing and balance disorders, including infants identified through the Newborn Hearing Screening Programme, children with permanent hearing impairment requiring diagnostic evaluation, and adults presenting with tinnitus, progressive hearing loss, vertigo, balance disorders and unexplained audiological symptoms. Working closely with colleagues across ENT, Paediatrics, Audiology, Therapy Services, Primary Care and wider multidisciplinary teams, you will play a key role in delivering safe, effective and coordinated care.

  • Deliver a comprehensive Audiovestibular Medicine service for paediatric and adult patients across Hywel Dda University Health Board, providing specialist assessment, diagnosis and management of hearing and balance disorders.
  • Assess and manage infants identified through the Newborn Hearing Screening Programme, children with permanent hearing impairment requiring diagnostic evaluation, and adults presenting with tinnitus, progressive hearing loss, unexplained audiological symptoms, vertigo, balance disorders and falls.
  • Provide clinical leadership in the development and enhancement of Audiovestibular Medicine services within the wider ENT framework, supporting service innovation, pathway development and the delivery of high-quality, patient-centred care.
  • Work collaboratively with clinical, medical, professional and managerial colleagues, leading and participating fully within multidisciplinary teams across ENT, Paediatrics, Audiology, Therapy Services, Primary Care and community services.
  • Provide specialist advice and leadership in the management of complex audiological and vestibular cases, supporting coordinated care across all Health Board sites and participating in domiciliary consultations where required.

Hywel Dda University Health Board plans and provides NHS healthcare services for people living in Carmarthenshire, Ceredigion, Pembrokeshire, and bordering counties.

We have over 13,000 staff and together we provide primary, community, in-hospital, mental health and learning disabilities services.

We work in partnership with the three local authorities, as well as public, private and third sector colleagues, including our valued team of volunteers.

Our services are provided in:

  • Four main hospitals: Bronglais Hospital in Aberystwyth; Glangwili Hospital in Carmarthen; Prince Philip Hospital in Llanelli; and Withybush Hospital in Haverfordwest
  • Five community hospitals: Amman Valley and Llandovery hospitals in Carmarthenshire; Tregaron Hospital in Ceredigion; and Tenby and South Pembrokeshire hospitals in Pembrokeshire
  • Two integrated care centres: Aberaeron and Cardigan in Ceredigion, and several other community settings
  • 47 general practices (six of which are health board managed practices); dental practices (including four orthodontic); 97 community pharmacies; 43 general ophthalmic practices; and 8 ophthalmic domiciliary providers
  • Numerous mental health and learning disabilities services

title: Consultant Psychiatrist, Adult Inpatients *enhanced recruitment premia
descriptionHtml:
Consultant Psychiatrist (General Adult Inpatients) - Blackpool (10 PA)

*RRP payment Payable*

This post will attract a Recruitment & Retention Premia of £40k (subject to tax and NI) payable on commencement of employment.

Eligibility criteria do apply. Please note that staff currently employed by the Trust would not be eligible to apply for this recruitment and retention premia.

We are excited to advertise for 2 x General Adult Consultant to join us working in inpatients at The Harbour, Blackpool. The post is substantive and full time (10 PAs).

You will be expected to participate on the Consultant On Call rota, for which additional remuneration is payable.

Post 1; 18 bedded male acute ward (Churchill)

Post 2; 18 bedded female acute ward (Stevenson)

Both posts have SAS Doctors and Resident Doctors established.

Flexible Job Plan option

We're really keen to 'think outside the box' and support interested applicants who may be considering a part time or job share option for this post.

Please don't hesitate to get in touch with us to discuss further, if you're looking to work less than full time.

The Harbour MH hospital is a state of the art unit based just off junction 4 on the M55. The M55 connects with the M6 and tends to be a really quiet connecting motorway, with rarely any delays. The Harbour is 2 mins from Junction 4 off the M55.

The post holder will be a leading member of the well-established, in-patient, multidisciplinary teams based at the Harbour and will have the following important clinical responsibilities:

o Responsible Clinician for a defined caseload.o Assessment of patients referred by the community teams and responsibility for any of admissions at the Harbour Hospital.o Out of Hours Cover.

Applicants should hold full GMC registration and be included on the Specialist register of the GMC or they should be eligible for entry to the Specialist Register within 6 months of the interview date.It is a requirement that applicants are Section 12 Approved at the time of commencing employment and have or are eligible to have Approved Clinician Status. The role:

o At least 2.5 SPAs as standard for a full time post (we would be flexible in looking at enhancements to support other activities that support the wider ambitions of the Trust).o Excellent peer support groupo Study leave budget of £3000 over 3 years or up to £5000 over 3 years for newly qualified Consultantso Opportunities to be a clinical supervisoro £8k Relocation package available should you need to move for the jobo £40k (gross) premia payable on commencement

At our Trust, we're really keen to develop our Consultant workforce and nurture their areas of interest in a flexible way where possible. Come and have a chat with us about what your special interest or development area and build a suitable job plan with us. We also have an extremely active Medical Education department and support our Consultants in becoming Clinical & Educational Supervisors and nurturing their interests in this area. There are also opportunities to have a role in Digital Leadership if this is a passion for any of our Consultants.

title: PCN Pharmacy Technician
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking to recruit a Pharmacy Technician on a full-time (37.5 hours per week), Permanent basis - part-time considered.

The focus of the post holders work will depend on the qualifications, skills and experience of the individual and the needs of the PCN, both of which may develop over time.

The post holder will: Support the role of PCN Clinical Pharmacists in the delivery of clinical pharmacy services Provide technical and administrative support to the clinicians within the PCN.

Clinical Undertake patient facing and patient supporting roles to ensure effective medicines use, through shared decision-making conversations with patients. Carry out medicines optimisation tasks including effective medicine administration (e.g., checking inhaler technique), supporting medication reviews and medicines reconciliation. Where required, utilise consultation skills to work in partnership with patients to ensure they use their medicines effectively. As determined by the PCN, support medication reviews and medicines reconciliation for new care home patients and synchronising medicines for patient transfers between care settings, linking with local community pharmacies Support the clinical pharmacists in providing medication reviews, developing further standard operating procedures, patient information and information about medicine awareness. Provide expertise to address both the public health and social care needs of patients, including lifestyle advice, service information, and help in tackling local health inequalities. Liaise with clinicians and admin staff to resolve prescribing queries To respond to medication queries from patients and staff in a professional manner referring to the GP/clinical pharmacist when appropriate. To provide advice to GPs, staff and patients in changes to prescribing to support the improvement of prescribing safety, quality and cost effectiveness Assist with medication safety monitoring systems (eg high risk drugs)

Join an award-winning organisation. title: Consultant - Palliative Care
descriptionHtml:
The successful candidate will be expected to work as part of North Tees and Hartlepool (NTUH) fully integrated Palliative Care team across hospital community and hospice settings as required. This post will involve a minimum of 1.5 sessions per week of regular hospice clinical work. This maybe in either one of two local hospices: Alice House Hospice in Hartlepool or Butterwick Hospice in Stockton (9 and 8 bedded adult inpatient units respectively).

Hospital and community clinical work will involve face to face and non-face to face patient reviews, as well as advising and supporting the palliative care team and wider healthcare teams with clinical management of patients.

On call duties are in the mainstay non-resident, taking advice calls from hospital, community and hospice settings, as part of University Hospital Tees (UHT) wide consultant rota. There is an expectation that consultants will attend to review patients face to face in a hospice setting out of hours if required to support a doctor in training in exceptional circumstances. Consultants on call are expected to be within 2 hours travel time from the hospices covered on call (located in Middlesbrough, Hartlepool and Stockton).

The successful candidatewill be welcomed to join our dynamic integrated palliative care service at North Tees and Hartlepool (NTH) providing input into community, hospital and hospice settings.

Base and clinical settings primarily based with the North Tees and Hartlepool integrated palliative care team at the University Hospital of North Tees.

  • Expected to work flexibly across hospital, community and hospice settings according to clinical need.
  • A minimum average of 1.5 sessions per week in a hospice is an essential requirement of the post.
  • Regular hospice work will be undertaken at either Butterwick Hospice, Stockton or Alice House Hospice, Hartlepool.
  • Butterwick Hospice is immediately adjacent to the University Hospital of North Tees. Alice House Hospice is located a 25-minute drive away in Hartlepool and includes a satellite office for the hospital and community team within.

Consultant team

The appointee joins a wider group of 10 Palliative Medicine consultants across University Hospitals Tees (a geographical area that covers: North Tees and Hartepool; Middlesbrough, Redcar and Cleveland; and Hambleton and Richmondshire).

North Tees and Hartlepool NHS Foundation Trust and South Tees Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust have come together to form University Hospitals Tees. As a result, post holders may be required to work across sites within both organisations.

At UHT our main priority is, and always will be, to provide safe and high quality care to our patients every day; the kind of care we would want for ourselves and our loved ones. We want our organisation to be the best place to work with the right staff, in the right roles, at the right time, to ensure we deliver exceptional patient care and experience.

We will support staff through providing an inclusive and supportive workplace with health and well-being initiatives, staff benefits and opportunities for personal and professional development. Staff recognition is very important to us; as well as performance reviews and appraisals, we recognise staff through Star and Team of the month, colleague recognition - a note of thanks, Managers awards, Shining Stars and Service Awards.

title: Support Worker
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a confident Care & Support Worker with a passion for delivering outstanding healthcare.

You'll be working full time 42 hours a week, 12 hour shifts, including alternate weekends (4 shifts week one, three shifts week two, on a two week rolling rota), days only, making a positive difference to the lives of the people in our care at Dene Brook.

Dene Brook is a specialist residential service in Rotherham, South Yorkshire, supporting people with learning disabilities, complex needs, autism and behaviours that may challenge.

We encourage and enable the people we support to lead a full and happy life. We work with them to ensure they have more choice and control in their lives. We find out their strengths, abilities and preferences so that the care provided can be as person-centred and meaningful to each individual.

At Cygnet, our perks go way beyond pension schemes and excellent professional development - you'll also enjoy discounts with our free NHS blue light card, perkbox with vouchers for everyday purchases and shopping, private health cash plans, free confidential mental health support and much more, to support your wellbeing in and out of work.

An unpaid carer? We recognise that many of our colleagues have unpaid caring responsibilities and we welcome applications from unpaid carers. We value the skills and experience that caring can bring to the workplace.

Your day-to-day...

  • Offer enhanced care with a flexible learning approach for all the people in our care
  • Provide guidance & encouragement through physical & emotional support
  • Learn about individuals specific needs & provide help in the most appropriate way

  • Maintain a safe, clean environment for all

Cygnet has been providing a national network of high-quality specialist mental health services for more than 30 years. In this role you'll have the chance to make a real impact on patients, service users & their families.

title: Salaried GP - Coleford Health Centre part of Dean Medical
descriptionHtml:

title: Consultant in Diabetes and Endocrinology
descriptionHtml:
An exciting and rare opportunity for a Consultant has arisen within the Diabetes & Endocrinology Directorate

This post is at the heart of an extensive experienced MDT within the Directorate of Diabetes and Endocrinology. The directorate provides both inpatient and outpatient care for patients with a wide range of complex Diabetes and Endocrine conditions.

The post holder will work 10 programmed activities for East Lancashire Hospitals NHS Trust. The job plan works on a 6 week cycle. Weeks 1 and 2 are wards and clinic and then weeks 3 to 6 are clinics only. There is a commitment to the emergency duties rota for general (internal) medicine including out of hours on call on a 1:21 rota.The department of Diabetes and Endocrinology provides a comprehensive service including a range of diabetes sub-specialty services on the two main hospital sites, two community hospital sites, and a number of other community sites. The service is supported by a team of 12 Diabetes Specialist Nurses along with Diabetes Specialist Dieticians and Podiatrists as well as a Diabetes Specialist Midwife. There is also a very active Clinical Trials Department supported by research nurses, admin and a medical team. Having been successful in our bid for national funding we are working to further expand the diabetes inpatient nursing and podiatry teams as well as increasing patient education in the community.Subsequent to a vision to improve clinical leadership and access to Consultant and Diabetes Specialist Nurse led services across the East Lancashire Health Economy we are developing a fully integrated diabetes service. The philosophy of the department is the prompt and effective implementation of evidence and national guidance into practice. The department is also recognised for its strength in clinical trials activities.

Established in 2003 ELHT is a large integrated health care organisation providing high quality acute secondary healthcare to the people of East Lancashire and Blackburn with Darwen.

Our vision is to be widely recognized for providing safe, personal and effective care. We currently provide high quality services and treat over 700,000 patients a year from the most serious of emergencies to planned operations and procedures. We employ over 8,000 staff.

This post is subject to the New Consultant Contract 2003.

The Trust will reimburse certain expenses relating to removal and relocation when required the expenses refunded shall reflect the actual costs but will not exceed £8,000.

Satisfactory medical examination is a condition of employment for Medical and Dental NHS staff.

Candidates should note that any person appointed to this post will be referred to the DBS for clearance.

title: Salaried GP (maternity cover)
descriptionHtml:

title: Specialist Practitioner
descriptionHtml:
As a Specialist Practitioner within the PHL ADHD Service, the post 
holder will play a central role in delivering a high-quality, patient
focused care pathway. Working as an autonomous professional, the 
role involves engaging with adults aged 18+ to undertake assessment 
and diagnosis, initiate and manage pharmacological treatment, and 
carry out ongoing reviews.* Conduct remote ADHD assessments for adults, using referral information and screening tools
* Initiate and titrate ADHD medication in line with national and local guidelines
* Complete holistic reviews to monitor patient progress and treatment outcomes
* Provide specialist advice and support to empower patients in managing their condition
* Collaborate with Primary Care teams through Shared Care agreements
* Engage with partner organisations to ensure continuity of care
* Contribute to service development, clinical governance, and quality improvement
PHL has been delivering an adult ADHD service since December 2020, expanding in April 2024 to provide the NHS Hampshire Adult ADHD Service alongside support for the Isle of Wight service.

The service provides comprehensive support across the ADHD care pathway for adults, including individuals seeking diagnosis and those already diagnosed, with or without medication. This includes transition reviews for young adults moving from child to adult services.

The pathway may include screening, triage, assessment, follow-up, medication initiation and titration, transition support, and annual reviews.

Delivery is primarily via virtual consultations (video and telephone), with face-to-face appointments available when required. The service is supported by an administrative team and Medical Secretary based in the Segensworth office.

title: Senior Care Assistant
descriptionHtml: As a Senior Care Assistant at HC One, Kindness will be at the core of everything you do. It touches upon every aspect of our Dementia, Nursing, Residential and Specialist care homes. Every single person who works here understands that our residents are people just like them with their own stories to tell. And, by joining us, youll have a wonderful opportunity to give something back to those people.For you, that will mean planning and implementing the kind of care that will give our residents a real sense of security, dignity and independence. You will get to know our residents and their families  helping to ensure we deliver truly personalised care plans. Leading a team of Care Assistants, you will be responsible for maintaining the highest standards of care and youll be a real influence on the rest of the team. Whether you are showing someone how to use a walking frame, helping someone at the end of their life to eat a meal or talking to a residents family on the phone, youll do so with a sense of kindness, above anything else. Assisting the Registered Nurse and Care Manager, you will be involved in providing essential physical and mental stimulation through a range of social and recreational activities, as well as administering medication.At HC-One, our purpose is to support those in our care to lead their best lives. As the Kind Care Company, it is our mission to provide the kindest support and care to Residents living in our care homes, as we strive to be the first-choice care provider for Families, our Colleagues and Commissioners in each of the communities that we serve.

employer: Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in Respiratory Medicine
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for a full time Consultant Respiratory Physician to join the Complex Home Ventilation and Specialist Weaning Service at Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust, primarily based at Royal Brompton Hospital.The successful candidate will join one of the largest and most established specialist ventilation services internationally, providing care to more than 3,000 patients receiving home ventilation, including over 100 patients requiring long term tracheostomy ventilation.The service also provides specialist assessment and management for patients requiring prolonged mechanical ventilation and complex ventilator weaning. This regional service receives over 100 referrals annually and operates through the Lane Fox Unit at St Thomas' Hospital, the Remeo Units and a specialist outreach service based at Royal Brompton Hospital.The post holder will work alongside an experienced multidisciplinary team of respiratory consultants, specialist nurses, physiotherapists, pharmacists, clinical psychologists and speech and language therapists.Applicants are expected to have specialist experience in home ventilation and ventilator weaning, alongside a commitment to clinical excellence, research, education and service development.

Please note that we will be closing the advert after the maximum number of applications have been received, so please apply as early as possible if interested.

The post holder will provide specialist consultant respiratory care within the Complex Home Ventilation and Specialist Weaning Service, primarily based at Royal Brompton Hospital, working collaboratively with colleagues across Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust.

Key responsibilities include:

Providing specialist assessment, treatment and ongoing management of patients requiring home ventilation and prolonged mechanical ventilation.

Supporting the assessment and management of patients referred for specialist ventilator weaning across inpatient and outreach services.Working closely with the multidisciplinary team to deliver safe, effective and individualised patient care.

Contributing to the development of clinical pathways and improvements in service delivery.

Participating in clinical governance, audit, quality improvement and service development.

Supporting clinical research, including recruitment to appropriate clinical trials.

Contributing to medical education, teaching and clinical supervision.Participating in departmental management, service planning and appropriate on call commitments.

The post holder will demonstrate effective clinical leadership and a commitment to high quality patient care.

Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust is one of the UK's largest NHS foundation trusts, providing specialist, hospital and community services.

The Trust comprises five hospitals: Guy's, St Thomas', Evelina London Children's Hospital, Royal Brompton and Harefield, alongside community services in Lambeth and Southwark.

With approximately 22,700 staff, the Trust is recognised for clinical excellence, research, innovation and education. As part of King's Health Partners, we work closely with academic and clinical partners to improve patient care through research and innovation.

The Royal Brompton Lung Directorate provides nationally and internationally recognised specialist respiratory services, including complex home ventilation and specialist weaning.

Our organisational values guide everything we do:

Caring: We put patients first.Ambitious: We innovate and strive for excellence.Inclusive: We respect each other and work collaboratively.

We are committed to providing an inclusive working environment, supporting staff development and delivering high quality patient care.

employer: Barking, Havering and Redbridge University Hospitals NHS Trust
title: Upper Limb Specialty Doctor in Trauma & Orthopaedics
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for the post of an Upper Limb Senior Specialty Doctor (middle grade) for Trauma and Orthopaedics (T&O) department.This is not a registrar post. This is a senior position for independent upper limb surgery. Please DO NOT apply if you are not proficient in running elective upper limb clinics and theatres independently. This is initially a one-year fixed term post, but extendable thereafter for the right candidate. We expect the candidate to be able to perform hand procedures (carpal tunnel, triggers, Dupuytren's, Trapeziectomy etc) and also basic shoulder procedures including arthroscopy procedures (eg subacromial decompression, capsular release etc) independently. The successful candidate will beindependently managing patient carein outpatient clinics, fracture clinics, virtual fracture clinics, triaging and running elective upper limb and trauma theatres. There will also be opportunities to teach and support more junior staff in the department.We are seeking a dynamic and proactive candidate, with elective upper limb experience, who would be able to make independent decisions in elective upper limb clinics, run elective upper limb theatres, and weekend general trauma lists (1:8). There will be consultant support and potential to do more complex elective upper limb cases jointly with consultants.

The main duties of the applicant include managing and treating T&O patients independently and under consultant supervision, leading and supporting other junior doctors. They will be expected to work as a part of a team and provide support to all staff within the team. TheOrthopaedicDepartment hascentralisedall Trauma Services at Queens Hospital in Romford, with Inpatient Elective activity being undertaken at King Georges Hospital inGoodmayes, with hospital-provided transportation available between sites.We are currently working with our external partners to ensure a streamlined pathway from referral to treatment thus ensuring achievement of the 18-week RTT target.We have a fully-fledged 'virtual fracture clinic' service since December 2019 to enable a more robust triage service and reducing the amount of unnecessary face-to-face appointments in fracture clinics, that patients are asked to attend following their A&E/UCC attendance. This is coupled with a more intuitive system of referring patients directly to the correct sub-specialty clinic for further treatment under the most relevant consultant.

We're an organisation that is getting better and better and our improvements are driven by a determination to deliver care we're proud of and our patients are happy with.

They are benefitting from a new electronic patient record (we were the last acute trust in London to introduce one) and our maternity services have been rated good by the Care Quality Commission.

We operate from two main sites - KGH in Goodmayes and Queen's Hospital in Romford. We have two busy emergency departments with more than 346,000 people visiting them last year. We're campaigning to secure the £35m we need to transform the A&E at Queen's and get rid of corridor care.

We're proud of our regional Neurosciences Centre, Radiotherapy Centre and Hyper Acute Stroke Unit. We're also part of the North East London Cancer Alliance.

We run a Women's Health Hub in Ilford; an Ageing Well Centre in Hornchurch; and Community Diagnostic Centres (CDC) at Barking Community Hospital and at St George's Health and Wellbeing Hub. These CDCs are open 12 hours a day, 7 days a week.

The majority of our 8,400 staff - who come from 146 different countries - live in the three diverse London boroughs we serve and are from black, Asian and minority ethnic groups. Many can work flexibly and more than 400 of them are on our Ofsted accredited apprenticeship programmes. We're proud to be a London Living Wage employer.

title: Salaried GP - GP Reimbursement Scheme
descriptionHtml:
We are delighted to offer an opportunity for a Salaried GP to join our friendly and supportive team at St Hilary Group Practice under the 2026/27 GP Reimbursement Scheme.

We are looking to recruit a GP for 4 sessions per week, ideally working Monday, Tuesday afternoon and Thursday afternoon. There may be some flexibility in the working pattern for the right candidate.

The post is offered on an initial 6 month fixed-term contract , with the potential for extension beyond this date, subject to practice requirements and funding arrangements.

We are offering a salary in line with the BMA salaried GP pay range, NHS Pension Scheme membership and 6 weeks annual leave with bank holidays (pro rata).

In accordance with the agreed practice rota, the post holder will undertake the usual duties associated with the role of a Salaried GP, including

Face to face and telephone consultations

Assessment, diagnosis and management of acute and chronic conditions

Prescribing in accordance with local and national guidance

Effective management of long term conditions

Reviewing and acting upon investigation results and clinical correspondence

Processing referrals, prescriptions and associated clinical administration in a timely manner

Maintaining accurate and contemporaneous clinical records

Providing continuity of care where appropriate

Working collaboratively with the wider practice and multidisciplinary team

Participating in practice clinical meetings, audit and quality improvement

Undertaking occasional home visits where clinically required, although the majority are carried out by the PCN Acute Home Visiting Service

The post holder will be expected to work collaboratively with colleagues and contribute fairly to the clinical workload of the practice.

St Hilary Group Practice is a friendly and supportive PMS training and teaching practice in Wallasey, serving a patient population of just under 6,000.

Education and training are an important part of practice life. We regularly support GP Registrars and Foundation Doctors, as well as welcoming third-year medical students from the Universities of Liverpool and Chester for placements within the practice.

Our clinical team includes GP Partners, a Salaried GP, Practice Nurses, HCAs and a range of clinicians working with us through our Primary Care Network, including pharmacists, paramedics and other additional roles.

We are a proactive member of North Coast Alliance SDU (Wallasey PCN) and work closely with our PCN colleagues to develop and deliver services for our local patient population. This collaborative approach provides access to a wider multidisciplinary team and additional services.

We use EMIS Web as our clinical system and PATCHS to support our total triage model.

Our appointment system is designed to ensure that GP appointment requests are clinically triaged and directed to the most appropriate clinician or service. Triage is undertaken by a dedicated triage GP, supported by our reception team.

We are proud of our strong QOF performance and CQC "Good" rating. We have an experienced and supportive management and administrative team.

title: ICU Consultant
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for enthusiastic colleagues to join the critical care team at Imperial College Healthcare.

You will be working as part of the wider critical care directorate at Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust, which provides 94 Adult ICU beds across three hospitals. All units were rated "Good" by the CQC in 2019, and achieved very positive feedback in peer reviews in 2023.

Each unit admits both elective and emergency Level 2 and 3 patients, but has a distinct character. St Mary's is a quaternary vascular centre and Major Trauma Centre, Charing Cross is a regional stroke and neurosurgical centre, and Hammersmith is a regional centre for cardiac, renal and haematology. As a result, we care for a hugely varied clinical case mix and are pioneers in multi-disciplinary and collaborative care.

As one of the largest acute teaching Trusts in the UK, we offer a wide range of opportunities to help you achieve the career you aspire to. Academic clinicians are welcome and will be encouraged to become local principal investigators for multicentre studies in collaboration with our internationally acclaimed academic department led by Prof A Gordon.

This will be a split-site post, working across St Mary's and Charing Cross Hospitals.

The posts will attract 10PAs including a minimum of 2SPAs, but we also welcome applications from individuals who wish to work less than full time. Our philosophy is to formulate an individualised job plan with successful candidates, with an emphasis on enabling professional development and pursuit of specific interests. We strongly believe that the job plan needs to be sustainable and should enable the successful candidate to maintain a good work-life balance.

Main duties contained within the job plan are assessing and managing critically unwell patients as part of the ICU MDT team. This will involve twice daily ward rounds as a minimum with targeted assessment and interventions as required. Outreach duties are also contained within the job plans and there are outreach clinics which can be job planned for interested candidates. SPA duties will vary but all consultants are expected to support and supervise trainees.

All appointments are to the Trust, but this post will be based across our St Mary's and Charing Cross sites. There may also be opportunities for consultants to move sites during their career if they wish to, in order to gain new clinical or leadership experience.

At Imperial College Healthcare you can achieve extraordinary things with extraordinary people, working with leading clinicians pushing boundaries in patient care.

Become part of a vibrant team living our values - expert, kind, collaborative and aspirational. You'll get an experience like no other and will fast forward your career.

Benefits include career development, flexible working and wellbeing, staff recognition scheme. Make use of optional benefits including Cycle to Work, car lease schemes, season ticket loan or membership options for onsite leisure facilities.

We are committed to equal opportunities and improving the working lives of our staff and will consider applications to work flexibly,part time or job share. Please talk tous at interview.

employer: Cambridgeshire and Peterborough NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Psychiatrist in Old Age CRHTT
descriptionHtml:
Main Duties of The Consultant PostConsultant Psychiatrists are a valuable and finite resource within our clinical services and whilst the primary responsibility for every consultant is the delivery of a high-quality clinical service all consultants will be expected to be actively involved in the strategic development of the service and work with their non-medical senior leaders to steer the development of their service in line with the strategic direction of the organisation.

We are committed to ensuring all our Consultant Psychiatrists are effective and compassionate clinical leaders. Clinical leadership, innovation and service performance are key components to all our consultant positions. We will provide the necessary training and development opportunities for all Consultants joining the Trust to ensure they are able to deliver these components of their role.

The PostThe Peterborough team covers both the Older Adults Crisis Resolution and Home Treatment Team (CHRTT-OP) and the Dementia Intensive Support Service (DIST). It forms part of Cambridgeshire and Peterborough NHS Foundation Trust's (CPFT) Older People's Mental Health Services and is based at The Cavell Centre. The service provides specialist, multidisciplinary assessment and intensive support for older adults, including people living with dementia, who are experiencing an acute mental health crisis, complex mental health needs or a deterioration in their wellbeing. The team works closely with service users, families, carers and partner agencies to provide timely, coordinated care that supports people to remain safely at home wherever possible and helps reduce the need for hospital admission.

The focus of the service is to meet the needs of service users who are experiencing an acute mental health crisis. All interventions provided by the service are short term and focused on the safety, wellbeing and empowerment of the service user and their carers and family during the period of the crisis.

CPFT is a health & social care organisation dedicated to providing high quality care with compassion to improve the health & wellbeing of the people we care for, as well as supporting & empowering them to lead a fulfilling life.

Our clinical teams deliver many NHS services not only via inpatient and primary care setting but also with the community. These services include Children, Adult & Older Peoples mental health, Forensic & Specialist mental health, Learning Disabilities, Primary Care & Liaison psychiatry, Substance misuse, Social care, Research & Development.

To achieve our goal, we look to recruit high calibre candidates that share our vision & values. As an equal opportunities employer, we encourage applications from all sectors of the community, particularly from under-represented groups including disabled people & members of our BAME & LGBTQ+ communities.

For further information on CPFT please visit our website www.cpft.nhs.uk

employer: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Anaesthetist - HGS sites
descriptionHtml:
We are excited to invite applications for a Consultant in Anaesthesia within University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust (UHB).

The current opportunity is for consultants to join the dedicated Anaesthetics team based at Birmingham Heartlands, Good Hope and Solihull hospitals.

We are looking to appoint consultants with an interest in Vascular, Regional, peadiatric and colorectal anaesthesia and perioperative medicine. They will be expected to join the general on-call at Heartlands Hospital or the General and obstetric on call at Good Hope Hospital as part of the on-call commitment. The appointee will be expected to participate in the Divisional and Departmental quality improvement projects as well as undergraduate and postgraduate teaching.

We are more than happy to arrange a call, or an informal visit, should you wish to discuss further. Please contact Clinical Service Lead for Anaesthetics Dr Saravanababu Gnanaseakaran - via email to saravanababu.gnanaseakaran@uhb.nhs.uk or to Mr Daniel Evans General Manager - daniel.evans@uhb.nhs.uk

The core component of this post is to provide anaesthetic cover for a variety of surgical services, if a consultant has a special interest in a sub speciality, then we will try to accommodate it.

A standard full time job plan will contain 10 programmed activities which could be filled by a variety of options from currently uncovered lists and flexible cover for consultant leave. Solihull Hub has extended lists running from 07:00 hrs to 19:00 hrs and employed consultants will be expected to take up some of these lists.

A programmed activity will normally have a timetable value of 4 hours, and a full-time consultant will normally devote 8.5 programmed activities to direct clinical care. The remaining programmed activities will be devoted to supporting professional activities.

An example 10 PA job plan is indicated in Appendix 1, but the successful candidate will be invited to discuss these options with the Clinical Service Lead on appointment.

University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust strives to have an inclusive culture where everyone feels like they belong, can thrive, knows that they add value and feels valued. We do this by developing compassionate and culturally competent leaders, being values driven in all that we do and by creating a welcoming and inclusive workplace that thrives on the diversity of our people. As such we want to attract and recruit talented individuals from all backgrounds, and for each of you to feel supported for the diversity you bring, to achieve your full potential. For those staff with a disability, including physical disability, long term health condition, mental health or neurodiverse condition, this also means being committed to making reasonable adjustments needed for you to carry out your role.

employer: Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust
title: Consultant in Stroke Medicine
descriptionHtml:
Join Our Visionary Stroke Team - Consultant Opportunity

Location: Humber Health Partnership (HUTH site based)Specialty: Stroke MedicineContract: Full-time | 10 PAs (8 DCC + 2 SPA)On-call: Flexible, remote access-enabled, with compensatory time off

Shape the Future of Stroke Care

Are you a dynamic and forward-thinking clinician ready to make a real impact? The Humber Health Partnership is seeking Consultant Stroke Physicians to join our expanding, innovative stroke service. This is your chance to be part of a high-performing team delivering cutting-edge hyperacute stroke care across one of the largest NHS partnerships in the country.

What You'll Do

Lead the assessment and management of stroke patients across the care pathway

Participate in hyperacute stroke treatments including:ThrombolysisMechanical thrombectomyIntracerebral haemorrhage management

Contribute to clinical trials and research, including hyperacute stroke studies

Provide on-call support with flexible, mostly remote coverage via telemedicine

Supervise and mentor junior doctors and medical students

Academic & Leadership Opportunities

Teach within the Hull York Medical School (HYMS) curriculum

Supervise trainees from FY1 to specialty registrar level

Take on a management or educational leadership role with full training and support

Additional SPA time available for research, education, or service development

The Humber Health Partnership is one of the largest acute and community Partnership arrangements in the NHS, seeing well over one million patients every year and managing a budget of over £1.3 billion.

Made up of two Trusts - Northern Lincolnshire and Goole NHS Foundation Trust (NLAG) and Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust (HUTH) - our Partnership has significant ambitions and is committed to delivering world-class hospital and community services for the 1.65 million people we serve.

Together we employ nearly 20,000 staff. Our five main hospital sites are Diana, Princess of Wales Hospital, Scunthorpe General Hospital and Goole and District Hospital, for NLAG and Hull Royal Infirmary and Castle Hill Hospital for HUTH.

As Teaching Hospitals working with the Hull York Medical School, we both lead and contribute to research in many areas - biomedical research, primary care, palliative medicine, cardiovascular and respiratory medicine, vascular surgery, cancer surgery and oncology.

We believe that by developing a diverse, inclusive, innovative, skilled and caring workforce, we can deliver excellent care to our patients and a great future for our employees, our Partnership and our community.

title: Clinical Fellow in Robotic Oesophago-Gastric (OG) Surgery
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for a full time post-CCT Clinical Fellow in Robotic Oesophago-Gastric (OG) Surgery at the Royal Surrey NHS Foundation Trust, Guildford.

This is a one year post commencing Wednesday 07th April 2027, specifically intended for senior trainees seeking to consolidate their training in robotic OG cancer, robotic complex benign, and emergency OG surgery.The Oesophago-Gastric unit is well supported with 6 consultant OG surgeons, 1 Fellow (this position), 2 SpRs, 2 SHOs and 2 F1s. There are 5 upper GI clinical nurse specialists, 5 dedicated OG dietitians, an excellent physiotherapy team and exceptional anaesthetic/intensive care support. The Trust offers full step down care for major resections and emergency cases where required, and a dedicated upper GI ward. Experience in the use of standardised enhanced recovery pathways will also be gained.

The successful applicant will attend the weekly multi-disciplinary team meeting, out-patient clinics, therapeutic endoscopy and theatre sessions, and take part in the General Surgery SpR on-call rota. There will specifically be opportunities to undertake training in radical robotic OG cancer surgery in 4 dedicated three session robotic lists per week. The successful applicant will be expected to participate in audits arranged by the firms and will have the opportunity to undertake research and teaching for undergraduate students.Interview : 17/11/26

The successful applicant will have responsibility for day-to-day management of the in-patients, attend outpatient clinics, and receive training in robotic oesophago-gastric cancer surgery, therapeutic endoscopy and endoscopic ultrasound. The successful applicant will also be involved in research and teaching activities. The appointee will also be part of the on-call rota (SpR), for surgical emergencies.

Royal Surrey is a compassionate and collaborative acute and community Trust. Recognising that our 5000 colleagues are our greatest strength, we offer a comprehensive health and wellbeing program along with a commitment to developing and advancing your career. Our diverse and welcoming Royal Surrey family will ensure you that you feel valued from your initial interview through your entire tenure.

We are clinically led and provide joined up care by bridging the gap between hospital and community services alongside regional specialist cancer care. Our main acute hospital site is in Guildford with community hospital sites at Milford, Haslemere and Cranleigh. We provide adult community health services in homes across Guildford and Waverley.

The Care Quality Commission (CQC) have given us an overall rating of Outstanding.

Royal Surrey has a strong reputation and history to build on. We are proud of our achievements and we are investing in our colleagues through our commitment to supporting professional development as well as investing more than £45 million in our physical environment and new equipment in the next few years. There has never been a better time to join us.

Although it isn't the Trusts normal practice, adverts may close early, so you are encouraged to submit an application as soon as possible.

descriptionHtml:
