employer: Great Ormond Street Hospital for Children NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in Paediatric Dermatology (Part-Time- 5 PAs) Vascular
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen within the Paediatric Dermatology Department at Great Ormond Street Hospital for Children for a 5 PA Consultant Paediatric Dermatologist post. The successful candidate will provide high-quality outpatient clinics for children with complex dermatological conditions and will contribute to inpatient dermatology reviews, ward referrals and the ongoing management of admitted patients. They will play a central role in the management of complex vascular anomalies, including the use of systemic and novel therapies, as well as in the care of a wide range of other paediatric skin disorders. In addition, they will undertake laser treatment for complex dermatological conditions.

The successful candidate will participate in multidisciplinary team meetings with colleagues from paediatric dermatology, histopathology, genetics, plastic surgery, interventional radiology and other paediatric subspecialties, contributing expert input to the management of complex cases. They will also participate in the 1:4 paediatric dermatology on-call rota, providing senior clinical advice and support.

Applicants must be on the GMC Specialist Register in Paediatrics or Paediatric Dermatology, or be within six months of CCT in Paediatrics at the time of interview. Applicants applying via the Portfolio Pathway (formerly CESR) must be on the Specialist Register in Paediatrics or Paediatric Dermatology at the point of application.

Applicants must have extensive experience in paediatric dermatology, including the management of complex and emergency presentations. They must also have extensive experience in the management of patients with complex vascular anomalies, including the use of systemic and targeted therapies, and experience in independently performing laser treatments in paediatric dermatology patients. Please see the person specification for further information.Based in central London, GOSH offers flexible working, support with childcare and travel, excellent training and development opportunities, and assistance with finding accommodation.

If you wish to discuss the role further, please contact Dr Mary Glover, Consultant Paediatric Dermatologist, at mary.glover@gosh.nhs.uk.

All applicants are strongly encouraged to apply electronically via www.jobs.nhs.uk. We welcome applications from all sections of the community.

GOSH is committed to recruiting the best person for the job, based solely on their ability and individual merit as measured against the criteria for the role; through a process that is fair, open, consistent and free from bias and discrimination.

We are committed to being a diverse and inclusive employer and foster a culture where all staff are valued, respected and acknowledged. All applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, colour, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, age, disability status or length of time spent unemployed.

We particularly welcome applications from BAME communities, people with disabilities and/or long-term health conditions and LGBT+ community members.

We have policies and procedures in place to ensure that all applicants and employees are treated fairly and consistently. We are proud to be accredited as a Disability Confident Employer, a member of Business Disability Forum and a Stonewall Diversity Champion.

We have active and Executive supported BAME, LGBT+ and Allies, Disability and Long-Term Health Conditions and Women's staff networks. Staff networks are employee-led groups formed around interests, issues and a common bond or background. Staff network members create a positive and inclusive work environment at Great Ormond Street Hospital by actively contributing to the Trust's mission, values and efforts specific to inclusion. All of our staff networks are open to any employee.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
Chiswick Family Practice is seeking a dedicated, motivated, enthusiastic and forward-thinking General Practitioner to join our friendly practice team. This is an excellent opportunity for a motivated GP who is passionate about delivering high-quality patient care within a supportive and collaborative primary care environment.

The postholder will primarily undertake patient-facing clinical work, contributing to the delivery of safe, effective, and responsive general practice services to our registered population. The role also offers opportunities to contribute to wider practice initiatives and quality improvement activities.

We are looking for an individual committed to excellent clinical care, teamwork, and continuous improvement, who thrives in a dynamic and patient-centred environment.

Assess and triage patients, including same-day presentations, providing treatment or referrals in line with NICE guidelines and local pathways. Manage undifferentiated and complex conditions through history taking, examination, diagnosis, and care planning. Deliver face-to-face and telephone consultations, supporting long-term conditions, acute presentations, and undertaking clinical administration (prescriptions, referrals, and test results). Provide high-quality, evidence-based care and prescribe in line with national and practice policies. Support vulnerable groups, including care home residents, and identify and manage mental health needs with appropriate referral. Accurately interpret pathology results and ensure effective use of read codes. Assist with clinical emergencies, safeguarding, and medicines optimisation. Contribute to QOF and practice targets, liaise with external services, support personalised care plans, and undertake home visits where required.

Chiswick Family Practice is a well-established, friendly and supportive GP surgery located in West London, committed to providing high-quality, patient-centred care to our local community. We pride ourselves on fostering a supportive and inclusive working environment, where teamwork, professional development, and innovation are encouraged. We have a team of approximately 20 staff and have an excellent reputation within the local area and high levels of patient satisfaction.

employer: University Hospitals Dorset NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in Geriatric Medicine
descriptionHtml:
We are looking to appoint two new colleagues to the Geriatric Medicine Department at University Hospitals Dorset, comprising of Poole Hospital, Bournemouth Hospital and Christchurch Hospital.

This is a permanent post for two full-time Consultant Geriatricians, though applicants wishing to work flexibly or less than full-time will be considered. Sub-specialty interests are encouraged.

The main purpose of the post is to support the provision of highest quality patient care through personal actions and continuous improvement. A variety of roles are available depending upon the individuals interests and some examples (for guidance only) are shown below.   • Interface and community geriatrics
  • Orthogeriatrics and surgical liaison
  • Movement disorders

We are keen to appoint the right candidates who are flexible, enthusiastic, self-motivated and will enable the successful candidates to develop as a leader and to further enhance service delivery within our changing organisation. Our values define who we are as #TeamUHD. They underpin everything we do now and in the future. They define how we treat our patients, visitors, and each other, our valued teammates and colleagues.

title: ARRS GP
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking to appoint an enthusiastic, motivated and forward-thinking General Practitioner (GP) to join our supportive and collaborative primary care team. This is an exciting opportunity for a GP to contribute to the delivery of high-quality patient care within general practice.

The post is offered on a fixed-term salaried contract and is supported through the Additional Roles Reimbursement Scheme (ARRS). The position is open to GPs who meet the current ARRS eligibility criteria, regardless of when they obtained their Certificate of Completion of Training (CCT).

Applicants must also meet the relevant professional registration and employment requirements.

We offer a supportive working environment, opportunities for professional development and the chance to make a meaningful contribution to the health and wellbeing of our local population.

We are looking for 4 sessions per week; Monday, Thursday and Friday.

Both Kelsall and Kent Practices are members of the Rural Alliance PCN working in collaboration with four other neighbouring practices

Both practices have high QOF achievement and are rated as Good by the CQC.

Both practices offer enhanced access on during the week and use EMIS Web, Docman 10, AccuRX, active workflow management and Microsoft Office programmes

Provide patient-centred, evidence-based care that addresses the medical needs of the local patient population. Including diagnosing, treating, and managing a wide variety of acute and chronic medical conditions, working to improve overall health outcomes.

Ensure that all medical services provided align with the standards and obligations set out in the primary care contract. Including meeting targets related to patient care, access, and service quality, in compliance with NHS guidelines.

Implement safe, effective, and cost-efficient prescribing practices, ensuring that medication choices follow both local formularies and national prescribing guidelines. Ensure all admin tasks, including managing referrals to secondary care, processing repeat prescription requests, reviewing test results, and handling patient queries, are completed promptly and accurately to support effective patient care.

Ensure that all patient consultations, treatments, and decisions are accurately recorded in patient notes in a timely manner, following best practices and adhering to legal and policy requirements.

Contribute to the practice team by taking on a fair and equitable share of clinical and admin duties to ensure smooth operations and a balanced workload across the practice.

Collaborate with other health and social care providers to ensure integrated services and maintain accurate patient records.

Kelsall Medical Centre is a friendly patient focussed and well-respected Practice located 9 miles from Chester. We offer -

Modern, purpose-built Health Centre with a Wellbeing Hub/Community Cafe attached to the site

Forward thinking multi-disciplinary team providing care to just under 6300 patients.

Medical Student Training Practice

Dr Kent and Partners is a dispensing practice with 8200 patients. We strive to be a family practice working as a team with well trained and motivated staff to achieve a high standard of care for all our patients.

Dr Kent and Partners is a located in rural Cheshire within the Village of Tarporley and is within a 30-minute commute of Chester and Nantwich offering excellent schools and amenities. We offer -

A personal and friendly service and encourage our patients to take an active interest in their healthcare.

We dispense our patients and provide a repeat prescription delivery service. This traditional yet pro-active and professional approach to the provision of primary care service has helped us to provide additional services for our patients.

Both practices value high quality care for our patients. We are looking for an individual whose key qualities are excellent clinical and interpersonal skills to ensure that care is provided safely, effectively and to a high standard.

employer: Kingston and Richmond NHS Foundation Trust
title: Locum Consultant in Sexual Health and HIV - Parental Leave Cover
descriptionHtml:
The Wolverton Centre (Kingston and Richmond NHS Foundation Trust ) is looking to recruit a full-time Locum consultant in Sexual Health and HIV to cover a period of parental leave. The centre is located on the Kingston Hospital site and prides itself on being a modern and progressive service, providing high quality care for patients presenting with both STI and contraceptive needs, as well as patients living with HIV. A range of clinics; general integrated sexual health, complex (consultant led clinics), and nurse led clinics currently exist across the service and in addition the service has psychology support. There is also a well-established vulval pain service supported by clinical psychology and a newly established tertiary level vulval MDT which is a clinical collaboration between the Gynaecology/Dermatology and Sexual Health consultants and runs a monthly clinic.

The successful candidate will provide clinical care in both the integrated sexual health service and the HIV Service. They will also provide support and training to the clinical team as well as contributing to the clinical governance of the department.

Provide GUM and integrated sexual health clinics and cover emergency presentations to the service.

Share the "Duty senior clinician of the day" rota and provide consultant advice and support to the multi-disciplinary team as well as training to the resident doctors.

Undertake one HIV clinic a week and manage emergencies that present to the clinic or acutely unwell to the wards.

Provide clinical advice to in-patient teams who admit patients living with HIV.

Contribute to the out of hours telephone on call service for GUM and HIV.

The opportunity to lead on the digital strategy for the department will be available for candidates with interests in this area.

The post holder will be expected to support service development including establishment of new community services as opportunities arise, to increase access for all patients, but particularly underserved populations in the boroughs that we provide services for.

They will undertake the role of Audit and Research lead for the department

Development and staff wellbeing

Your growth and happiness matters to us. After all, we can't expect the best from you if we don't invest in your development and nurture your wellbeing. Whether you're just starting your career or looking to advance further, we provide you with the tools and opportunities you need to succeed. Wherever you work across our organisation, we look forward to welcoming you.

descriptionHtml:
An excellent opportunity has arisen to join our expanding patient centred and supportive Gastroenterology department at Blackpool Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust. Our hard-working and forward-thinking team are keen to develop the Gastroenterology and Liver service and would welcome similar minded candidates to join our department. This is an exciting time to join us following investment of £4.0 million recurrent funding to support a blended workforce and £4.5 million capital investment to refurbish our Endoscopy unit. There will be opportunity to support outpatient transformation as part of a blended workforce as we develop our Luminal and Liver services and establish novel outpatient pathways.

Our Gastroenterology and Liver service is one of the busiest in the UK - we offer a broad range of diagnostic and therapeutic services for all gastroenterological conditions. Our recently refurbished JAG accredited, performance driven and patient centred Endoscopy unit delivers approximately 15,000 procedures per annum and is a spoke centre for the North-West Endoscopy training academy and is the admin hub for Bowel cancer screening within the Lancashire region.

The post holder is expected to have a broad experience of Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Endoscopy, contributing to the core Gastroenterology elective and emergency service but with special emphasis on delivering Hepatology services.

There is shared care of inpatients under the Gastroenterology team on the Gastroenterology ward with a Consultant currently being ward based for 1 week out of every 6 weeks. The appointee will make an equal contribution to the care of Gastroenterology inpatients and the out-of-hours GI-Bleed endoscopy service which is 1:6 at present with plans to transition to a 1:8 model with further recruitment. All on-call weeks are followed by a post-on-call (POC) week where Gastroenterology triage, a post-on-call clinic and fast-track clinic are delivered. The POC week is followed by standard normal weeks until the next on-call cycle. Elective activity (outpatient clinics, endoscopy lists) is mainly concentrated in the 5-week period off the ward.

The job plan comprises 10 Programmed activities including allocation for the current on call commitment. Job plans will be formally reviewed within the first 6 months after appointment and agreed according to evidence from actual activity.

Blackpool Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is situated on the west coast of Lancashire, with services covering the local authority areas of Blackpool, Fylde and Wyre. The Trust is part of the Lancashire and South Cumbria Integrated Care System (ICS) supporting a population of around 1.6 million people.

Blackpool Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust serves a resident population of approximately 330,000 and the 12 million holidaymakers who visit the area every year. The Trust comprises Blackpool Victoria Hospital which is a large busy acute hospital and a smaller community/ rehabilitation hospital - Clifton Hospital. Outpatient services are also provided in Blackpool, Fleetwood and Lytham Hospital. employer: Surrey and Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust
title: Consultant in Microbiology and Infection
descriptionHtml:
Consultant in Microbiology and Infection

We have an exciting opportunity for a consultant who is interested in working within an innovative NHS Trust that is regarded as Outstanding by the CQC.

Applications are invited for a whole-time Consultant post in Microbiology & Infection (10 PAs, of which 8.5 are DCC and 1.5 are SPA) based at East Surrey Hospital in Redhill, which is the main acute site for Surrey & Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust (SASH). The Trust's catchment area comprises over half a million population, around half of which reside in West Sussex (Crawley, Horsham, Gatwick Airport, and extending towards Haywards Heath and East Grinstead) and half in eastern Surrey (Redhill, Reigate, Dorking, extending towards Epsom and Sutton in the north).

We are looking for a consultant who is highly motivated, committed to improvement, patient-centred and a strong team-player. If you are interested in ambulatory (COPAT, SDEC, virtual ward) and multi-disciplinary infection services over and above core clinical microbiology services, then this post will be very attractive to you. Applicants must hold FRCPath or equivalent and must be on the GMC Specialist Register (or be within six months of being included in the register). In addition, training in infectious diseases and holding MRCP are highly desirable.

The successful candidate will be part of a team of two full-time consultant microbiologists, 1 full-time associate specialist in microbiology and infection, 1 specialty registrar, 4 infection prevention & control nurses, 1 antimicrobial stewardship pharmacist, 1 practice development nurse and 1 tissue viability nurse. There are academic, teaching and research opportunities through the Trust's association with Brighton & Sussex Medical School as well as our own highly active R&D department. A suitably qualified candidate may be eligible for an honorary academic appointment at the medical School. The Trust is a partner of Berkshire & Surrey Pathology Services (BSPS), which would present further academic and research opportunities via the University of Surrey.

The counties of Surrey and Sussex provide an ideal mix of beautiful countryside (the North Downs, the South Downs and an Area of Outstanding Beauty around Box Hill); vibrant city life in Brighton and via easy access to London; a wonderful range of National Trust, National Heritage and other places of interest, such as Wakehurst Place, the Bluebell railway, Epsom racecourse, Brighton & Hove Albion's Amex Stadium, and many wineries; excellent schools and colleges; and easy access to Europe and further afield via Gatwick Airport and the nearby Channel Tunnel. The Trust offers a contribution towards relocation expenses.

We are a leading local employer with a diverse workforce of approximately 6,000 staff, dedicated to providing healthcare services to a growing population of around 780,000 individuals.

Our Trust provides both emergency and planned healthcare across East Surrey, North-East West Sussex, and South Croydon - covering towns like Crawley, Horsham, Reigate, and Redhill. Our main hospital, East Surrey in Redhill, offers a full range of acute and specialist services and is also the closest trauma unit to Gatwick Airport. We also provide outpatient, diagnostic, and planned care services at sites including The Earlswood Centre, Caterham Dene Hospital, Oxted Health Centre, Crawley Hospital, and Horsham Hospital.

We are proud to be an inclusive employer, and we work hard to create an environment where everyone feels valued and supported. At our Trust, we strive to be the best place to work and receive care. We are dedicated to supporting you in your current role while helping you grow and develop your career. As part of our team, you will have access to excellent training opportunities, flexible working, dedicated support networks, and a strong emphasis on health and wellbeing to ensure a thriving and positive work environment.

descriptionHtml:
We are looking for talented, committed health care professionals to lead our ambitious new healthcare organisation. In return, the Barts Health will provide unsurpassed professional development opportunities, enabling investment in a range of new initiatives that would mean:

  • there would be greater opportunity for career progression - we will retain good staff who might otherwise leave to gain promotion.

The practice is based in the historic town of Maldon, with easy access to the A12 and convenient links to London, Chelmsford, and Colchester. We also benefit from having an on-site dispensary and community pharmacy, which enhances continuity of care for our patients.

title: Pharmacy Technician
descriptionHtml:
Pharmacy Technicians play a vital role within the primary care multidisciplinary team, supporting the safe, effective and efficient use of medicines. Working alongside GPs, Clinical Pharmacists and other healthcare professionals, they help to optimise prescribing processes, improve patient outcomes and ensure compliance with medicines management policies and procedures.

The role focuses on the delivery of high-quality prescribing support, including medicines optimisation, repeat prescribing management, medication reviews, medicines reconciliation and reducing medicines waste. Pharmacy Technicians contribute to improving patient safety by identifying and resolving medication-related issues, supporting prescribing audits and implementing best practice guidance.

As an integral member of the practice team, the Pharmacy Technician helps to streamline prescribing systems, enhance operational efficiency and support the delivery of patient-centred care, ensuring that medicines are used safely, appropriately and cost-effectively across the practice population.

Main Duties and Skills
  • Qualified to BTEC or NVQ Level 3 in Pharmaceutical Sciences (or equivalent), with a minimum of two years' post-qualification experience.
  • Demonstrates a strong understanding of primary care prescribing and the ability to review, monitor and improve prescribing practices, with a focus on patient safety, clinical effectiveness and cost efficiency.
  • Possesses excellent communication, interpersonal and leadership skills, enabling effective collaboration with Pharmacists, GPs, and administrative teams.
  • Self-motivated and proactive, with the ability to work independently, prioritise tasks effectively, manage workloads and meet deadlines.
  • Supports the delivery of high-quality patient care by developing and implementing safe, effective and efficient prescribing processes, including repeat prescribing systems, medicines optimisation initiatives, reduction of medicines waste and other prescribing improvement activities.
  • Works under the guidance of the Clinical Pharmacist Team to promote best practice, improve prescribing outcomes and enhance patient safety across the practice.

Newquay Health Centre is a busy and forward-thinking GP practice serving a growing population of approximately 17,500 patients. We are committed to providing high-quality healthcare services in a friendly, supportive and positive environment for both our patients and staff.

Our multidisciplinary team includes GPs, nurses, healthcare professionals and a dedicated administrative team, all working together to deliver excellent patient care. We also have a well-established pharmacy team comprising a Clinical Pharmacist, Pharmacy Technician and Pharmacy Administration Support staff, who play a key role in medicines optimisation, prescribing management and improving patient outcomes.

We are committed to continuous improvement and staff development, offering opportunities for role progression, skill enhancement and professional growth within a collaborative and supportive working environment.

title: Salaried GP - East Cliff Practice
descriptionHtml:
Invicta Health has a Salaried GP opportunity available at East Cliff Practice, with up to 5 sessions available.

East Cliff Practice is based in Ramsgate with its historic harbour, attractive coastline and on the high speed rail link to London. Our neighbours are the traditional seaside towns of Broadstairs with its blue flag beaches, and Margate, home to the Turner Centre and Old Town area.

East Cliff Practice is warm and friendly with a robust multi-disciplinary team, which includes Advanced Nurse Practitioners, Nurse Practitioners and a Clinical Pharmacy team. The multi-disciplinary team is supported by an experienced reception and administration team who handle referrals, prescriptions, reports and other general tasks.

East Cliff Practice is one of seven GP Practices that sit under Invicta Health. We are a well known community interest company, devoted to supporting and improving primary care in the Kent area.

We are looking for an enthusiastic and compassionate GP who enjoys a team focus in problem solving and also enjoys sharing knowledge. You will have excellent verbal and written communication skills and you will be an excellent listener. You will be on the General Medical Council's GP register, having passed the MRCGP (or equivalent) and gained a certificate of Completion of Training (CCT). Good communication between colleagues is essential to the role, as we routinely share our experience and knowledge within the practice in order to optimise patient care.

Home visits by the GPs are rare.

Invicta Health is a non-profit company, with a passion for primary care. We have a wide range of services such as hub-based GPs services, GP surgeries, services in Urgent Care Centres and A&E, a Community Primary Care mental health service, GP staff training service and the list is growing all the time.

We are formed by a federation of General Practitioners working in Canterbury and South Kent Coast areas of East Kent. Our aim is to provide local, high quality services for local people by collaborating with other established organisations in the health and social care community.

employer: The Royal Marsden NHS Foundation Trust
title: Registrar in Clinical Oncology
descriptionHtml:
We are looking to appoint enthusiastic and forward-thinking doctors to the post of Registrar in Clinical Oncology. This post is offered on a fixed-term basis until 2nd March 2027 to cover a gap in the current Deanery rotation. There may be scope to extend the appointment for a further six months, subject to confirmation of Deanery placements and continued service requirements.

To fulfil the responsibilities of the post, the successful candidate will be required to demonstrate experience in oncological management and preferably hold MRCP or an equivalent qualification. The post may also be attractive to candidates preparing for the FRCR.

The post would be particularly suitable for experienced international oncologists wishing to gain further specialist experience in an international tertiary centre. The post could also be tailored to an experienced medical doctor who having completed Foundation and Core Medical competencies (or equivalent), wish to gain a period of focused experience and training in Clinical Oncology before pursuing ST3 training.

The specialty of Clinical Oncology comprises management of cancer using both radiotherapy and systemic therapy (chemotherapy, hormone therapy and biological agents). It offers a unique opportunity to develop expertise in managing cancer patients and engaging in clinical research and academia. A multidisciplinary team approach and effective communication is integral to the specialty of oncology.

The Royal Marsden is a world leader in cancer research, treatment and education. Together with our academic partner, The Institute of Cancer Research (ICR), we are the largest comprehensive cancer centre in Europe and the only National Institute of Health Research (NIHR) Biomedical Research Centre specialising in cancer in the UK.

Our mission is to continue to make a national and international contribution to cancer research and treatment, so that more people are cured and quality of life is improved for those with cancer. The Royal Marsden therefore plays an important role in championing change and improvement in cancer care through research and innovation, education and leading-edge treatment.

We have a reputation for delivering high quality performance. We were ranked joint first in the CQC national inpatient survey results, above average in national cancer patient experience survey and ranked first amongst teaching hospitals in the UK for our staff survey results.

Predominantly the Trust's workload is from within the South West and West London Cancer Networks but, as a specialist cancer, the Trust has a high out-of-area referral rate for rare cancers, recurrent disease and treatment-related problems including international referrals. The Trust operates a shared care model with St George's Healthcare NHS Trust for paediatric cancer.

employer: Sherwood Forest Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Specialty Doctor in Newark Urgent Treatment Centre
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for a Specialty Doctor to join an innovative team dedicated to the delivery of high quality care within Sherwood Forest Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust.

This post is based at Newark Urgent Treatment Centre, Newark Hospital, but may also undertake programmed activities at King's Mill Hospital if required.

Whilst on duty a doctor has clinical and professional responsibility for their patients. It is also the duty of a doctor to:

Keep patients (and/or their carers if appropriate) informed about their condition.

Involve patients (and/or their carers if appropriate) in decision-making about their treatment.

Maintain professional standards and obligations as set out from time to time by the General Medical Council (GMC) and comply with GMC's guidance on 'Good Medical Practice' as amended or substituted from time to time.

A doctor is responsible for carrying out any work related to and reasonably incidental to the duties set out in the Job Plan such as:

The keeping of records and the provision of reports.

The proper delegation of tasks.

Maintaining skills and knowledge.

Doctors will be expected to be flexible and to cooperate with reasonable requests to cover for their colleagues' absence where they are safe and competent and where it is practicable to do so.

The overriding purpose is to support the provision of the highest quality patient care through personal actions and continuous improvement.

- Under the supervision of the Consultant in Emergency Medicine, provide to the care of patients in the department with responsibility for the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of illness or injury.

- Referral of patients to appropriate inpatient facilities as appropriate.

- Involvement in Emergency Medicine multi-disciplinary teams and meetings.

- Outpatient programmed activities depending on the needs of patients.

- Teaching and supervision of junior medical staff and nursing staff as appropriate.

- Active involvement in audit, clinical governance, and the development of departmental policies.

- So far as is consistent with the discharge of the above duties, the post-holder shall undertake to deputise for absent colleagues, when the post-holder deputises outside his/her normal contracted duties and commitment, an equivalent amount of off-duty shall be given.

- The post-holder undertakes to be available for such irregular commitments outside normal reserved duties as are essential for the continuity of patient care.

- To take responsibility for your own continuing professional education in accordance with guidelines set out by the appropriate college/faculty/professional body.

We are an award-winning NHS Foundation Trust working alongside health and social care colleagues across the county to provide acute and community healthcare services to more than 420,000 people across Mansfield, Ashfield, Newark and Sherwood, and parts of Derbyshire and Lincolnshire.

Sherwood is nationally recognised as being an excellent place to work and deliver care. We are rightly proud of the 5,500 colleagues who work here.

We are proud that our Trust colleagues have voted us the best acute Trust to work for in the East Midlands for seven years running in the National NHS Staff Survey, while the Care Quality Commission has rated our Trust as 'outstanding' for care and our King's Mill Hospital as the only 'outstanding' NHS-run hospital in the East Midlands.

We know happy colleagues deliver better care. All our teams work in a supportive environment, which nurtures your wellbeing and provides opportunities for development and progression. We do not just care for our patients, we also care for you.

We have an open, inclusive and diverse culture and we would like you to be part of the team.

employer: The Newcastle upon Tyne Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Deputy Clinical Director Genomic Medicine Service - Cancer
descriptionHtml:
We are delighted to be able to offer an opportunity for a highly motivated, ambitious individual to join our well integrated team.

The NEY GMS brings together regional Clinical and Laboratory Partners, all working together to improve health and equity of access to genomic tests, diagnosis and related treatments for patients in the region.

The NEY GMS is led by four partner trusts: The Newcastle upon Tyne Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, The Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust, Sheffield Children's NHS Foundation Trust and Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust. There are around 500 medical, scientific, technologist, counselling and support staff focused entirely on Genomics. They support a much larger network of mainstream clinicians including Oncologists, Pathologists, Neurologists, Obstetricians, Paediatricians, Nurses and Pharmacists who use genomic diagnosis to support clinical decision making and improve patient care.

The NEY GMS is governed via a partnership arrangement that is delivered by a regional GMS executive team which has operational responsibility for the quality of services. The GMS executive team is accountable to the NEY GMS Partnership Board which includes representation from partner Trusts.

Closing date: 11 November 2026 @ midnight

Interview Date: TBC

This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced clinical leader to support the delivery of the Cancer clinical function within the North East and Yorkshire Genomic Medicine Service. Working closely with the Clinical Director for Cancer and wider GMS leadership team, you will help drive the development of genomic testing pathways, improve access to precision oncology and support the implementation of transformational programmes across the region. The role offers the opportunity to influence strategy, strengthen partnerships and ensure genomic advances continue to improve outcomes for cancer patients throughout North East and Yorkshire.

We are aiming to appoint a highly credible and influential clinical leader with a proven track record of leading service transformation, and the strategic insight to drive innovation across complex healthcare systems. The role will combine clinical and scientific credibility with strong executive leadership, demonstrating the ability to shape regional and national agendas, build effective partnerships across organisational boundaries, and deliver measurable improvements in quality, access, and patient outcomes.

For an informal discussion and further information regarding the opportunity and Directorate, please contact: Mr Neville Gaukroger (NEY GMS Managing Director) via email at Neville.Gaukroger@nhs.net

Please refer to the attached Job Description and Person Specification document for full details of the role and essential criteria.

As a flexible working friendly organisation, we want to be sure that you can work in a way that is best for us and for our patients, and for you. Speak to us about how we might be able to accommodate a flexible working arrangement. If it works for the service, we will do our best to make it work for you.

With around 2 million contacts with patients every year, we deliver care from:

title: Consultant Adult Critical Care Transfer Service (ACCTS) Cymru
descriptionHtml:
Join a dynamic and forward-thinking team that combines cutting-edge transfer and retrieval medicine with critical care and anaesthesia.

This exciting role is perfect for doctors, offering a unique opportunity to work at the forefront of critical care transfers in Wales.

Each year, approximately 800 critical care transfers (Level 2 and Level 3) are undertaken across Wales. In response to the growing demand for critical care and the regionalisation of specialist services, the Welsh Government launched the Adult Critical Care Transfer Service (ACCTS) Cymru in 2020. As networks continue to develop and evolve, the number of transfers is set to rise, reflecting the increasing need for this essential service.

ACCTS Cymru is a road-based service, deploying with state-of-the-art critical care transfer vehicles and equipment. Every mission is supported by a highly skilled team, including a critical care transfer physician, a support worker, and a retrieval and transfer practitioner. These practitioners bring diverse expertise, with backgrounds in critical care nursing all with extensive intensive care experience and specialised training in inter-facility critical care transfer.

The Critical Care Transfer Physician has an advanced level of relevant knowledge and skills in order to support the assessment, care and management of critically ill or unwell patients.

Successful candidates will be deployed within this role as part of a multidisciplinary team configuration: predominantly by road, but also on occasion by air. Therefore, the role requires the practitioner to be able to operate comfortably and effectively in these environments and undergo further training applicable to these aspects of the role including:

Timely response to transfer requests from the critical care network made via the EMRTS Critical Care Hub (ECCH) and/or the duty transfer coordinator.

Participate in multidisciplinary handover in the referring unit, taking responsibility for the patients ongoing nursing care needs throughout the transfer

Provide and/or support appropriate assessment, stabilisation and clinical intervention in the referring hospital as part of the Critical Care transfer team, prior to transfer, in line with the Critical Care clinical and equipment standard operating procedures.

Working closely with the duty co-ordinator and practitioner in planning and executing the safe and efficient transfer of critically ill patients that meet the Service criteria for dispatch

Coordinated activity in line with the Adult Critical Care Transfer Service standard clinical and operational operating procedures

The Health Board is part of A Regional Collaboration for Health (ARCH), which is a partnership with Hywel Dda UHB and Swansea University. Aimed at improving the wellbeing and wealth of South West Wales.

Swansea is Wales' second-largest city, and sits on the five-mile sweep of Swansea Bay. An ideal base for exploring South-West Wales, there is also much on offer for visitors in Swansea itself. Swansea has a range of shops, cozy cafes, great restaurants, art galleries as well as being able to offer good outdoor lifestyle with its beautiful coastline and beaches on the Gower Peninsula. descriptionHtml:
Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is seeking to appoint an experienced and motivated Specialist Doctor to join the Breast Surgery team.

This is an exciting opportunity to join a busy specialist service, providing senior clinical care across the breast pathway. The post holder will work as an integral member of the multidisciplinary team, contributing to outpatient assessment, elective operating, peri-operative care and the ongoing development and delivery of the service.

The post will provide additional senior surgical capacity to support the service in delivering timely cancer care and increasing elective activity. The successful candidate will also play an important role in supporting the expansion of elective surgery through the Surgical Elective Centre (SEC), including delivery of additional operating capacity as the centre becomes operational.

We are looking for an experienced doctor who is able to work autonomously within their scope of practice, demonstrates sound clinical judgement and is committed to delivering high-quality, patient-centred breast care.

The post holder will work as part of the Breast Surgery multidisciplinary team and will undertake a broad range of clinical duties across the breast pathway.

Key responsibilities will include:

  • Undertaking breast outpatient clinics, including assessment and follow-up of patients.
  • Contributing to elective breast operating lists and providing appropriate peri-operative and post-operative clinical care.
  • Supporting the delivery of timely cancer treatment and the service's ongoing work to improve cancer pathway performance.
  • Participating in multidisciplinary working and contributing to relevant MDT meetings.
  • Providing senior clinical assessment, decision-making and management of patients within the post holder's agreed scope of competence.
  • Supporting additional elective activity, including weekend operating where required.
  • Providing appropriate cross-cover for surgical activity to support continuity and effective utilisation of available theatre capacity.
  • Supporting the delivery of breast surgical activity through the Surgical Elective Centre (SEC), including undertaking additional operating lists and reviewing patients within the SEC as required.
  • Contributing to clinical governance, audit, teaching, service development and continuous improvement within the Breast Surgery service.
  • Working flexibly across Oxford University Hospitals sites in accordance with service requirements and the agreed job plan.

Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is one of the largest NHS teaching trusts in the country. It provides a wide range of general and specialist clinical services and is a base for medical education, training and research. The Trust comprises four hospitals - the John Radcliffe Hospital, Churchill Hospital and Nuffield Orthopaedic Centre in Headington and the Horton General Hospital in Banbury.

Our values, standards and behaviours define the quality of clinical care we offer and the professional relationships we make with our patients, colleagues and the wider community.

These values put patients at the heart of what we do and underpin the quality healthcare we would like for ourselves or a member of our family. Watch how we set out to deliver compassionate excellence via the OUH YouTube channel.

The Health in Justice team at Practice Plus Group makes a real difference across over 53 prisons, young offenders and immigration removal centres. Were the UKs leading independent provider of NHS services to over 40,000 patients in secure environments, always putting their needs first, regardless of their background.

employer: South Downs Health and Care Ltd (SDHC)
title: GP with an Interest in Frailty
descriptionHtml:
South Downs Health and Care (SDHC) is seeking a compassionate, enthusiastic and motivated Salaried GP with an Interest in Frailty to join our Integrated Neighbourhood Team (INT) in Eastbourne.

This is an exciting opportunity to make a meaningful difference to the lives of older people and those living with frailty, helping them remain healthy, independent and supported within their communities.

Working as part of a supportive multidisciplinary team, you will provide expert clinical care to patients with frailty, multiple long-term conditions and complex health and social care needs. You will play a key role in delivering proactive, personalised care, preventing avoidable hospital admissions and improving patient outcomes.

You will work closely with Frailty Practitioners, community services, local GP practices and wider health and social care partners to ensure coordinated, patient-centred care.

We are looking for a GP who is passionate about older people's healthcare, enjoys collaborative working and is keen to contribute to the development of innovative community-based frailty services.

As a Salaried GP with an Interest in Frailty, you will provide senior clinical expertise within the Integrated Neighbourhood Team, supporting patients with frailty, multimorbidity and complex care needs.

Your main responsibilities will include:

  • Undertaking comprehensive clinical assessments in patients' homes, care homes and community settings.

  • Completing Comprehensive Geriatric Assessments (CGA) and supporting structured medication reviews.

  • Developing personalised care plans, advance care plans and treatment escalation plans.

  • Identifying patients at risk of deterioration and implementing proactive interventions to prevent avoidable hospital admissions.

  • Supporting safe hospital discharge and continuity of care.

  • Providing clinical leadership, guidance and advice to Frailty Practitioners and wider multidisciplinary colleagues.

  • Working collaboratively with GP practices, geriatricians, community services, mental health teams and social care partners.

  • Participating in multidisciplinary team meetings and complex case discussions.

  • Contributing to service development, clinical governance and quality improvement initiatives.

You will help deliver safe, effective and compassionate care that promotes independence, improves quality of life and supports patients to remain well within their communities.

South Downs Health and Care GP Federation is a social enterprise. It was established in 2016 in service to shareholding/member GP practices in the areas of Eastbourne, Hailsham and Seaford. It now has extended membership within East Sussex. Our main purpose is to support GP practices in their task of providing patient care by enabling them to provide and invest in sustainable services by reducing the burden of their workload, maximising income opportunities and minimising their risks and liabilities.

We encourage our staff to take ownership and responsibility, to highlight concerns and feedback and to make an active contribution to their individual success as well as that of their team and the wider organisation. We operate a no-blame culture; by this we mean that everyone is held accountable but in an environment where the focus is on the learning that can be adopted and shared from instances where things havent gone so well.

Benefits of Working with SDHC

  • NHS Pension Scheme with generous employer contributions
  • 25 days holiday plus bank holidays, increasing in stages to 30 days holiday plus bank holidays after 5 years service (pro rata for part time hours)
  • Employee Assistance Programme including access to counselling and support with legal and financial matters
  • CycleScheme
  • Christmas and summer events
  • Discounted rate for membership of Hillbrow Health and Wellbeing Centre facilities

descriptionHtml:
We are looking for an enthusiastic consultant cardiologist to join our comprehensive cardiology service delivered from our 4 hospital sites.

The post will contribute to a full range of in-patient and out-patient cardiology services and be based at Worthing Hospital but contribute to and collaborate with teams at Worthing Hospital, St Richard's Hospital and the Royal Sussex County Hospital in Brighton (RSCH).

The post will participate in the separate cross-site general cardiology on-call rota with no current commitment to the G(I)M on-call rota

The appointee will form part of a team of 10 cardiologists at Worthing Hospital who deliver a comprehensive outpatient and inpatient Cardiology service for patients from across the Trust.

We are seeking to appoint a Cardiologist with sub-specialty training in Heart Failure and another sub-speciality interest who can also contribute to the General Cardiology On-call Rota.

According to sub-speciality training we will enable access to cath lab facilities on the Worthing Hospital and Royal Sussex County Hospital sites or diagnostic facilities at Worthing Hospital, St Richard's Hospital and the community diagnostic centre at Southlands Hospital.

The appointee will join the team of 9 other Consultant Cardiologists Worthing Hospital delivering a comprehensive outpatient and inpatient cardiology service for patients from across the Trust. There will be a regular commitment to outpatient clinic activity. Generic Cardiology referrals and advice and guidance requests are divided between the consultants for response via the e-RS system. This post will support the expansion of the heart failure service to include rapid access heart failure clinics, heart failure ward rounds with the clinical nurse specialists and heart failure MDT (hospital and community). There will be a commitment to managing the administration generated by these activities including the reporting of investigations back to GPs and responding to GP correspondence.

Consultant input and support for the non-invasive Cardiology investigation services.

Teaching and supervision of medical students, junior medical staff and technicians/nurses.

Applicants are encouraged to take part in audit and support junior team members in their audit projects. There are opportunities for clinical research and to take part in the Trusts' excellent Quality Improvement Programme - the Patient First Improvement System.

On call (for cardiology) 1:12 nights and weekends covering cardiology advice for Worthing and St Richard's Hospitals. No GIM on-call commitment currently. Category B. 1% supplement

Working for our organisation

At UHSussex, diversity is our strength, and we want you to feel included to help us always deliver Excellent Care Everywhere, as shown in our Outstanding for Caring CQC rating. Your uniqueness and experiences will be part of our creative and innovative community where everyone is encouraged to succeed. employer: Barking, Havering and Redbridge University Hospitals NHS Trust
title: Consultant Clinical Oncologist (Lung)
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for a candidate interested in a permanent clinical oncology consultant post at Barking, Havering & Redbridge University Hospitals NHS Trust.

We are looking for an enthusiastic clinical oncologist to join our well-established, dedicated and supportive team.

The successful candidate will join a team of 14 consultant oncologists supported by three specialty doctors and six clinical oncology SpRs to serve a population of 750,000. The department treats the full spectrum of malignant disease including breast, lung, lower and upper GI, haematology, gynaecology, urology, neuro-oncology, skin, and head and neck. SABR is delivered for primary lung cancer and oligometastatic disease. SRS is delivered in partnership with Barts Health NHS Trust for skull base tumours and brain metastasis.

The post will cover lung and one other tumour group preferably breast (radiotherapy only) or lymphoma though other interests can be discussed. You will be located at Queen's Hospital, Romford, Essex where the Oncology department is based.

Consultant Clinical Oncologist (Lungs)

To provide, to a high standard, the full range of specialist diagnosis, treatment and care to patients requiring oncology services, as outlined in the proposed program which includes the following:

Clinical oncology management of lung malignancy including RT/SABR and SACT.

Clinical oncology management of one other tumour site.

New patient numbers approx. 170-200 per annum. This will be four to five patients per week on a 42-week year.

To work with and support the established multi-disciplinary site-specific teams.

Outpatient chemotherapy and inpatient clinical opinions.

Participate in the oncology urgent/emergency care service:

    • Once current recruitment is complete consultants on-call frequency will be 1:15 non-resident for advice.
    • During core hours 0845-1700 Monday to Friday we operate a 'consultant of the day model'. This consists of attendance of the Sky B board round, input into oncology patients presenting to ED overnight. Patients who present with SACT or RT related toxicity are expected to have care 'taken over' by oncology. Those patients placed outside of the specialist ward are required to have daily input from the consultant or SpR of the day. Routine elective work within the job plan is cancelled or reduced accordingly.

(Please see attached JD for full details of the main duties)

We're an organisation that is getting better and better and our improvements are driven by a determination to deliver care we're proud of and our patients are happy with.

They are benefitting from a new electronic patient record (we were the last acute trust in London to introduce one) and our maternity services have been rated good by the Care Quality Commission.

We operate from two main sites - KGH in Goodmayes and Queen's Hospital in Romford. We have two busy emergency departments with more than 346,000 people visiting them last year. We're campaigning to secure the £35m we need to transform the A&E at Queen's and get rid of corridor care.

We're proud of our regional Neurosciences Centre, Radiotherapy Centre and Hyper Acute Stroke Unit. We're also part of the North East London Cancer Alliance.

We run a Women's Health Hub in Ilford; an Ageing Well Centre in Hornchurch; and Community Diagnostic Centres (CDC) at Barking Community Hospital and at St George's Health and Wellbeing Hub. These CDCs are open 12 hours a day, 7 days a week.

The majority of our 8,400 staff - who come from 146 different countries - live in the three diverse London boroughs we serve and are from black, Asian and minority ethnic groups. Many can work flexibly and more than 400 of them are on our Ofsted accredited apprenticeship programmes. We're proud to be a London Living Wage employer.

employer: University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Locum Consultant Paediatrician
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for an energetic, skilled Paediatric Consultant to join the Lighthouse, the UK's first dedicated service for children and young people affected by non-recent sexual abuse and exploitation. The Lighthouse forms part of the Paediatric and Adolescent Division at UCLH NHS Foundation Trust.Based on the Child House (Barnahus) model, the service provides holistic health assessments, reduces trauma for children, and provides support for children who have experienced child sexual abuse. Located in London, it serves half a million children and supports children and young people aged 0 to 18 and adults 18 to 25 with learning disabilities.You will join a specialist health team of four consultants, a 0.7 WTE clinical nurse specialist, and a 0.6 WTE play specialist, working alongside a multidisciplinary team including social workers, ChISVAs, CAMHS practitioners, and the admin and Senior Leadership team.

This maternity cover post involves one day per week with two programmed activities including one clinic, with opportunities to join peer review and team meetings contributing to holistic assessments, legal and social care reports, and care planning. The role covers a range of clinical issues including psychosomatic symptoms, sleep difficulties, headaches, menstrual problems, sexually transmitted infections, contraception including LARC, and immunisations including Hep B and HPV.

CV required for the application

Maternity (cover until: 31-12-2026)

Provide multidisciplinary medical assessments for children and young people referred with suspected sexual abuse or exploitation, including 0 to 18 years and adults 18 to 25 with learning disabilities.o Undertake direct clinical care, manage complex cases, and contribute to care planning and risk management.o Perform colposcopic ano-genital examinations and collect evidence in line with legal and safeguarding requirements.o Prepare high-quality reports for families, professionals, and criminal courts as required.o Contribute to holistic assessment, treatment, and follow-up of children and young people, including psychosomatic symptoms, sleep problems, headaches, menstrual issues, STIs, contraception, and immunisations.o Participate in safeguarding and strategy meetings, case reviews, and multidisciplinary team discussions.o Collaborate with the health team, social workers, ChISVAs, CAMHS practitioners, and administrative staff to provide integrated care.o Contribute to teaching, training, and supervision of medical students, junior doctors, and specialty trainees.o Participate in departmental peer review, quality improvement, governance, and research initiatives.o Represent the department in internal and external meetings, contributing to service development, clinical guidelines, and best practice.

University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (UCLH) is one of the most complex NHS trusts in the UK, serving a large and diverse population. We provide academically led acute and specialist services, to people from the local area, from throughout the United Kingdom and overseas. Our vision is to deliver top-quality patient care, excellent education, and world-class research.

We provide first-class acute and specialist services across eight sites:

University College Hospital (incorporating the Elizabeth Garrett Anderson Wing)

National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgery

Royal National ENT and Eastman Dental Hospitals

University College Hospital Grafton Way Building

Royal London Hospital for Integrated Medicine

University College Hospital Macmillan Cancer Centre

The Hospital for Tropical Diseases

University College Hospital at Westmoreland Street

We are dedicated to the diagnosis and treatment of many complex illnesses. UCLH specialises in women's health and the treatment of cancer, infection, neurological, gastrointestinal and oral disease. It has world class support services including critical care, imaging, nuclear medicine and pathology.

title: GP - Out of Hours
descriptionHtml:
We have immediate opportunities for GPs to join our Out of Hours (OOH) team

Working as a salaried or self-employed GP with FedBucks offers competitive pay, flexibility, a good work life balance, training and career development opportunities, and round-the-clock clinical and operational support.

Our multidisciplinary OOH team provides primary care services across Buckinghamshire for patients who require medical attention when their own GP surgery is closed.

We welcome applications from experienced GPs who are considering a career move or are seeking additional hours alongside another role.

GP weekday cover from 18:30 to 08:00, as well as 24-hour service at weekends and on bank holidays, delivered via telephone consultations, face-to-face appointments and home visits. In addition, we provide in-hours telephone support for our member practices Monday to Friday, 08:0018:30.

The overnight GP will cover the period from midnight to 08:00 alongside another GP. The two clinicians will be based in different parts of the county at Wycombe Hospital and Stoke Mandeville Hospital and will work jointly within the central advice pool to triage patients. Any base appointments or home visits required will be undertaken by the clinician located at the Primary Care Centre (PCC) closest to the patients address. Overnight GPs will be working alone; however, they will have a driver with them.

GP Employed from: £61.38 per Hour (Including NHS Pensions)

GP Self Employed from £72.50 per Hour

Responsibilities/Expectations

An experienced OOHs GP, previously worked with FedBucks and Buckinghamshire is desirable.

To provide timely high quality clinical care, telephone consultations (average 1 every 15 minutes), base appointments (1 every 20 minutes) and home visits (1 an hour, dependant on location).

To monitor the central, advise pool for patients safety.

To provide appropriate care and services to patients in all age ranges and level of health care needs.

To be competent in dealing with face-to-face base consultations, home visits and triage cases over the phone.

Keep good quality up to date medical records including ensuring appropriate documentation and coding is used to provide consistent RCGP audit requirements.

To provide clinical advice and support to team members as requested.

To develop and maintain high levels of communication with patients and carers ensuring effective care delivery.

To promote effective communication processes between all team members to enable good working practices.

To maintain communication processes with acute and other colleagues and partners in care to ensure care delivery

FedBucks is a not-for-profit GP federation of 45 GP practices covering a population of over 550,000 patients across Buckinghamshire. We began in 2016 and now employ around 300 members of staff at our head office site, and across our planned and unplanned care services.

As a GP Federation and Social Enterprise, we are proud to represent our member practices and to champion primary care by working with local general practice and system partners in the provision of community-based healthcare services. We are dedicated to providing safe and compassionate care to our patients across our range of planned and unplanned healthcare services in Buckinghamshire and believe in continuous commitment to quality service delivery and positive patient outcomes.

Patients are at the heart of everything we do, and we pride ourselves in our purpose when enabling excellent patient care and supporting general practice.

FedBucks is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people, and vulnerable adults. All staff are expected to share this commitment and to uphold the organisations safeguarding policies and procedures at all times.

The successful applicant will be required to undergo an enhanced background check (e.g., DBS) prior to appointment, and regular safeguarding training will be provided and required.

employer: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant psychiatrist - Crisis Care
descriptionHtml:
This Consultant General Adult Psychiatrist post is based within the Southampton Crisis Resolution and Home Treatment Team (CRHTT), located at Antelope House, Southampton. The CRHTT provides a 24/7 service for adults experiencing acute mental health crises, offering intensive home treatment as an alternative to hospital admission and acting as the gatekeeper to inpatient mental health beds across Southampton. The Consultant will provide senior clinical leadership within a well established multidisciplinary team, supporting the assessment and management of patients with complex and severe mental health needs while maintaining a small caseload of the most complex cases. The role includes medical supervision of junior medical staff, participation in clinical governance, service development, teaching, and quality improvement activities. The post comprises 9 Programmed Activities (6.5 DCC, 2.5 SPA) and includes participation in the Southampton consultant on-call rota. The Trust offers excellent opportunities for CPD, mentorship, leadership development, and collaborative working within a newly integrated healthcare organisation committed to its CARE values.

The post holder will work within the Southampton Crisis Resolution and Home Treatment Team, providing consultant leadership and specialist psychiatric input to a multidisciplinary team delivering urgent assessment and home based treatment for adults experiencing mental health crises. The team works closely with inpatient services at Antelope House, ensuring appropriate admission avoidance, gatekeeping of acute beds, and timely discharge planning.

The Consultant will undertake scheduled and urgent clinical reviews, contribute to multidisciplinary decision making, and provide expert guidance on the management of patients with complex presentations and significant levels of risk. The role includes supporting a caseload of patients requiring the highest level of clinical expertise, as well as providing leadership, advice, and supervision to the wider team.

The post holder will supervise junior medical staff, including a Specialty Doctor and Resident Doctors, and contribute to teaching, training, and educational supervision. They will participate in clinical governance, service improvement, and quality assurance activities, while supporting the continued development of the Acute and Crisis Care Pathway. The role involves working closely with community mental health teams, inpatient wards, Early Intervention in Psychosis services, perinatal services, liaison psychiatry, and local addiction services to ensure seamless patient care across organisational boundaries.

Hampshire and Isle of Wight Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust is a newly established organisation, bringing together expertise from across mental health, learning disabilities, community, and physical health services. We are dedicated to delivering compassionate, high-quality, and accessible care to the diverse communities of Hampshire and the Isle of Wight.

With over 13,000 dedicated staff working across more than 300 sites, we place patients and staff at the centre of everything we do. Our goal is to create an integrated healthcare system that improves accessibility and ensures more consistent care for patients. By working together, we aim to improve patient outcomes, drive innovation, and meet the unique needs of the populations we serve.

Our Trust unites services from Southern Health, Solent NHS Trust, Isle of Wight NHS Trusts community and mental health teams, as well as Hampshire CAMHS, originally part of Sussex Partnership NHS Foundation Trust. This transformation enables us to deliver more seamless care across the region, ensuring that patients receive the right support, in the right place, at the right time.

Join us as we embark on this exciting journey to shape the future of healthcare across Hampshire and the Isle of Wight. We are deeply committed to our CARE values of compassion, accountability, respect, and excellence, and offer outstanding opportunities for career development, training, and collaborative working.

employer: Honeybeerecruitment.com Ltd. trading as Military Medical Personnel (MMP)
title: Consultant in Occupational Medicine
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a Locum Doctor (Consultant in Occupational Medicine) to cover an assignment with the Ministry of Defence (MoD), at Catterick Occupational Health, in Catterick, North Yorkshire.

This is a locum role (40 hours per week) and the successful candidate will deliver an exceptional standard of care to the MoD service personnel.

Hourly Rate - £84.82 per hour

Job Description:

  • To provide Defence Primary Healthcare (DPHC) medical staff and the Chain of Command (CoC) with specialist Occupational Health (OH) advice concerning medical aspects of a Service Persons (SP) employability, deployability and ongoing employment.
  • To undertake fitness for work assessments and Medical Boards on SP as determined by Single Service (SS) and Joint Medical Employment Policy, fulfilling the role of President or Board Member as required and as laid down in MOD and single Service and Joint Medical Employment Policy.
  • To complete reports and documentation in accordance with MOD policy or the requirements of any other government department.
  • To provide occupational health advice and guidance to SP regarding their employment when appearing before fitness for work assessments and Medical Boards.

About Military Medical Personnel and Our Benefits:

Military Medical Personnel (MMP) is a specialist recruitment consultancy dedicated exclusively to providing locum civilian medical, dental and healthcare professionals to the Ministry of Defence. We are a contracted supplier to the MOD and have locum vacancies on military bases throughout the UK and occasionally overseas locations.

Military Medical Personnel offer an attractive package for candidates which may include the following:

  • Attractive rates of pay with weekly payments and choice of payment model
  • A generous Refer a Friend bonus scheme
  • Flexibility of long- and short-term assignments to suit your availability
  • Free uniforms provided (if required)
  • A PVG membership (Disclosure Scotland) or an Access Northern Ireland certificate is required for this role.
  • Free mandatory training
  • Weekly payments
  • Assigned an experienced consultant who will support you throughout your application and will continue to look after you during your assignment

All job placements are subject to the receipt of satisfactory compliance requirements.

Please note that MMP is unable to sponsor work visas. Applicants must already have the right to work in the UK, such as a valid visa with no restrictions on hours.

title: Consultant Psychiatrist
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking an experienced full-time Consultant who will work at Cygnet Joyce Parker Hospital and provide senior medical cover on our 12-bed PICU inpatient service for men.

Blythe Ward is a 12 bed male PICU which accepts emergency and crisis admissions. Referrals come to us from all areas, including acute and prison services.

Our aim is a short, rapid intervention to help individuals regain a sense of control and order in their lives, so they can move to a less restrictive care setting and ultimately return home.

The post holder will be the Responsible Clinician and will oversee and maintain the care of all ward inpatients as required and will also have responsibility for auditing the medical services rendered at the ward and ensuring their good quality in accordance to GMC standards of good medical practice and other relevant professional guidelines.

In this role, your expertise will be the driving force for life-changing treatment fully supported by a Specialty Doctor and first-class multidisciplinary team including qualified nurses, psychologist and occupational therapist.

Cygnet Joyce Parker Hospital is our emergency mental health hospital in Coventry. The service supports adults across three wards to move as quickly and safely as possible to the most appropriate and least restrictive environment for them.

The ethos of the service is about assessing and treating individuals in the least restrictive environment and planning for discharge in a robust and timely fashion.

With a focus on stabilisation, we support individuals to manage their mental health, reinforce daily living skills and prepare for independent life back in the community.

The post holder will be the Responsible Clinician on our Male Acute ward and have overall medical responsibility of patient treatment plans, whilst liaising closely with the Multi-Disciplinary Team (Psychologists, Occupational Therapists, Registered Mental Health Nurses, Social Workers etc.)

The post holder will be expected to act as a positive role model, maintaining and demonstrating a positive attitude towards patients, their families, visitors and other staff.

Cygnet have been providing a national network of high-quality specialist mental health services for more than 30 years. We have built a reputation for delivering pioneering services and outstanding outcomes. Our expert care enables thousands of individuals to consistently make a positive difference to their lives.

We maintain a good relationship with our quality regulators and undergo regular inspections, with 85% of our services rated Good or Outstanding. We also operate an internal system of quality care, treatment and positive outcomes.

title: Senior Care Assistant

As the Kind Care Company, it is our mission to provide the kindest support and care to Residents living in our care homes, as we strive to be the first-choice care provider for Families, our Colleagues and Commissioners in each of the communities that we serve.

title: Practicing Privileges ENT Doctor
descriptionHtml:

Our ENT services are among the busiest and most highly regarded, offering patients timely access to high-quality care in their local communities. We are now seeking a GP with a Special Interest (GPSI) in ENT to join our expert team across Manchester.The Role: As an ENT GPSI, you will provide clinical assessment and treatment for patients with ENT conditions such as impacted wax, epistaxis, sinusitis, recurrent tonsillitis, and more. New opportunities open as we grow - whether that's progressing, moving sideways or taking on something different as your strengths evolve. And everything we do is focussed on making healthcare better - for patients, partners and the people delivering care.

title: Urgent Primary Care Doctor (GP) - Bank
descriptionHtml: Urgent Primary Care Doctor  Bank (Home Visiting) Bring urgent primary care to the patients who need it most - in their own homes. Urgent care is General Practice at its most immediate. Patients don't always know what they need when they reach us. They may have been referred through NHS 111 and, following clinical assessment, need to be seen in their own home. What they need is an experienced doctor who can listen, assess, make confident clinical decisions and get them to the right care. At IC24, we're looking for Urgent Primary Care Doctors to work within our Home Visiting Service across Sussex, providing urgent face-to-face care to patients in their own homes. You will have access to IC24s fleet of vehicles and any equipment required to carry out this role, we only need you to bring your clinical expertise. You'll work alongside our drivers, dispatch teams and wider urgent care colleagues, providing safe, timely and effective care while helping patients access the most appropriate treatment for their needs. If you enjoy the variety of General Practice, the autonomy of home visiting and the clinical challenge of assessing and treating patients in their own environment, this could be the role for you.At IC24, we're searching for Urgent Primary Care Doctors to work within our Home Visiting Service across Sussex, offering urgent face-to-face care to patients in their own homes. This role goes beyond practical support, addressing immediate healthcare needs for patients who might be housebound, nearing the end of life, or undergoing urgent clinical issues. You'll coordinate closely with drivers, dispatch teams, and other care personnel to deliver timely and effective treatment. Tasks include assessing and treating patients, making confident clinical decisions, managing risks, and ensuring patients receive appropriate care. title: Consultant CAMHS ID + 20% Golden Hello
